source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 13

stem: At which layer of the OSI model do you find the protocol responsible for the delivery of data to its ultimate destination on an internetwork?
explanation: On a TCP/IP network, the Internet Protocol (IP) at the Network layer is the protocol responsible for the delivery of data to its final destination. Data link layer protocols are only concerned with communication between devices on a local area network (LAN) or between two points connected by a wide area network (WAN) link. The Session and Application layers are not involved in the actual delivery of data.
whyWrong: The Data link layer deals with MAC addresses and frames on the local network; it is not the layer that delivers data to its final destination on an internetwork.
The Session layer deals with dialogue control between end systems; it is not the layer that delivers data to its final destination on an internetwork.
The Application layer is the entry point for applications into the protocol stack; it is not the layer that delivers data to its final destination on an internetwork.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 14

stem: Which of the following is not a protocol operating at the Network layer of the OSI model?
explanation: Internet Protocol (IP), Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP), and Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP) are all Network layer protocols. Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP) is a mail protocol that operates at the Application layer.
whyWrong: IP is the main Network layer protocol for addressing and routing.
ICMP is a Network layer protocol that carries error and control messages.
IGMP is a Network layer protocol that manages multicast group membership.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 15

stem: Ed is a software developer who has been given the task of creating an application that requires guaranteed delivery of information between end systems. At which layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model does the protocol that provides the guaranteed delivery run, and what type of protocol must Ed use?
explanation: A connection-oriented Transport layer protocol, such as Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), provides guaranteed delivery of data for upper layer applications. Connectionless protocols do not guarantee delivery of information and therefore are not a good choice. Guaranteed delivery of information between end systems is generally not a function of the Data link, Network, or Application layer.
whyWrong: Data link layer protocols work only on the local link and do not guarantee end-to-end delivery.
The Network layer routes data, but its main protocol, IP, is connectionless and does not guarantee delivery.
A connectionless protocol cannot guarantee delivery, and delivery guarantees belong to the Transport layer.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 16

stem: Alice is a network administrator designing a new local area network (LAN). She needs to determine the type of cabling and the network topology to implement. Which layers of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model apply to cabling and topology elements?
explanation: The Physical layer defines the mechanical and electrical characteristics of the cables used to build a network. The Data link layer defines specific network (LAN or WAN) topologies and their characteristics. The Physical layer standard that Alice will implement depends on the Data link layer protocol she selects. The Network, Transport, and Application layers are not concerned with cables and topologies.
whyWrong: The Network layer handles logical addressing and routing, not cabling.
The Network and Transport layers handle routing and end-to-end delivery, not cables or topology.
The Transport and Application layers deal with delivery and applications, not cables or topology.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 17

stem: Which layers of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model do not have protocols in the TCP/IP suite exclusively dedicated to them? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: In the TCP/IP suite, the functions of the Session layer are primarily implemented in the Transport layer protocols: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and User Datagram Protocol (UDP). The Presentation layer functions are often implemented in Application layer protocols, although some functions, such as encryption, can also be performed by Transport or Network layer protocols.
whyWrong: The Physical layer has its own dedicated standards, such as cabling and signaling specifications.
The Data link layer has its own dedicated protocols, such as Ethernet and ARP.
The Network layer has dedicated TCP/IP protocols, such as IP and ICMP.
The Transport layer has dedicated TCP/IP protocols, TCP and UDP.
The Application layer has many dedicated TCP/IP protocols, such as HTTP, DNS, and SMTP.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 18

stem: The protocols at which layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model use port numbers to identify the applications that are the source and the destination of the data in the packets?
explanation: Transport layer protocols, such as Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and User Datagram Protocol (UDP), have header fields that contain the port numbers of the applications that generated the data in the packet, and which will receive it. The Application, Presentation, and Network layers do not use port numbers.
whyWrong: The Application layer is the entry point for applications into the protocol stack; it is not the layer that uses port numbers to identify source and destination applications.
The Presentation layer deals with translation, formatting, compression, and encryption; it is not the layer that uses port numbers to identify source and destination applications.
The Network layer deals with logical IP addressing and routing between networks; it is not the layer that uses port numbers to identify source and destination applications.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 19

stem: Which of the following is a correct listing of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model layers, in order, from top to bottom?
options: Physical, Data link, Transport, Network, Session, Presentation, Application
Application, Session, Presentation, Transport, Network, Data link, physical
Presentation, Application, Transport, Session, Network, Physical, Data link
Session, Application, Presentation, Transport, Data link, Network, Physical
Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data link, Physical
explanation: The correct order of the OSI model layers, from top to bottom, is Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data link, Physical. The Application layer (layer 7) sits at the top, and the Physical layer (layer 1) sits at the bottom. A common memory aid from the top is "All People Seem To Need Data Processing."
whyWrong: This list starts at the bottom of the model and also swaps the Transport and Network layers.
This list swaps the Session and Presentation layers.
This list is out of order from the top, because Application is the top layer.
This list is out of order, because Application is the top layer and Physical sits below Data link.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 20

stem: At which of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model layers do switches and bridges perform their basic functions?
explanation: Switches and bridges are involved in local area network (LAN) communications only and therefore primarily at the Data link layer. They are not primarily associated with the Physical, Network, or Transport layers, although some switches include Network layer routing capabilities.
whyWrong: The Physical layer deals with the medium, connectors, and signaling; it is not the layer that switches and bridges work at.
The Network layer deals with logical IP addressing and routing between networks; it is not the layer that switches and bridges work at.
The Transport layer deals with end-to-end delivery, port numbers, and flow control; it is not the layer that switches and bridges work at.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 21

stem: On a TCP/IP network, flow control is a function implemented in protocols operating at which layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model?
explanation: Flow control is a process that adjusts the transmission rate of a protocol based on the capability of the receiver. If the receiving system becomes overwhelmed by incoming data, the sender dynamically reduces the transmission rate. In the TCP/IP protocol suite, Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) is responsible for implementing flow control. TCP runs at the Transport layer. None of the other layers listed have TCP/IP protocols that provide flow control.
whyWrong: The Presentation layer deals with translation, formatting, compression, and encryption; it is not the layer that implements flow control in TCP/IP.
The Session layer deals with dialogue control between end systems; it is not the layer that implements flow control in TCP/IP.
The Network layer deals with logical IP addressing and routing between networks; it is not the layer that implements flow control in TCP/IP.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 22

stem: Which layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model defines the medium, network interfaces, connecting hardware, and signaling methods used on a network?
explanation: The Physical layer of the OSI model defines the standards for the physical and mechanical characteristics of a network, such as cabling (copper and fiber), connecting hardware (hubs and switches), and signaling methods (analog and digital). None of the other layers are involved in the mechanical characteristics of the network.
whyWrong: The Data link layer deals with MAC addresses and frames on the local network; it is not the layer that defines the medium, interfaces, connecting hardware, and signaling.
The Network layer deals with logical IP addressing and routing between networks; it is not the layer that defines the medium, interfaces, connecting hardware, and signaling.
The Transport layer deals with end-to-end delivery, port numbers, and flow control; it is not the layer that defines the medium, interfaces, connecting hardware, and signaling.
The Session layer deals with dialogue control between end systems; it is not the layer that defines the medium, interfaces, connecting hardware, and signaling.
The Presentation layer deals with translation, formatting, compression, and encryption; it is not the layer that defines the medium, interfaces, connecting hardware, and signaling.
The Application layer is the entry point for applications into the protocol stack; it is not the layer that defines the medium, interfaces, connecting hardware, and signaling.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 23

stem: Which of the OSI model layers is responsible for syntax translation and compression or encryption?
explanation: The Presentation layer provides a syntax translation service that enables two computers to communicate, despite their use of different bit-encoding methods. This translation service also enables systems using compressed or encrypted data to communicate with each other.
whyWrong: The Data link layer deals with MAC addresses and frames on the local network; it is not the layer that handles syntax translation, compression, and encryption.
The Network layer deals with logical IP addressing and routing between networks; it is not the layer that handles syntax translation, compression, and encryption.
The Session layer deals with dialogue control between end systems; it is not the layer that handles syntax translation, compression, and encryption.
The Application layer is the entry point for applications into the protocol stack; it is not the layer that handles syntax translation, compression, and encryption.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 24

stem: Which layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model is responsible for transmitting signals over the network medium?
explanation: The Physical layer of the OSI model defines the functions specific to the network medium and the transmission and reception of signals. All of the other layers are software components that do not physically send or receive signals.
whyWrong: The Data link layer deals with MAC addresses and frames on the local network; it is not the layer that transmits signals over the network medium.
The Network layer deals with logical IP addressing and routing between networks; it is not the layer that transmits signals over the network medium.
The Transport layer deals with end-to-end delivery, port numbers, and flow control; it is not the layer that transmits signals over the network medium.
The Session layer deals with dialogue control between end systems; it is not the layer that transmits signals over the network medium.
The Presentation layer deals with translation, formatting, compression, and encryption; it is not the layer that transmits signals over the network medium.
The Application layer is the entry point for applications into the protocol stack; it is not the layer that transmits signals over the network medium.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 25

stem: Specify the layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model at which the Internet Protocol (IP) operates and whether it is connection-oriented or connectionless.
explanation: IP is a connectionless protocol that operates at the Network layer of the OSI model. There are no connection-oriented protocols at this layer. The protocols at the Transport layer include Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), which is connection-oriented, and User Datagram Protocol (UDP), which is connectionless.
whyWrong: IP works at the Network layer, but it is connectionless, not connection-oriented.
IP is not a Transport layer protocol, and the connection-oriented protocol there is TCP.
IP is not a Transport layer protocol, and the connectionless protocol there is UDP.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 26

stem: An Ethernet network interface adapter provides functions that span which two layers of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model?
explanation: An Ethernet network interface adapter functions at the Data link layer by encapsulating Network layer data for transmission over the network. It provides Physical layer functions by providing the connection to the network medium and generating the appropriate signals for transmission. Network interface adapters do not operate at the Network, Transport, or Application layers.
whyWrong: A network adapter does not route by IP address, which is the work of the Network layer.
Network and Transport layer functions run in the operating system's protocol stack, not in the adapter.
Transport and Application layer functions run in software, not in the network adapter.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 27

stem: Which of the following protocols operate at the Application layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) and Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) operate at the Application layer. Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) and Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP) both operate at the Network layer. User Datagram Protocol (UDP) operates at the Transport layer.
whyWrong: ICMP is a Network layer protocol for error and control messages.
IGMP is a Network layer protocol for multicast group membership.
UDP is a connectionless Transport layer protocol.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 28

stem: Which layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model would be responsible for converting a text file encoded using EBCDIC on the sending system into ASCII code, when required by the receiving system?
explanation: The Presentation layer of the OSI model is responsible for translating different kinds of syntax, including text-encoding systems, such as EBCDIC and ASCII. The Application, Session, and Physical layers do not perform this function.
whyWrong: The Application layer is the entry point for applications into the protocol stack; it is not the layer that converts EBCDIC text into ASCII.
The Session layer deals with dialogue control between end systems; it is not the layer that converts EBCDIC text into ASCII.
The Physical layer deals with the medium, connectors, and signaling; it is not the layer that converts EBCDIC text into ASCII.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 29

stem: Which of the following protocols operates at the Network layer of the OSI model but does not encapsulate data generated by an upper layer protocol for transmission over the network?
explanation: Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) operates at the Network layer by sending operational and error messages. It does not encapsulate upper layer protocol data. Internet Protocol (IP) operates at the Network layer, but it does encapsulate Transport layer protocol data. Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and User Datagram Protocol (UDP) are Transport layer protocols that encapsulate upper layer protocol data. Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) does not encapsulate upper layer protocol data, but it is a Data link layer protocol.
whyWrong: IP works at the Network layer, but it does encapsulate Transport layer data.
UDP is a Transport layer protocol that encapsulates application data.
ARP resolves IP addresses to MAC addresses and is treated as a Data link layer protocol.
TCP is a Transport layer protocol that encapsulates application data.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 30

stem: Which of the following devices run exclusively at the Physical layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: A repeater is a Physical layer device that amplifies the signals entering it and transmits them again. A hub is a Physical layer device that propagates incoming signals out through all of its ports. Switches and routers have Physical layer elements but are primarily Data link and Network layer devices, respectively.
whyWrong: Routers are mainly Network layer devices that forward packets by IP address.
Switches are mainly Data link layer devices that forward frames by MAC address.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 31

stem: Which of the following devices enables two computers to communicate when they are using different protocols at each layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) reference model?
explanation: A gateway enables two devices using different protocols to communicate by performing translation and conversion services for them. Routers, hubs, and switches all require the same protocol at some of the OSI model layers.
whyWrong: A router needs the same Network layer protocol on both sides and does not translate between protocol stacks.
A hub only repeats signals at the Physical layer.
A switch forwards frames by MAC address and needs the same Data link protocol on its ports.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 32
note: N10-009 does not name gateways under 1.1; the question tests which OSI layers a device works at, so 1.1 was kept.

stem: Which of the following BEST describes the function of a firewall?
options: A device located between two networks that enables administrators to restrict incoming and outgoing traffic
A device that connects two networks together, forwarding traffic between them as needed
A device that enables Internet network clients with private IP addresses to access the Internet
A device that caches Internet data for subsequent use by internal network clients
explanation: A firewall is a filter that can prevent dangerous traffic originating on one network from passing through to another network. A device that connects two networks together and forwards traffic between them is a router, not a firewall. A device that enables Internet network clients with private IP addresses to access the Internet is a description of a network address translation (NAT) router or a proxy server, not a firewall. A device that caches Internet data is a proxy server or caching engine, not a firewall.
whyWrong: A device that connects networks and forwards traffic between them is a router.
A device that lets private-address clients reach the internet is a NAT router or a proxy server.
A device that caches internet data for clients is a proxy server or caching engine.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 33

stem: Which of the following terms is used to describe the method by which a firewall examines the port numbers in Transport layer protocol headers?
explanation: Service-dependent filtering blocks traffic based on the port numbers specified in the Transport layer header fields. Because port numbers represent specific applications, you can use them to prevent traffic generated by these applications from reaching a network. IP address filtering operates at the Network layer. DPI scans the contents of packets, rather than their headers. NGFW defines a device with advanced protection capabilities; port number scanning is a basic firewall function.
whyWrong: IP address filtering checks source or destination addresses at the Network layer, not port numbers.
Deep packet inspection examines the data inside packets rather than the port numbers in headers.
A next-generation firewall is a class of device with advanced features, not the name of port-based filtering.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 34

stem: Which of the following physical network devices can conceivably be implemented as software in a computer's operating system? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Most operating systems are capable of functioning as routers or firewalls. To route traffic, the system must have two network connections. A software firewall can be part of a computer's routing functionality, or it can be a stand-alone firewall that protects only the local system. Computers cannot function as hubs or switches because multiple ports would be required, and standard network adapters do not implement those functions.
whyWrong: A hub needs many ports and cannot be built in a computer's operating system.
A switch needs many switched ports and is not implemented in a standard computer's operating system.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 35

stem: Which of the following criteria does a firewall capable of service-dependent filtering use to block traffic?
explanation: Service-dependent filtering blocks traffic based on the port numbers specified in the Transport layer header fields. Because port numbers represent specific applications, you can use them to prevent traffic generated by these applications from reaching a network. IP address filtering enables you to limit network access to specific computers; it is not service dependent. Filtering based on hardware addresses provides the same basic functionality as IP address filtering, but it is more difficult to spoof hardware addresses than IP addresses. Filtering by protocol identifier enables you to block all traffic using TCP or UDP; it is not service dependent.
whyWrong: Filtering by hardware addresses controls which systems can connect, not which services they use.
Filtering by protocol identifier blocks whole protocols such as TCP or UDP, not specific services.
Filtering by IP address limits which computers can communicate, not which services they use.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 36

stem: Ralph is a freelance network consultant installing a three-node small business network. The computers are all in the same room and use wired Ethernet to connect to the switched ports of a multifunction device. The device also functions as a network address translation (NAT) router for a cable modem connection to the Internet. NAT provides a measure of security, but Ralph wants to be sure that the network is protected from unauthorized Internet traffic and attacks against open ports. Which of the following solutions would enable Ralph to accomplish this goal with the minimum cost to the client?
options: Install a hardware firewall between the multifunction device and the cable modem.
Install an intrusion prevention system (IPS) between the multifunction device and the cable modem.
Install a personal firewall on each of the computers.
Connect an intrusion detection system (IDS) to one of the switched ports in the multifunction device.
Use a port scanner to monitor the traffic entering the open ports on the computers.
explanation: A personal firewall is an inexpensive way to protect an individual computer from Internet incursions. Installing a hardware firewall is a complex and expensive solution, not suitable for a small network. An IPS is a relatively expensive solution, suitable for larger networks. An IDS is also expensive, and connecting it to a switched port would not enable it to protect the other computers on the network. A port scanner is a device that performs scans on demand. It does not continuously monitor ports, and it does nothing to protect them.
whyWrong: A hardware firewall costs more and is harder to set up than this small network needs.
An IPS is an expensive solution meant for larger networks.
An IDS on a switched port is expensive and would not see or protect the other computers' traffic.
A port scanner checks ports on demand and does not protect them.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 37

stem: Which of the following statements about hubs and switches are true? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Hubs operate only at the Physical layer, whereas switches operate only at the Network layer.
All of the devices connected to a hub are part of a single collision domain, whereas each device connected to a switch has its own collision domain.
There are switches available with Network layer functionality, but there are no hubs with that capability.
Switches create a separate broadcast domain for each connected device, whereas hubs create a single broadcast domain for all of the connected devices.
explanation: Hubs operate at the Physical layer, and switches operate at the Data link layer. Hubs and switches both create a single broadcast domain for all of the connected devices. Switches create a separate collision domain for each connected device, whereas hubs create a single collision domain. There are switches (but not hubs) with Network layer (layer 3) functionality.
whyWrong: Switches operate at the Data link layer, not only at the Network layer.
Both hubs and switches forward broadcasts, so all their connected devices share one broadcast domain.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 38

stem: Which of the following devices perform essentially the same function? (Choose two.)
explanation: A switch is essentially a multiport bridge. Both switches and bridges process incoming packets by scanning their Data link layer hardware addresses and forwarding the packets out the port connected to the destination system. The primary difference between them is that switches have many ports, whereas bridges have only two. Hubs and routers are Physical layer and Network layer devices, respectively, and perform different functions.
whyWrong: Hubs repeat signals at the Physical layer and do not read MAC addresses.
Routers forward packets by IP address at the Network layer, which is a different function.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 39

stem: Which of the following switch types immediately forwards frames after looking at only the destination address?
explanation: Cut-through switches are fast, because they look at only the first 6 bytes (the destination media access control, or MAC, address) when forwarding a frame. They do not perform a cyclical redundancy check (CRC) on the entire frame's contents prior to forwarding it out a port leading to the destination. Source route is a bridging technique in which the source host, not the switch, determines the path a frame will take through a network to reach a destination. Store-and-forward switches take in the entire frame and verify its contents by performing a CRC calculation before forwarding it. There is no switch called a destination switch.
whyWrong: Source route is a bridging method in which the sending host chooses the path, not a switch type.
A store-and-forward switch receives the whole frame and checks its CRC before forwarding.
There is no switch type called a destination switch.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 40

stem: Which of the following is something that only a firewall capable of stateful packet inspection can do?
options: Block traffic destined for specific IP addresses
Scan Transport layer header fields for evidence of SYN floods
Block all TCP traffic from entering a network
explanation: A firewall that supports stateful packet inspection examines other network and Transport layer header fields, looking for patterns that indicate damaging behaviors, such as IP spoofing, SYN floods, and teardrop attacks. Port number filtering is the most commonly used form of packet filtering; it is not the same as stateful packet inspection. Blocking traffic based on IP addresses prevents specific systems from accessing a network; stateful packet inspection is a much more complicated operation. Packet filtering based on protocol identifiers enables you to block TCP traffic; this is not stateful packet inspection.
whyWrong: Filtering by port number is basic packet filtering that any firewall can do.
Blocking traffic to specific IP addresses is basic packet filtering, not stateful inspection.
Blocking all TCP traffic is protocol filtering, which a basic packet filter can do.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 41

stem: Which of the following are methods typically used by intrusion detection systems (IDSs) to analyze incoming network traffic? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: IDSs can use anomaly-based detection to identify deviations from a known baseline of trustworthiness, or signature-based detection to locate specific malicious byte or instruction sequences. Behavior-based and statistic-based detection are not typical IDS methods.
whyWrong: The book does not list behavior-based detection as a typical IDS method.
Statistic-based detection is not a typical IDS analysis method.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 42
note: Behavior-based detection is often treated as another name for anomaly-based detection; the book's answer is kept.

stem: Which of the following is another term for a multiport bridge?
explanation: A traditional switch is a Data link layer device that essentially performs the function of a bridge for each device connected to one of its ports. It can therefore be described as a multiport bridge. Some switches include layer 3 functionality, but they still function as bridges. Routers, hubs, and gateways are devices that operate at the Network, Physical, and Application layers, respectively, so they cannot be described as bridges.
whyWrong: A router connects networks at the Network layer and is not a multiport bridge.
A hub repeats signals at the Physical layer and does not bridge frames by MAC address.
A gateway translates between different protocols and is not a multiport bridge.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 43

stem: Which of the following statements about switches and routers are true? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Routers operate at the Network layer, whereas switches operate at the Data link layer.
All of the devices connected to a switch are part of a single broadcast domain, whereas the networks connected to a router form separate broadcast domains.
Routers can communicate with each other and share information, but switches cannot.
Switches forward packets based on their hardware addresses, whereas routers forward packets based on their IP addresses.
explanation: Routers are Network layer devices that do not forward broadcast messages, so they create separate broadcast domains for each network. Switches do forward broadcasts, forming a single broadcast domain. Routers and switches can communicate using dedicated protocols. As Data link layer devices, switches read only hardware addresses from packet frames; routers forward traffic based on the IP addresses in packets' IP headers.
whyWrong: Switches can also exchange information with each other through protocols such as Spanning Tree Protocol.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 44

stem: Which of the following explains why splitting a large, switched Ethernet LAN into two LANs by adding a router can help to alleviate traffic congestion and improve performance? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Adding a router reduces the amount of broadcast traffic on each of the two LANs.
Adding a router reduces the amount of unicast traffic on each of the two LANs.
Adding a router diverts traffic to an alternate path through the network.
Adding a router prevents computers on one LAN from communicating with computers on another LAN.
explanation: Adding a router splits the Ethernet LAN into two LANs, creating two separate broadcast domains. Each computer, therefore, has a smaller number of broadcast messages to process. Because the network is split by the router, the amount of unicast traffic on each subnet is reduced.
whyWrong: A router splits the LAN into two networks; it does not create an alternate path for the traffic.
Computers on the two LANs can still communicate, because the router forwards traffic between them.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 46
note: The claim that a router reduces unicast traffic on each LAN depends on traffic patterns; the book's answer is kept.

stem: Which of the following statements about traditional bridges and switches is true?
options: Bridges and switches are Network layer devices that use logical addressing to forward frames.
Bridges and switches are Data link layer devices that use media access control (MAC) addresses to forward frames.
Bridges and switches build their internal tables based on destination addresses and forward packets based on source addresses.
Bridges and switches must support the Network layer protocol implemented on the local area network (LAN).
Each port on a bridge or switch defines a separate broadcast domain.
explanation: Traditional bridges and switches are Data link layer devices that forward frames based on the destination MAC address contained in the frame. They operate in promiscuous mode, listening and processing all frames on each segment, and they build forwarding tables with this information. Forwarding tables are built based on source MAC addresses. Some switches include layer 3 functionality, but their primary function is still based at the Data link layer. Bridges are protocol independent; they are not involved with the upper layer protocols being carried on the LAN. Broadcast domains are defined by Network layer devices, not Data link layer devices.
whyWrong: Bridges and switches are Data link layer devices that use MAC addresses, not logical addresses.
Bridges and switches build their tables from source addresses and forward by destination addresses.
Bridges and switches are protocol independent and do not need to support the Network layer protocol.
Bridges and switches forward broadcasts, so all their ports share one broadcast domain.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 47

stem: Which of the following is a correct term describing the function of a traditional switch?
explanation: A traditional switch is best described as a multiport bridge because it reads the hardware addresses of incoming packets and forwards them out through the port for the destination node. Although a traditional switch does function at layer 2 of the OSI model (the Data link layer), there are also switches with Network layer capabilities that can function as a router, which connects networks together at layer 3. Hubs and repeaters are Physical layer (layer 1) devices that are not capable of performing the functions of a switch.
whyWrong: A layer 2 device does not route, and routing is a layer 3 function.
A hub repeats signals out all ports and does not forward frames by MAC address.
A repeater is a layer 1 device, and there is no layer 3 repeater.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 48

stem: Which of the following is the primary reason why replacing hubs with layer 2 switches on an Ethernet local area network (LAN) improves its performance?
options: Layer 2 switches forward packets faster than hubs.
Layer 2 switches do not forward broadcast transmissions.
Layer 2 switches reduce the number of collisions on the network.
Layer 2 switches read the IP addresses of packets, not the hardware addresses.
explanation: The main reason why traditional layer 2 switches improve the efficiency of an Ethernet LAN is that they create a separate collision domain for each switched port, eliminating most collisions. Collisions result in packets having to be retransmitted, so fewer collisions mean fewer retransmissions, which improves performance. Layer 2 switches do not forward packets faster than hubs, but they do forward broadcast transmissions. Layer 2 switches do read hardware addresses, not IP addresses, but there are switches with layer 3 capabilities that route data packets to their destinations using IP addresses and subnetting.
whyWrong: Layer 2 switches do not forward packets faster than hubs; they forward them more selectively.
Layer 2 switches do forward broadcast transmissions out all ports.
Layer 2 switches read MAC addresses, not IP addresses.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 49

stem: Which of the following statements about routers are true? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Routers are Network layer devices that use IP addresses to forward frames.
Routers are Data link layer devices that use media access control (MAC) addresses to forward frames.
Routers build their internal tables based on destination MAC addresses and forward frames based on source MAC addresses.
Routers must support the Network layer protocol implemented on the local area network (LAN).
Each port on a router defines a separate broadcast domain.
explanation: Routers are Network layer devices that use IP addresses to forward frames, not MAC addresses. Routers are protocol dependent. They must support the Network layer protocol being routed. As a Network layer device, a router defines networks (or LANs) that represent a separate broadcast domain. Routers do not build their routing tables or forward frames using MAC addresses.
whyWrong: Routers are Network layer devices that forward by IP address, not by MAC address.
Routers build routing tables from network addresses, not from MAC addresses.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 50

stem: Which of the following statements about routers is not true?
options: Routers can connect two or more networks with dissimilar Data link layer protocols and media.
Routers can connect two or more networks with the same Data link layer protocols and media.
Routers store and maintain route information in a local text file.
Servers with multiple network interfaces can be configured to function as software routers.
Routers can learn and populate their routing tables through static and dynamic routing.
explanation: Routers store and maintain route information in a routing table that is stored in memory, not in a local text file. All of the other statements about routers are true.
whyWrong: This statement is true, because routers can join networks with different Data link protocols and media.
This statement is true, because routers can join networks that use the same Data link protocols and media.
This statement is true, because a server with several network interfaces can act as a software router.
This statement is true, because routers fill their tables with static and dynamic routes.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 51

stem: The network administrator for a small business is installing a computer to function as a firewall protecting their internetwork from Internet intrusion. At which of the following locations should the administrator install the firewall system?
options: Anywhere on the private internetwork, as long as the Internet is accessible
Between the Internet access router and the Internet service provider's (ISP's) network
Between the Internet access router and the rest of the private internetwork
explanation: The firewall is a conduit between the private network and the ISP's network (which provides access to the Internet), through which all traffic must pass. This ensures that the firewall has the opportunity to examine every packet that passes between the private network and the Internet and filter out those that are not authorized. If the firewall were located in the midst of the private internetwork, it would be possible for Internet computers to bypass the firewall and communicate directly with the private systems. Placing the firewall on the far side of the router would put it on the ISP's network, causing it to filter all of the ISP's traffic and not just that destined for the private network. Installing the firewall at the ISP's site would have the same effect as installing it on the far side of the router at the private network site.
whyWrong: A firewall placed inside the private network could be bypassed, because traffic would not all pass through it.
A firewall on the far side of the router would sit on the ISP's network and filter the ISP's traffic.
A firewall at the ISP's site would filter the ISP's traffic rather than only the private network's.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 52

stem: Proxy servers operate at which layer of the OSI reference model?
explanation: A proxy server is an Application layer service because it receives Internet service requests from client computers, reads the Application layer protocol data in each request, and then generates its own request for the same service and transmits it to the Internet server the client specifies. Only an Application layer service can read and process the Application layer data in network packets. A proxy server cannot be a Data link layer device because it can provide Internet access to an entire internetwork, while the Data link layer is concerned with communications on a single subnet. Proxy servers cannot be Network layer devices because the Network layer handles all internetwork packets indiscriminately and is unaware of what application generated the data carried inside the packets. The Transport layer is not involved in processing application data, so proxy servers cannot be said to function at the Transport layer.
whyWrong: A proxy server reads application data, which Data link layer devices cannot do.
Network layer devices route packets without knowing which application created them.
The Transport layer does not process application data, so a proxy does not work there.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 53

stem: Which of the following is a feature that is not found in a traditional firewall product, but which might be found in a next-generation firewall (NGFW)?
explanation: DPI is a firewall technique that examines the data carried in packets and not just the protocol headers. While traditional firewalls typically do not support DPI, NGFWs often do. Stateful packet inspection, NAT, and VPN support are all features that are commonly supported by traditional firewall products.
whyWrong: Stateful packet inspection is a common feature of traditional firewalls.
Network address translation is a common feature of traditional firewalls.
VPN support is a common feature of traditional firewalls.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 54

stem: Which of the following statements about content filtering in firewalls is true?
options: Content filters examine the source IP addresses of packets to locate potential threats.
Content filters enable switches to direct packets out through the correct port.
Content filters examine the data carried within packets for potentially objectionable materials.
Content filters use frequently updated signatures to locate packets containing malware.
explanation: Content filters are a firewall feature that examine the data inside packets, rather than their origin, to locate objectionable material. They do not scan IP addresses, nor do they detect typical types of malware. Content filters are not implemented in switches.
whyWrong: Content filters examine the data inside packets, not their source IP addresses.
Content filters are a firewall feature, and switches use MAC address tables to choose ports.
Signature-based malware scanning is antivirus work, not content filtering.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 55

stem: Which of the following is not one of the criteria typically used by load balancers to direct incoming traffic to one of a group of servers?
options: Which server has the lightest load
Which server has the fastest response time
Which server is next in an even rotation
Which server has the fastest processor
explanation: In most cases, a load balancing router works by processing incoming traffic based on rules set by the administrator. The rules can distribute traffic among a group of servers using various criteria, such as each server's current load or response time, or which server is next in a given rotation. Load balancers typically do not use the hardware configuration of the servers to direct traffic since this is a factor that does not change.
whyWrong: Load balancers often send traffic to the server with the lightest load.
Load balancers often send traffic to the server with the fastest response time.
Round-robin rotation is a common load balancing method.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 56

stem: Which of the following devices enables administrators of enterprise wireless networks to manage multiple access points (APs) from a central location?
explanation: In many enterprise wireless networks, the access points (APs) do not run a full operating system and are called thin or lightweight APs. The network also has a device called a wireless controller that performs some of the required tasks and manages the APs. A wireless endpoint is another term for a computer or other device that is a client on the wireless network. Hypervisors and demarcation points have nothing to do with wireless networking. A hypervisor creates and manages virtual machines (VMs) on a host server, and a demarcation point is the interface between a private network and an outside telecommunications service.
whyWrong: A hypervisor creates and manages virtual machines on a host server.
A wireless endpoint is a client device on the wireless network.
A demarcation point is where a private network meets an outside telecommunications service.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 57

stem: A load balancer is a type of which of the following devices?
explanation: A load balancer is a type of router that forwards traffic with a single IP address to multiple servers in turn. In most cases, a load balancing router works by processing incoming traffic based on rules set by the administrator. Because a load balancer works with IP addresses, it is a Network layer device. Load balancers are not switches, gateways, or firewalls.
whyWrong: A load balancer forwards traffic by IP address, which a layer 2 switch does not do.
A gateway translates between different protocols, which is not what a load balancer does.
A firewall filters traffic, while a load balancer spreads traffic among servers.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 58

stem: Which of the following devices expands on the capabilities of the traditional firewall by adding features like deep packet inspection (DPI) and an intrusion prevention system (IPS)?
explanation: Next-generation firewalls (NGFWs) expand on the packet filtering capabilities of traditional firewalls by adding features such as DPI and IPSs, as well as inspection of encrypted traffic and antivirus scanning. Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service (RADIUS) servers can provide centralized authentication, authorization, accounting, and auditing (AAAA) services. A CSU/DSU is a device that provides a router on a private network with access to a leased line. A proxy server is an Application layer service that receives Internet service requests from client computers, reads the Application layer protocol data in each request, and then generates its own request for the same service and transmits it to the Internet server the client specifies.
whyWrong: A RADIUS server provides centralized authentication, authorization, and accounting.
A CSU/DSU connects a router to a leased digital line.
A proxy server makes internet requests on behalf of clients at the Application layer.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 59

stem: Which of the following statements about Internet access through a proxy server accounts for the security against outside intrusion that a proxy provides?
options: The proxy server uses a public IP address, and the client computers use private addresses.
The proxy server uses a private IP address, and the client computers use public addresses.
Both the proxy server and the client computers use private IP addresses.
Both the proxy server and the client computers use public IP addresses.
explanation: Because the client computers use private IP addresses, they are invisible to the Internet, so users outside the private network cannot see or access them. The proxy server has a public IP address so that it can participate in service transactions with Internet servers. If the proxy server used a private IP address, it would not be able to access the Internet directly. If the clients used public IP addresses, they would be visible to the Internet and vulnerable to intrusion.
whyWrong: A proxy server with a private address could not reach the internet directly.
A proxy server with a private address could not take part in transactions with internet servers.
Client computers with public addresses would be visible to the internet and open to intrusion.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 60

stem: Which of the following devices can an administrator use to monitor a network for abnormal or malicious traffic?
explanation: Intrusion detection systems (IDSs) are designed to monitor network traffic for anomalies and send notifications to administrators. Uninterruptible power supplies (UPSs), Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service (RADIUS) servers, denial-of-service (DoS) attacks, and Remote Access Service (RAS) servers all have nothing to do with network monitoring.
whyWrong: A UPS supplies battery power during an outage and does not monitor traffic.
A RADIUS server provides centralized authentication and does not monitor traffic.
A denial-of-service attack floods a target with traffic and is not a monitoring device.
A remote access server lets remote users connect to a network and does not monitor traffic.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 61

stem: Which of the following storage area network (SAN) protocols are capable of sharing a network medium with standard local area network (LAN) traffic? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: iSCSI runs on a standard IP network, and Fibre Channel over Ethernet (FCoE) runs on a standard Ethernet network. Both of these protocols can share a network with LAN traffic, although the use of a quality of service (QoS) mechanism is usually recommended. Fibre Channel and InfiniBand both require a dedicated network medium that does not support LAN traffic.
whyWrong: Fibre Channel needs its own dedicated network and cannot share the LAN medium.
InfiniBand needs its own dedicated network and cannot share the LAN medium.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 63

stem: Which of the following protocols is not used for storage area networks (SANs)?
explanation: Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) is a technology for the transmission of voice communications over IP networks; it is not a SAN protocol. Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI), Fibre Channel over Ethernet (FCoE), and Fibre Channel are all SAN protocols.
whyWrong: iSCSI is a SAN protocol that carries SCSI commands over IP networks.
FCoE is a SAN protocol that carries Fibre Channel frames over Ethernet.
Fibre Channel is a SAN protocol that uses its own dedicated network.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 64

stem: Which of the following storage area network (SAN) technologies do iSCSI initiators use to locate iSCSI targets on the network?
explanation: The Internet Storage Name Service (iSNS) is an application that provides iSCSI initiators with automated discovery of targets located on the network. iSNS can also function as a discovery service for Fibre Channel devices. Active Directory, Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP), and Domain Name System (DNS) are not capable of registering iSCSI targets. iWINS does not exist.
whyWrong: Active Directory is a directory service and does not register iSCSI targets.
ICMP carries error and control messages and cannot register iSCSI targets.
DNS resolves names to IP addresses but does not register iSCSI targets.
There is no technology called iWINS.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 65

stem: What is the highest possible data transfer rate on a storage area network (SAN) using Fibre Channel?
explanation: The current Fibre Channel standard calls for a maximum data transfer rate of 128 gigabits per second (Gbps), for a nominal throughput of 12,800 megabytes per second (MBps). Fibre Channel speeds have doubled with each generation, from 1 Gbps through 8, 16, 32, and 64 Gbps. Fibre Channel needs its own dedicated network for SAN traffic.
whyWrong: 8 Gbps is an older Fibre Channel speed, not the highest.
16 Gbps is an older Fibre Channel speed, not the highest.
32 Gbps is a Fibre Channel speed, but it is not the highest.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 66

stem: In its primary functionality, a network-attached storage (NAS) device is most closely associated with which of the following devices?
explanation: A NAS device is essentially a file server that connects to a network and provides users with access to shared files. A NAS is a single computer, so it cannot be associated with failover clustering. Just a bunch of disks (JBOD) is a simple storage array that provides block-level access to data, whereas NAS devices provide file-level access. Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) is a fault tolerance technology that might be implemented in NAS devices, but it is not the device's primary function.
whyWrong: A NAS is a single device, so it is not a failover cluster.
JBOD is a simple disk array that gives block-level access, while a NAS gives file-level access.
RAID is a fault tolerance method that a NAS may use, not the device's main function.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 67

stem: Which of the following statements about the differences between network-attached storage (NAS) and storage area networks (SANs) are true? (Choose all that apply.)
options: NAS provides file-level storage access, whereas SAN provides block-level storage access.
NAS devices typically contain integrated iSCSI targets.
SAN devices have an operating system, whereas NAS devices do not.
NAS devices typically provide a filesystem, whereas SAN devices do not.
explanation: NAS devices are self-contained file servers that connect directly to a standard IP network. A NAS device provides file-level access to its storage devices and includes an operating system and a filesystem. NAS devices are typically not iSCSI targets.
whyWrong: NAS devices give file-level access and typically are not iSCSI targets.
NAS devices include an operating system, so this statement is wrong.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 68

stem: Which of the following statements specify advantages of FCoE over the original Fibre Channel standard? (Choose all that apply.)
options: FCoE is less expensive to implement than Fibre Channel.
FCoE can share a network with standard IP traffic, whereas Fibre Channel cannot.
FCoE is routable over IP networks, whereas Fibre Channel is not.
FCoE uses standard Ethernet networking hardware.
explanation: Because it uses standard Ethernet hardware, Fibre Channel over Ethernet (FCoE) is far less expensive to implement than Fibre Channel, which requires a dedicated fiber-optic network. Because Fibre Channel requires a dedicated network, it cannot coexist with standard IP traffic, whereas FCoE can. Because it is encapsulated in Ethernet frames, FCoE is not routable on IP networks.
whyWrong: FCoE is carried in Ethernet frames and is not routable over IP networks.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 69

stem: Which of the following are Application layer protocols that network-attached storage (NAS) devices can use to serve shared files to clients on the network? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Common Internet File System (CIFS), Network File System (NFS), and Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) are all file sharing protocols supported by many NAS devices. Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) provides high-speed network data transfers, but it is not an Application layer file sharing protocol.
whyWrong: RDMA provides high-speed data transfers, but it is not an Application layer file sharing protocol.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 70

stem: Which of the following is not one of the advantages of iSCSI over Fibre Channel?
options: iSCSI is routable, whereas Fibre Channel is not.
iSCSI is less expensive to implement than Fibre Channel.
iSCSI includes its own internal flow control mechanism, whereas Fibre Channel does not.
iSCSI can share the same network as standard local area network traffic, whereas Fibre Channel cannot.
explanation: iSCSI does not include its own flow control mechanism. It runs over a TCP connection, which is the protocol responsible for flow control. Because it runs on any IP network, iSCSI traffic is routable, and it is less expensive to implement. Fibre Channel requires a dedicated network using fiber-optic cable. iSCSI traffic can coexist with standard LAN traffic on a single network, although some type of quality of service (QoS) mechanism is frequently recommended.
whyWrong: This is an advantage of iSCSI, because it runs on routable IP networks.
This is an advantage of iSCSI, because it uses standard Ethernet hardware.
This is an advantage of iSCSI, because it can share a network with LAN traffic.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 71

stem: Which of the following is the term for the client that accesses an iSCSI device on a storage area network?
explanation: The client side of an iSCSI implementation is called an initiator. The storage device to which the initiator connects is called a target. Controller and adapter are not terms used for iSCSI clients or servers.
whyWrong: The target is the storage device that the initiator connects to.
Controller is not the iSCSI term for the client.
Adapter is not the iSCSI term for the client.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 72

stem: Which of the following protocols are included in an iSCSI packet on a storage area network (SAN)? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: iSCSI runs on a standard IP network; therefore, iSCSI messages are encapsulated using Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) at the Transport layer, Internet Protocol (IP) at the Network layer, and Ethernet at the Data link layer. iSCSI does not use the User Datagram Protocol (UDP). Ethernet frames carry the IP packets, and the iSCSI commands ride inside the TCP segments.
whyWrong: iSCSI runs over TCP, not UDP.
Several protocols are in an iSCSI packet, so None of the above is wrong.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 73

stem: Which of the following protocols are included in a Fibre Channel packet?
explanation: The Fibre Channel standard defines a unique, five-layer protocol stack that does not correspond to the OSI model layers. Therefore, Fibre Channel does not use Ethernet, nor does it use Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), Internet Protocol (IP), User Datagram Protocol (UDP), or any of the other TCP/IP protocols.
whyWrong: Fibre Channel uses its own protocol stack, not Ethernet.
Fibre Channel does not use IP.
Fibre Channel does not use TCP.
Fibre Channel does not use UDP.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 74

stem: Which of the following protocol standards defines a layered implementation that does not correspond to the layers of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model?
explanation: The Fibre Channel standard defines a five-layer networking stack, with layers numbered FC-0 to FC-4, that does not correspond to the layers of the OSI model. Internet Small Computer System Interface (iSCSI), Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP), and Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) all function within the standard OSI model layers.
whyWrong: iSCSI works within the standard OSI layers on top of TCP/IP.
PPP is a Data link layer protocol that fits the OSI model.
RDMA works within the standard OSI model layers.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 75

stem: Which of the following protocols are included in an FCoE packet?
explanation: Fibre Channel over Ethernet (FCoE) uses Ethernet frames in place of the bottom two layers (FC0 and FC1) of the Fibre Channel protocol stack. The remaining layers (FC2, FC3, and FC4) use the standard Fibre Channel protocols. FCoE does not use Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), Internet Protocol (IP), User Datagram Protocol (UDP), or any of the other TCP/IP protocols.
whyWrong: FCoE does not use IP, so it is not routable.
FCoE does not use TCP.
FCoE does not use UDP.
FCoE frames include Ethernet, so None of the above is wrong.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 76

stem: Ralph, the administrator of a 500-node private internetwork, is devising a plan to connect the network to the Internet. The primary objective of the project is to provide all of the network users with access to web and email services while keeping the client computers safe from unauthorized users on the Internet. The secondary objectives of the project are to avoid having to manually configure IP addresses on each one of the client computers individually and to provide a means of monitoring and regulating the users' access to the Internet. Ralph submits a proposal calling for the use of private IP addresses on the client computers and a series of proxy servers with public, registered IP addresses, connected to the Internet using multiple T-1 lines. Which of the following statements about Ralph's proposed Internet access solution is true?
options: The proposal fails to satisfy both the primary and secondary objectives.
The proposal satisfies the primary objective but neither of the secondary objectives.
The proposal satisfies the primary objective and one of the secondary objectives.
The proposal satisfies the primary objective and both of the secondary objectives.
explanation: Proxy servers provide network users with access to Internet services, and the unregistered IP addresses on the client computers protect them from unauthorized access by users on the Internet, which satisfies the first objective. The proxy servers also make it possible for network administrators to regulate users' access to the Internet, which satisfies one of the two secondary objectives. However, the proxy servers cannot assign IP addresses to the client computers, and the plan makes no mention of DHCP or another automatic TCP/IP configuration mechanism. Therefore, the plan does not satisfy the other secondary objective.
whyWrong: The proposal does meet the primary objective, because proxy servers give access while private addresses protect clients.
The proxy servers can also regulate users' internet access, which meets one secondary objective.
Proxy servers cannot assign IP addresses, so the automatic addressing objective is not met.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 77

stem: Which of the following is not a mechanism for distributing incoming network traffic among multiple servers?
explanation: A virtual private network (VPN) headend is a type of router that enables multiple client systems to access a network from remote locations. It does not distribute traffic among servers. A load balancer is a type of router that forwards traffic with a single IP address to multiple servers in turn. Round-robin DNS is a technique in which a DNS server resolves a name into several IP addresses, each in turn. A network load balancing (NLB) cluster is a group of servers, all running the same application, that distribute incoming traffic among themselves.
whyWrong: A load balancer spreads incoming traffic among a group of servers.
Round-robin DNS resolves one name to several IP addresses in turn to spread traffic.
An NLB cluster is a group of servers that share incoming traffic among themselves.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 78

stem: Which of the following is not a function that is typically provided by a unified threat management (UTM) appliance?
explanation: Network-attached storage (NAS) is a separate device that connects storage to the network; it is not a normal function of a UTM appliance. UTM appliances do typically perform VPN, firewall, and antivirus functions.
whyWrong: UTM appliances typically include VPN functions.
UTM appliances typically include a network firewall.
UTM appliances typically include antivirus and antimalware protection.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 79
note: N10-009 does not name UTM appliances; the closest objective is 1.2 (firewall appliances).

stem: A multilayer switch can operate at which layers of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: A multilayer switch typically operates at the Data link and Network layers, assuming the functions of a switch and a router by using media access control (MAC) addresses at the Data link layer (layer 2) and IP addresses at the Network layer (layer 3) to forward packets to their appropriate destinations. Some switches also function at the Transport layer (layer 4) by distinguishing between User Datagram Protocol (UDP) and Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) traffic and using port numbers to forward packets.
whyWrong: A multilayer switch is described by the Data link and higher layers it forwards on, not by the Physical layer.
A multilayer switch does not work at the Session layer.
A multilayer switch does not work at the Presentation layer.
A multilayer switch does not work at the Application layer.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 80

stem: Control plane policing (CPP or CoPP) is a feature on some routers and switches that limits the rate of traffic on the device's processor to prevent denial-of-service (DoS) and reconnaissance attacks, using which of the following technologies?
explanation: Control plane policing uses quality of service (QoS) policies to block, allow, or impose rate limits on the traffic processed by the router or switch. IPsec is a Network layer security mechanism that encrypts or authenticates traffic. 802.1X is a network authentication mechanism. Router Advertisement (RA) guard is a feature found on certain switches that prevents the misuse of RA messages to redirect traffic. VLAN hopping is a method for sending commands to switches to transfer a port from one VLAN to another.
whyWrong: IPsec encrypts or authenticates traffic at the Network layer and does not rate-limit traffic.
802.1X is a port-based network authentication method.
RA guard is a switch feature that blocks misused IPv6 Router Advertisement messages.
VLAN hopping is an attack that gets traffic into another VLAN, not a rate limiting technology.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 81

stem: Which of the following is a device that switches calls between endpoints on the local IP network and provides access to external Internet lines?
explanation: A private branch exchange (PBX) switches internal calls and provides access to external lines. A VoIP PBX performs the same tasks as a traditional PBX. A VoIP gateway is the device that provides the conduit between an IP network and the public switched telephone network (PSTN). A VoIP endpoint is a device that makes use of the VoIP system, such as a computer or handset. A multilayer switch is a data networking device that includes both switching and routing capabilities.
whyWrong: A VoIP gateway connects the IP network to the public switched telephone network.
A VoIP endpoint is a device that uses the VoIP system, such as a handset.
A multilayer switch is a data device with switching and routing functions, not a call switch.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 82
note: N10-009 does not name VoIP PBX; the closest objective is 1.2 (network appliances).

stem: Which of the following is the true definition of the term modem?
options: A device that connects a computer to the public switched telephone network (PSTN)
A device that connects a local area network (LAN) to the Internet
A device that converts analog signals to digital signals and back again
A device that connects a local area network (LAN) to a wide area network (WAN)
explanation: A modem (modulator/demodulator) is any device that converts analog signals to digital signals and digital signals back to analog signals. The digital device does not have to be a computer, and the analog device does not have to be the PSTN. There are many devices that are incorrectly referred to as modems, such as devices that connect a digital LAN to a digital WAN or all-digital devices that connect computers to the Internet.
whyWrong: Connecting a computer to the PSTN describes only one use of a modem, not its defining function.
A device that links a LAN to the Internet is a router or gateway, and that link can be fully digital.
A device that links a LAN to a WAN is a router, and that link does not need any analog conversion.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 83

stem: Which of the following terms are used to describe the device used to place calls on a Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) installation? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: VoIP uses the terms terminal and endpoint to refer to the device with which users make calls, including computers and telephone handsets. A VoIP gateway is the device that provides the conduit between an IP network and the public switched telephone network (PSTN). A VoIP private branch exchange (PBX) is a device that switches calls between endpoints on the local IP network and provides access to external Internet lines.
whyWrong: A VoIP gateway connects the IP network to the PSTN and is not the device users call from.
A VoIP PBX switches calls between endpoints and outside lines rather than being the device used to place calls.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 84
note: VoIP devices are not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with the closest objective (network appliances).

stem: Which of the following devices enables you to use a standard analog telephone to place calls using the Internet instead of the public switched telephone network (PSTN)?
explanation: A VoIP gateway is a device that provides a conduit between an IP network and the public switched telephone network (PSTN). The gateway enables standard telephones connected to the PSTN to place calls using VoIP services on the Internet. A proxy server is an Application layer device that provides web browsers and other client programs to access the Internet. A virtual private network (VPN) headend enables multiple client systems to access a network from remote locations. A unified threat management (UTM) appliance typically performs VPN, firewall, and antivirus functions.
whyWrong: A proxy server makes requests to Internet resources for clients and does not connect analog phones.
A VPN headend accepts remote VPN client connections and does not convert analog telephone calls.
A UTM appliance combines firewall, VPN, and antivirus functions and does not connect analog phones to VoIP.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 85

stem: Which of the following prevents packets on a TCP/IP internetwork from being transmitted endlessly from router to router?
explanation: TTL is a value included in the IPv4 header that specifies the maximum number of hops the packet is allowed on the network. Each router processing the packet reduces the TTL value by one and discards the packet when the value reaches zero. OSPF is a routing protocol. MTU specifies the maximum size of a frame. Administrative distance is a value that routers use to select the most efficient route to a destination.
whyWrong: OSPF is a link-state routing protocol that builds routing tables, not a hop limit in the packet.
MTU sets the largest frame or packet size a link can carry, not how many hops a packet may take.
Administrative distance ranks how trustworthy a route source is when a router selects routes.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 86

stem: Which of the following is the abbreviation for a network of Internet datacenters supplying end users with localized access to their data?
explanation: A content delivery network (CDN) is a geographically scattered array of datacenters that provides users with access to their data from a nearby site, thereby decreasing latency delays and reducing bandwidth utilization. Quality of service (QoS) is a technique for prioritizing traffic by tagging packets based on their content. Network-attached storage (NAS) refers to a device containing shared drives that is connected to a network. A storage area network (SAN) is a separate network dedicated to shared storage devices.
whyWrong: QoS prioritizes certain traffic types on a network and is not a group of datacenters.
NAS is a single storage device with shared drives attached to the network.
A SAN is a separate network dedicated to shared block storage devices.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 87

stem: Which of the following cloud service models enables you to perform a new installation of an operating system of your choice?
