explanation: The infrastructure as a service (IaaS) model provides consumers with processing, storage, and networking resources that they can use to install and run operating systems and other software of their choice. Platform as a service (PaaS) provides consumers with the ability to install applications of their choice on a server installed by the provider. Software as a service (SaaS) provides consumers with access to specific applications running on the provider's servers. Desktop as a service (DaaS) provides remote virtualization of the entire workstation desktop, instead of a single application.
whyWrong: PaaS supplies a server with the operating system already installed, so you cannot install your own OS.
SaaS supplies only a finished application running on the provider's servers.
DaaS supplies a virtual desktop that the provider manages, not a blank system for your own OS installation.
Only IaaS gives the consumer control over the operating system installation.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 88

stem: When you contract with a provider to obtain email services for your company using their servers in the public cloud, which of the following service models are you using?
explanation: The software as a service (SaaS) model provides consumers with access to a specific application running on the provider's servers. Infrastructure as a service (IaaS) provides the consumers with processing, storage, and networking resources that they can use to install and run operating systems and other software of their choice. Platform as a service (PaaS) provides consumers with the ability to install applications of their choice on a server installed by the provider. Desktop as a service (DaaS) provides remote virtualization of the entire workstation desktop, instead of a single application.
whyWrong: IaaS supplies raw compute, storage, and networking on which you would have to install and run the email server yourself.
PaaS supplies a platform for your own applications rather than a finished email service.
DaaS supplies a full virtual desktop rather than a single application such as email.
A hosted email application is a clear example of the SaaS model.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 89

stem: Which of the following cloud service models provides the consumer with the most control over the cloud resources?
options: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, and DaaS all provide the same degree of control.
explanation: The infrastructure as a service (IaaS) model provides consumers with the most control, as the provider furnishes processing, storage, and networking resources that the consumer can use as needed. Platform as a service (PaaS) provides consumers with the ability to install applications of their choice on a server furnished by the provider, but they have only limited control over the server and no control over the underlying resources. Software as a service (SaaS) and desktop as a service (DaaS) provide consumers with access to a specific application or an entire desktop environment running on the provider's servers, but the consumers have no control over the operating system, the servers, or the underlying resources.
whyWrong: PaaS gives control of your applications but only limited control of the server and none of the underlying resources.
SaaS gives control of only some application settings and none of the operating system or servers.
DaaS gives a desktop environment but no control of the servers or underlying resources.
The service models differ in control, and IaaS gives the consumer the most.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 90

stem: Alice has just created a new Windows Server virtual machine using remote controls provided by a cloud service provider on the Internet. Which of the following cloud architectures is she using? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Infrastructure as a service (IaaS) provides consumers like Alice with processing, storage, and networking resources that they can use to install and run operating systems and other software of their choice. In the public cloud model, one organization or user functions as the provider, and another organization or user—in this case, Alice—consumes the services of the provider. Platform as a service (PaaS) provides consumers with the ability to install applications of their choice on a server furnished by the provider. Software as a service (SaaS) provides consumers with access to a specific application running on the provider's servers. In a private cloud, the same organization that utilizes the cloud services is also the sole owner of the infrastructure that provides those services. A hybrid cloud is a combination of public and private infrastructure so that the consumer organization is only a partial owner of the infrastructure. A virtual private cloud (VPC) is a secured private cloud hosted within a public cloud.
whyWrong: PaaS supplies a server that the provider has already installed, so Alice would not create the Windows Server VM herself.
SaaS supplies only a finished application, not a virtual machine.
A private cloud is owned by the same organization that uses it, not by a provider on the Internet.
A hybrid cloud combines public and private resources, and the question describes only a public provider.
A VPC is an isolated private network inside a public cloud, and nothing in the question says one is in use.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 91

stem: In which of the following cloud models can a single organization function as both the provider and the consumer of all cloud services?
explanation: In a private cloud, the same organization that utilizes the cloud services can also be the sole owner of the infrastructure that provides those services. A private cloud can also be owned by a third party, all or in part. In the public cloud model, one organization functions as the provider, and another organization consumes the services of the provider. A hybrid cloud is a combination of public and private infrastructure so that the consumer organization is only a partial owner of the infrastructure. A multicloud is an integrated environment consisting of multiple cloud services from multiple providers.
whyWrong: In a public cloud one organization is the provider and a different one is the consumer.
A hybrid cloud combines public and private resources, so the consumer owns only part of the infrastructure.
A multicloud uses services from several different providers.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 92

stem: Ed is the overnight manager of his company's datacenter, and he is responsible for both private and public resources in the company's hybrid cloud. Due to a new TV commercial shown that night, the company's website experiences a massive upsurge in traffic. The web server farm on the private cloud is being overwhelmed, so Ed configures some virtual machines in the public cloud to take up the slack. Which of the following is a common term for what Ed has done?
explanation: Cloud bursting is a common term for the offloading of excess traffic from private to public cloud resources when necessary to maintain satisfactory performance levels. Cloud busting, cloud splitting, and cloud migrating are not standard cloud computing terms.
whyWrong: Cloud busting is not a standard cloud computing term.
Cloud splitting is not a standard cloud computing term.
Cloud migrating is not a standard term for temporarily offloading peak traffic to public resources.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 93

stem: Microsoft's Outlook.com email service is an example of which of the following cloud service models?
explanation: Software as a service (SaaS) provides consumers with access to a specific application running on the provider's servers (in this case, an email service). Consumers have control over some of their email functions, but they have no control over the operating system, the servers, or the underlying resources. The infrastructure as a service (IaaS) model provides the consumers with access to processing, storage, and networking resources that the consumer can use as needed. Platform as a service (PaaS) provides consumers with the ability to install applications of their choice on a server furnished by the provider. Desktop as a service (DaaS) provides remote virtualization of the entire workstation desktop, instead of a single application.
whyWrong: IaaS supplies raw compute, storage, and networking rather than a finished email application.
PaaS supplies a platform on which you install your own applications.
DaaS supplies a full virtual desktop rather than a single application.
A hosted email service is a clear example of the SaaS model.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 94

stem: Which of the following statements about cloud delivery models is true?
options: A public cloud is inherently insecure because anyone can access it.
A private cloud consists of hardware that is all located in a single datacenter.
A hybrid cloud enables administrators to migrate services between public and private resources.
Public, private, and hybrid clouds all utilize the same hardware resources.
explanation: A hybrid cloud consists of both public and private resources. One of its main advantages is that administrators can move services from private to public cloud servers and back again as needed, depending on the current workload. Public cloud resources require authentication, so while they might be less secure than a private cloud, they are not inherently insecure. The term private cloud refers to hardware resources that are owned and operated by either a single organization or a third party, regardless of their location. The various cloud delivery models do not impose specific hardware resource requirements.
whyWrong: Public cloud resources require authentication, so they are not inherently insecure.
A private cloud is defined by who owns and uses it, not by keeping all hardware in one datacenter.
The cloud delivery models do not require any specific or shared hardware resources.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 95

stem: Ed has just created a new Windows application for his company and wants to deploy it in the public cloud. He is looking for a provider that will furnish his company with a fully installed and configured Windows server on which he can install and run his application. Which of the following service models is he seeking to use?
explanation: The platform as a service (PaaS) model provides consumers with the ability to install applications of their choice on a server furnished by the provider. Infrastructure as a service (IaaS) provides the consumers with processing, storage, and networking resources that they can use to install and run operating systems and other software of their choice. Software as a service (SaaS) provides consumers with access to a specific application running on the provider's servers. Desktop as a service (DaaS) provides remote virtualization of the entire workstation desktop, instead of a single application.
whyWrong: IaaS would require Ed to install and configure the Windows server himself.
SaaS supplies a finished application from the provider, so Ed could not run his own application on it.
DaaS supplies a virtual desktop rather than a server for hosting an application.
PaaS matches Ed's need for a provider-installed server that runs his own application.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 96

stem: Which of the following are valid advantages or disadvantages of multitenancy in a public cloud datacenter? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Multitenancy presents a potential security risk because other tenants are utilizing the same hardware.
Multitenancy reduces the cost of utilities and other overhead.
Multitenancy introduces the possibility of competition for bandwidth with other tenants.
Multitenancy separates tenants by assigning each one its own virtual machine.
explanation: Multitenancy is a software architecture in which multiple tenants share a single instance of an application running in the cloud. Because tenants share a single application, there is a chance that data could be compromised. Because a single application instance is running in the cloud, the operational overhead is reduced compared to the use of individual virtual machines. Tenants share a finite amount of bandwidth, so the possibility exists for competition to occur, such as when one tenant is the target of a denial-of-service (DoS) attack. Multitenancy does not call for tenants to have individual virtual machines.
whyWrong: Multitenancy shares one application instance among tenants rather than giving each tenant its own virtual machine.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 97

stem: Ralph is designing a hybrid deployment for a corporate client that will require a connection between the client's private network and a public cloud provider. The client is concerned about this connection becoming a speed bottleneck at times of heavy user traffic. Which of the following options can Ralph offer the client that will BEST address this potential problem?
options: Use a different ISP for the cloud connection.
Use a VPN for the cloud connection.
Use a cloud direct connection for the hybrid link.
Use a leased line connection to the ISP.
explanation: A cloud direct connection is a private link between the client's private network and the cloud service provider. This link is independent from any ISP connection used by the client organization for other traffic, so it ensures a consistent bandwidth for the hybrid cloud network. Using a different ISP or a leased line does not replace the entire connection; there are still potential bottlenecks. A VPN can provide better performance than a standard connection and greater security, but it is not as consistent (or as expensive) as a direct cloud connection.
whyWrong: A different ISP still leaves the cloud link on a shared Internet path that can become a bottleneck.
A VPN adds security over the Internet, but its bandwidth still depends on shared Internet links.
A leased line to the ISP improves only the first segment, and traffic still crosses the shared Internet to reach the cloud.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 98

stem: Which of the following is not one of the primary components of the network functions virtualization (NFV) framework?
explanation: The NFV specification, published by the European Telecommunications Standards Institute (ETSI), calls for three main components: virtualized network functions (VNFs), which are software-based implementations of standard network services, such as firewalls and load balancers; a network functions virtualization infrastructure (NFVI), which is the hardware/software environment that hosts the VNFs; and a network functions virtualization-management and orchestration (NFV-MANO) framework, which includes the elements required to deploy and administer the NFVI and the VNFs. The Network Functions Virtualization Industry Specification Group (NFV ISG) is the group within ETSI that develops the NFV specifications; it is not one of the three components.
whyWrong: VNFs, the software versions of network services, are one of the three NFV components.
NFVI, the hardware and software environment that hosts VNFs, is one of the three NFV components.
NFV-MANO, the management and orchestration framework, is one of the three NFV components.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 99

stem: Ralph is designing the datacenter for his company's new branch office. He is considering various options, including building a new datacenter at the branch office facility, using a colocated datacenter, and creating a virtual datacenter using a public cloud provider. Which of the following statements about the differences between these options are true? (Choose all that apply.)
options: A colocated datacenter would be less expensive to implement than a branch office or public cloud datacenter.
In a branch office or colocated datacenter, Ralph's company would own the hardware.
In all three datacenter options, the administrators in Ralph's company would be responsible for setting up and managing the hardware.
In a branch office or colocated datacenter, Ralph's company would be responsible for all utility costs, including heating, cooling, and power.
A public cloud datacenter would have greater physical security than the other two options.
A public cloud datacenter is easier to expand than a colocated or branch office datacenter.
explanation: In a colocated datacenter, a client houses its own servers and other hardware in a shared third-party facility. Therefore, Ralph's company would own the hardware in a branch office or colocated datacenter. A datacenter in a public cloud is easier to expand than the other options because it is simply a matter of creating additional virtual devices. A colocated datacenter would be less expensive to implement than a branch office datacenter, but the public cloud option would require the smallest initial outlay. The administrators would set up and manage the hardware in a branch office or colocated datacenter, but not in a public cloud datacenter. In a colocated datacenter, Ralph's company would share utility costs with other tenants. A public cloud facility is not necessarily more secure.
whyWrong: The public cloud option needs the smallest initial outlay, so a colocated datacenter is not the least expensive.
In a public cloud the provider sets up and manages the hardware, not the company's administrators.
In a colocated datacenter the utility costs are shared with the other tenants of the facility.
A public cloud datacenter is not necessarily more physically secure than the other options.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 100

stem: Which of the following statements about the differences between network security groups and security lists is true?
options: Security lists contain ingress and egress rules that apply to all of the virtual network interface cards (VNICs) in a subnet.
Network security groups can have no more than five member VNICs.
A VNIC can be added to no more than five security lists.
Network security groups can only contain members from their assigned subnet.
explanation: Security lists are virtual firewalls that contain rules that apply to all of the VNICs on a designated subnet. Network security groups are not limited to five member VNICs and can have members from any subnet in the virtual cloud network. A VNIC can be a member of no more than five network security groups, not security lists.
whyWrong: Network security groups are not limited to five member VNICs.
The five-group limit applies to the network security groups of a VNIC, not to security lists.
Network security groups can contain VNICs from any subnet in the virtual cloud network.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 102

stem: Which of the following statements about the differences between a NAT gateway and an Internet gateway in a virtual cloud network (VNC) are true? (Choose all that apply.)
options: A NAT gateway allows traffic from the VNC to reach the Internet but does not allow Internet traffic into the VNC.
A NAT gateway allows VNC traffic both to and from the Internet.
An Internet gateway allows traffic from the VNC to reach the Internet but does not allow Internet traffic into the VNC.
An Internet gateway allows VNC traffic both to and from the Internet.
explanation: A network address translation (NAT) gateway enables elements on a virtual cloud network to connect to services on the Internet but allows no public Internet traffic onto the VNC. An Internet gateway allows traffic in both directions between the VNC and the Internet.
whyWrong: A NAT gateway allows only outbound connections and blocks unsolicited inbound traffic from the Internet.
An Internet gateway allows traffic in both directions, not only outbound.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 103

stem: Which of the following pairs of well-known ports are the default values you would use to configure a POP3 email client?
explanation: The default port for the Post Office Protocol (POP3) is 110. The default port for the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP), the other protocol used by email clients, is 25. Port 143 is the default for the Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP), a different email mailbox protocol that clients never use with POP3. Port 80 is the default for the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP), which is not used by POP3 email clients.
whyWrong: Port 143 is IMAP, a different mailbox protocol that is not used together with POP3.
Port 143 is IMAP, and the client also needs SMTP on port 25 to send mail.
Port 80 is HTTP, which a POP3 email client does not use.
Port 80 is HTTP, and the client also needs POP3 on port 110 to receive mail.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 104

stem: Which of the following server applications use two well-known port numbers during a typical transaction?
explanation: The File Transfer Protocol (FTP) uses two port numbers. It uses the first, port 21, for a control connection that remains open during the entire client/server session. The second port, 20, is for a data connection that opens only when the protocol is actually transferring a file between the client and the server. Network Time Protocol (NTP), Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP), and Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) all use a single port on the server.
whyWrong: NTP uses a single well-known port, UDP 123.
SNMP agents answer requests on a single well-known port, 161.
HTTP uses a single well-known port, 80.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 105

stem: Which of the following protocols does the Ping utility use to exchange messages with another system?
explanation: Ping uses the Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) to exchange messages with other systems. ICMP is also used to return error messages to sending systems. The User Datagram Protocol (UDP) and the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) are both Transport layer protocols that carry Application layer data; Ping does not use either one. The Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP) is used to create multicast groups; Ping does not use it.
whyWrong: UDP is a Transport layer protocol that carries application data, and Ping does not use it.
TCP is a connection-oriented Transport layer protocol, and Ping does not use it.
IGMP manages multicast group membership and is not used by Ping.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 106

stem: Which of the following components does the port number in a Transport layer protocol header identify?
explanation: The port numbers specified in a Transport layer protocol header identify the application that generated the data in the packet or the application that will receive the data. Port numbers do not identify Transport layer protocols, gateways, or proxy servers.
whyWrong: The protocol field in the IP header, not the port number, identifies the Transport layer protocol.
A gateway is identified by its IP address, not by a port number.
A proxy server is identified by its address, not by the port number in a packet header.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 107

stem: Which of the following organizations is responsible for assigning the well-known port numbers used in Transport layer protocol headers?
options: Institute for Electronic and Electrical Engineers (IEEE)
explanation: The IANA assigns values for well-known port numbers. The IEEE publishes Ethernet standards, among many others. The IETF develops standards for Internet technologies. The ISO developed the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model.
whyWrong: The IEEE publishes Ethernet and wireless standards, not port number assignments.
The IETF develops Internet standards but does not assign the port numbers.
The ISO developed the OSI model and does not assign port numbers.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 108

stem: Which of the following is the default well-known port number for the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) used for web client/server communications?
explanation: Port 80 is the default well-known port for HTTP. Port 22 is for the Secure Shell (SSH) protocol, port 20 is for File Transfer Protocol (FTP), and port 443 is for secured HTTP.
whyWrong: Port 22 is used by SSH.
Port 20 is used by FTP for data transfers.
Port 443 is used by HTTPS, the secured version of HTTP.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 109

stem: The secured version of the Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS) uses a different well-known port from the unsecured version. Which of the following ports is used by HTTPS by default?
explanation: The well-known port for HTTPS is 443. Port 25 is for the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP), port 80 is for unsecured HTTP, and port 110 is for the Post Office Protocol (POP3).
whyWrong: Port 25 is used by SMTP.
Port 80 is used by unsecured HTTP.
Port 110 is used by POP3.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 110

stem: What field in the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) Option subheader specifies the size of the largest segment a system can receive?
explanation: The Maximum Segment Size (MSS) field in the TCP Options subheader specifies the size (in bytes) of the largest segment a system can receive. The Window field indicates the amount of data (in bytes) that the receiver can accept. There are no MMS or WinMS fields in a TCP header.
whyWrong: The Window field gives the amount of data the receiver can accept, not the largest segment size.
There is no MMS field in a TCP header.
There is no WinMS field in a TCP header.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 111

stem: What is the term for the combination of an IPv4 address and a port number, as in the following example: 192.168.1.3:23?
explanation: The term for an IPv4 address and port number in combination is socket. An organizationally unique identifier (OUI) identifies a manufacturer of networking hardware. A well-known port is a port number assigned to a specific application. A network address is the network identifier part of an IP address. A domain is a group of computers and other resources.
whyWrong: An OUI is the part of a MAC address that identifies the hardware manufacturer.
A well-known port is only the port number assigned to a specific application.
A network address is the network identifier part of an IP address.
A domain is a group of computers and other resources, not an address and port pair.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 112

stem: Which of the following protocols generate messages that are carried directly within Internet Protocol (IPv4) datagrams, with no intervening Transport layer protocol? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) and Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP) are unusual in that they generate messages that are encapsulated directly within IP datagrams. Nearly all of the other TCP/IP protocols, including Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) and Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP), are encapsulated within one of the Transport layer protocols—User Datagram Protocol (UDP) or Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)—which is encapsulated in turn within an IP datagram.
whyWrong: SMTP messages are carried inside TCP segments, not directly in IP datagrams.
SNMP messages are carried inside UDP datagrams, not directly in IP datagrams.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 113

stem: Which of the following protocols is used to exchange directory service information?
explanation: The Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) is an Application layer protocol used for managing and accessing information stored in directory services. The Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) is used to establish a graphical remote control session with another computer. The Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is used to carry information gathered by management agents distributed around a network to a central management server. Server Message Block (SMB) is the primary file sharing protocol used by Windows systems.
whyWrong: RDP opens a graphical remote control session with another computer.
SNMP carries management data from agents to a central management server.
SMB is the Windows file and printer sharing protocol.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 114

stem: Ralph is configuring a new email client on a workstation to use the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) and Post Office Protocol (POP3) email protocols. He wants SMTP to use encryption when communicating with the email server. Which of the following port numbers should Ralph use to create the POP3 connection and secure the SMTP connection with Transport Layer Security (TLS)? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: SMTP Secure (SMTPS) uses port number 587. POP3 uses port number 110. Port number 25 is used for SMTP without encryption. Port number 443 is used for Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS).
whyWrong: Port 25 is used by SMTP without encryption.
Port 443 is used by HTTPS for secure web traffic.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 115

stem: Which of the following is not a port number used for Structured Query Language (SQL) communications?
explanation: The port number 3389 is used by the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) and is not involved in SQL communication. Port 1433 is used by SQL Server; port 1521 is used by SQLnet; and port 3306 is used by MySQL.
whyWrong: Port 1433 is used by Microsoft SQL Server.
Port 1521 is used by Oracle SQL*Net.
Port 3306 is used by MySQL.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 116

stem: Which of the following port numbers is assigned to a Unix/Linux logging services program?
explanation: Port number 514 is assigned to syslog, a Unix/Linux standard designed to facilitate the transmission of log entries generated by a device or process, such as the sendmail SMTP server, across an IP network to a message collector, called a syslog server. Port number 389 is assigned to the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP). Port number 636 is assigned to LDAP over Secure Sockets Layer (SSL). Port number 993 is assigned to Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP) over SSL.
whyWrong: Port 389 is used by LDAP.
Port 636 is used by LDAP over SSL (LDAPS).
Port 993 is used by IMAP over SSL.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 117

stem: Which of the following is the primary Application layer protocol used by web browsers to communicate with web servers?
explanation: Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS) is the primary protocol used for web client/server communications. Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) is a coding language used to create web content. Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) and File Transfer Protocol (FTP) can both be used in web communications, but neither is the primary protocol.
whyWrong: HTML is a markup language for building web pages, not a communications protocol.
SMTP is an email transfer protocol, not the main web protocol.
FTP is a file transfer protocol, not the main protocol between browsers and web servers.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 118

stem: Which of the following protocols appears on the network as a service that client computers use to resolve names into IP addresses?
explanation: The Domain Name System (DNS) is a protocol that computers on a TCP/IP use to resolve host and domain names into the IP addresses they need to communicate. Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) and Bootstrap Protocol (BOOTP) are both IP address allocation protocols, although BOOTP has largely been superseded by DHCP, and Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) carries information gathered by agents to a central management console.
whyWrong: DHCP assigns IP addresses and other settings to clients and does not resolve names.
BOOTP is an older IP address allocation protocol that DHCP replaced.
SNMP carries management data from agents to a central console.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 119

stem: Which of the following protocols use the term datagram to describe the data transfer unit they create? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: The term datagram is typically used by protocols offering connectionless delivery service. The two main connectionless protocols in the TCP/IP suite are the Internet Protocol (IP) and the User Datagram Protocol (UDP), both of which use the term datagram. Ethernet uses the term frame, and Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) uses segment.
whyWrong: Ethernet calls its data unit a frame.
TCP calls its data unit a segment.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 120

stem: What is the native file sharing protocol used on all Microsoft Windows operating systems?
explanation: The default file sharing protocol used on all Windows operating systems is SMB. HTTPS is the native protocol used by web clients and servers. NFS is the native file sharing protocol used on Unix/Linux networks. FTP is a protocol used for transferring files from one system to another. LDAP is a protocol for transmitting directory service information.
whyWrong: HTTPS is the secure protocol used by web clients and servers.
NFS is the native file sharing protocol of Unix and Linux.
FTP transfers files between systems but is not the native Windows file sharing protocol.
LDAP carries directory service information.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 121

stem: When analyzing captured TCP/IP packets, which of the following control bits must you look for in the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) header to determine whether the receiving host has successfully received the sending host's data?
explanation: The receiving host uses the ACK bit to notify the sending host that it has successfully received data. The other control bits are not used to acknowledge receipt of information.
whyWrong: The FIN bit starts the termination of a connection.
The PSH bit asks the receiver to pass data to the application at once.
The SYN bit synchronizes sequence numbers when a connection is set up.
The URG bit marks data as urgent.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 122

stem: Which of the following terms describes the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) exchange that establishes a connection prior to the transmission of any data?
explanation: Two systems establishing a TCP connection exchange three messages before they begin transmitting data. The exchange of these synchronization messages is referred to as a three-way handshake. The other terms listed are not formally used to describe this exchange.
whyWrong: Synchronization describes the SYN messages but is not the formal name of the whole exchange.
Initialization exchange is not a formal term for the TCP connection setup.
Connection establishment describes the purpose but is not the formal name of the exchange.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 123

stem: Alice has been instructed to install 100 Windows workstations, and she is working on automating the process by configuring the workstations to use PXE boots. Each workstation therefore must obtain an IP address from a DHCP server and download a boot image file from a TFTP server. Which of the following well-known ports must Alice open on the firewall separating the workstations from the servers? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) servers use port numbers 67 and 68. The Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP) uses port number 69. Neither protocol uses port 65 or 66.
whyWrong: Port 65 is not used by DHCP or TFTP.
Port 66 is not used by DHCP or TFTP.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 124

stem: Which of the following explanations BEST describes the function of a Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) or User Datagram Protocol (UDP) port number?
options: The port number indicates to the receiver that the sender can activate a specific port only.
The port number is used by both the sender and the receiver to identify the application that generated the information in the datagram.
The port number is used only by the receiver, to indicate the application process running on the sender.
The port number is used by both the sender and the receiver to negotiate a well-known server port for the communicating processes.
explanation: TCP ports and UDP ports identify the application protocol or process that generated the information in a datagram. Client ports are chosen randomly from the range 1024 through 65,535. Server ports are well known and are chosen from the range 1 through 1023.
whyWrong: A port number identifies an application, not a port that only the sender can activate.
Both the sender and the receiver use port numbers, and they identify applications on both ends.
Port numbers identify applications rather than being used to negotiate a server port.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 125

stem: What is the valid range of numbers for the ephemeral client ports used by the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and User Datagram Protocol (UDP)?
explanation: Ephemeral client ports are in the range of 49,152 through 65,535. Well-known TCP and UDP server ports are in the range of 0 through 1023. Registered port numbers are in the range of 1024 through 49,151.
whyWrong: The range 1023 through 65,534 mixes well-known, registered, and ephemeral ports.
0 through 1023 is the range of well-known server ports.
1024 through 49,151 is the range of registered ports.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 126

stem: Which of the following statements about the User Datagram Protocol (UDP) are true? (Choose all that apply.)
options: UDP does not use packet sequencing and acknowledgments.
UDP uses packet sequencing and acknowledgments.
explanation: UDP is a connectionless Transport layer protocol. It has a small, 8-byte header and does not use packet sequencing or acknowledgments.
whyWrong: UDP has no packet sequencing or acknowledgments, which TCP provides.
UDP is connectionless, while TCP is connection-oriented.
A 20-byte minimum header belongs to TCP, not UDP.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 127

stem: Which of the following port values are used by the File Transfer Protocol (FTP)? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: FTP uses two ports: one for control messages (port 21) and one for data transfers (port 20). Port 23 is used by Telnet. Port 53 is used by the Domain Name System (DNS). Port 69 is used by the Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP).
whyWrong: Port 23 is used by Telnet.
Port 53 is used by DNS.
Port 69 is used by TFTP.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 128

stem: Which of the following protocols provides connectionless delivery service at the Transport layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model?
explanation: The User Datagram Protocol (UDP) provides connectionless service at the Transport layer. Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) provides connection-oriented service at the Transport layer. Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) is an Application layer protocol, and Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) is a Data link layer protocol.
whyWrong: TCP provides connection-oriented service at the Transport layer.
HTTP is an Application layer protocol.
ARP resolves IP addresses to MAC addresses and does not provide Transport layer service.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 129

stem: What is the valid range of numbers for the well-known Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and User Datagram Protocol (UDP) ports used by servers?
explanation: Well-known TCP and UDP server ports are in the range of 1 through 1023. Registered port numbers are in the range of 1024 to 49151. Ephemeral client ports are in the range of 49152 through 65535.
whyWrong: 1024 through 49151 is the range of registered ports.
1 through 49151 includes both the well-known and the registered ports.
49152 through 65534 falls within the range of ephemeral client ports.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 130

stem: Ralph is a network administrator who has just installed a new open-source email server for the users at his company. The server is configured to send and receive Internet email and create a mailbox for each user that will permanently store the user's mail on the server. Ralph next uses a protocol analyzer to examine the network traffic resulting from the new server installation. Which of the following new protocols should Ralph expect to see in his network traffic analysis? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Ralph's traffic analysis should show the addition of the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP), which handles incoming and outgoing Internet mail, and Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP), which provides mailboxes for users that store their mail permanently on the server. POP3 is a mailbox protocol that enables users to download their messages and therefore should not be present on the network. SNMP is a network management protocol, and RIP is a routing protocol; neither of these carries email traffic.
whyWrong: SNMP is a network management protocol and does not carry email.
POP3 downloads messages to the client, so it does not match mailboxes that keep mail permanently on the server.
RIP is a routing protocol and does not carry email.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 131

stem: Which of the following values could a web client use as an ephemeral port number when communicating with a web server?
explanation: An ephemeral port number is a temporary port supplied by a client to a server, for use during a single session or transaction. The allowed ephemeral port number values range from 49152 to 65535. The port values below 1024 are reserved for use as well-known ports, and the values from 1024 to 49151 are reserved for ports registered by specific manufacturers for their applications. Of these answers, 50134 is the only value that the client can use as an ephemeral port.
whyWrong: Port 1 is in the well-known port range reserved for server applications.
Port 23 is the well-known port for Telnet.
Port 80 is the well-known port for HTTP on the web server.
Port 1024 is in the registered port range, not the ephemeral range.
Port 1999 is in the registered port range, not the ephemeral range.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 132

stem: Which of the following protocols provides connection-oriented service with guaranteed delivery at the Transport layer of the OSI model?
explanation: The Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) provides connection-oriented service at the Transport layer, with guaranteed delivery. The User Datagram Protocol (UDP) provides connectionless service at the Transport layer. Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) operates at the Application layer, and Internet Protocol (IP) is a connectionless Network layer protocol.
whyWrong: UDP provides connectionless service with no guaranteed delivery.
HTTP operates at the Application layer.
IP is a connectionless Network layer protocol.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 133

stem: Which of the following protocols is limited to use on the local subnet only?
explanation: ARP relies on broadcast transmissions, which are not routable. It is therefore limited to use on the local subnet. DHCP also relies on broadcasts, but the ability to create DHCP relay agents makes it usable on an entire internetwork. DNS and SMTP do not rely on broadcasts and therefore are not limited to the local subnet. GRE is a tunneling protocol used to establish point-to-point links between devices on different networks.
whyWrong: DHCP relies on broadcasts, but DHCP relay agents let it work across an internetwork.
DNS does not rely on broadcasts, so it works across routed networks.
SMTP does not rely on broadcasts, so it works across routed networks.
GRE is a tunneling protocol that carries traffic between devices on different networks.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 134
note: The book explanation called GRE links secure; GRE has no encryption of its own, so the word was removed.

stem: Which of the following prefixes must you use in the URL you type into a web browser when the website you want to access has been secured with Transport Layer Security (TLS)?
explanation: No matter what protocol is used to encrypt a website, you must use the HTTPS:// prefix to access it. HTTP:// is for unencrypted sites, and TLS:// and HTLS:// are nonexistent prefixes.
whyWrong: TLS:// is not a valid URL prefix.
HTTP:// is used for unencrypted websites.
HTLS:// is not a valid URL prefix.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 135

stem: What is the difference when you specify the HTTPS:// prefix in a Uniform Resource Locator (URL) instead of HTTP://? (Choose all that apply.)
options: The connection between the web browser and the server is encrypted.
The browser uses a different port number to connect to the server.
The connection uses SSL or TLS instead of HTTP.
The browser uses a different IP address to connect to the server.
explanation: Using the prefix HTTPS:// causes a web browser to use a different port number to establish a secure connection to the web server. Security is provided by encrypting all data using Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) or Transport Layer Security (TLS). However, SSL and TLS do not replace HTTP; they just augment it. The HTTPS:// prefix does not affect the IP address used to connect to the server.
whyWrong: SSL or TLS adds encryption to HTTP but does not replace it.
The HTTPS prefix does not change the IP address of the server.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 136

stem: You are a consultant installing a web server application for a client called Adatum. The domain name Adatum.com has been registered in the DNS, and the server has one public IP address, so the new website will be accessible to users on the Internet. You want to be able to access the web server application's administrative site from your remote office, so you configure that site to be encrypted and to use the port number 12354 instead of the default. Which of the following URLs will you have to use to access the administrative website?
explanation: Because the administrative site is encrypted, you must use the HTTPS:// prefix to access it. Because the administrative site uses the nondefault port number 12354, you must append that number to the server name with a colon.
whyWrong: This URL is encrypted but uses the default port 443 instead of port 12354.
This URL uses the right port but the unencrypted HTTP prefix.
This URL is unencrypted and uses port 80 instead of port 12354.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 137
note: The extracted options lost their http:// and https:// prefixes; the prefixes were restored from the explanation and the answer.

stem: Which of the following protocols does IPsec use to digitally encrypt packets before transmitting them over the network?
explanation: Encapsulating Security Protocol (ESP) is a protocol in the TCP/IP suite that is capable of providing encryption services for IPsec. Authentication Header (AH) provides digital integrity services for IPsec, in the form of a digital signature. Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) is a security protocol that provides encrypted communications between web browsers and servers. Internet Key Exchange (IKE) is a security protocol that IPsec uses to create security associations that specify agreed-upon policies between systems.
whyWrong: SSL secures web traffic between browsers and servers and is not part of IPsec.
AH provides authentication and integrity for IPsec but no encryption.
IKE negotiates the security associations for IPsec but does not encrypt the packets.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 138

stem: Which of the following are the protocols that IPsec uses to secure network traffic? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Authentication Header (AH) is an IPsec protocol that provides authentication and digital integrity services. Encapsulating Security Protocol (ESP) provides encryption services for IPsec. Secure Shell (SSH) is a remote administration tool, and Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) is a protocol that provides encrypted communications between web browsers and servers.
whyWrong: SSH is a secure remote administration protocol, not part of IPsec.
SSL secures web traffic and is not one of the IPsec protocols.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 139

stem: What is the primary shortcoming of the File Transfer Protocol (FTP) that is addressed by FTPS and SFTP?
explanation: FTP does provide authentication capabilities, but passwords are transmitted over the network in cleartext, which is an unacceptable security condition. FTP Secure (FTPS) adds security in the form of the Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol. SSH File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) uses Secure Shell (SSH) security. File transfer speed and size limitations are not an issue.
whyWrong: FTP transfer speed is not the problem that FTPS and SFTP solve.
FTP has no file size limitation that FTPS and SFTP address.
FTP does authenticate users, but it sends the passwords in cleartext.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 140

stem: Which of the following File Transfer Protocol (FTP) variants do not transmit authentication passwords over the network in cleartext?
explanation: FTPS adds security to FTP in the form of the Transport Layer Security (TLS) and Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) protocols. SFTP uses Secure Shell (SSH) for security. Both of these encrypt authentication passwords before transmitting them. FTP transmits passwords over the network in cleartext, which is an unacceptable security condition. Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP) does not authenticate clients, so it does not transmit passwords at all.
whyWrong: FTP sends user names and passwords over the network in cleartext.
TFTP does not authenticate clients, so it has no passwords to protect.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 141
note: TFTP sends no passwords at all, so it could also be read as fitting the stem; the book answer counts only the variants that encrypt the passwords.

stem: Which of the following File Transfer Protocol (FTP) variants is typically used to download boot image files during Preboot Execution Environment (PXE) startup sequences?
explanation: Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP) is a simplified version of FTP that does not authenticate clients, so systems booting with PXE can download boot images invisibly after being directed to a TFTP server by the Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP). FTP, FTPS, and SFTP all require authentication and other interaction, which would be impractical for use with PXE.
whyWrong: FTP needs user authentication and interaction, which does not suit PXE boots.
FTPS needs authentication and a TLS session, which does not suit PXE boots.
SFTP needs SSH authentication, which does not suit PXE boots.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 142

stem: Which of the following protocols does IPsec use to digitally sign packets before transmitting them over the network?
explanation: Authentication Header (AH) is a protocol in the TCP/IP suite that provides digital integrity services in the form of a digital signature, which ensures that an incoming packet actually originated from its stated source. Encapsulating Security Protocol (ESP) provides encryption services for IPsec. Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) is a security protocol that provides encrypted communications between web browsers and servers. Internet Key Exchange (IKE) is a security protocol that IPsec uses to create security associations that specify agreed-upon policies between systems.
whyWrong: ESP provides encryption for IPsec rather than the digital signature.
SSL secures web traffic and is not part of IPsec.
IKE negotiates security associations for IPsec and does not sign packets.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 143

stem: What must you do to configure a firewall to admit File Transfer Protocol (FTP) traffic to the internal network using its default port settings? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: The FTP protocol uses two well-known ports: 20 and 21. A firewall must have both of these ports open to admit FTP traffic. FTP does not require ports 22, 23, or 24.
whyWrong: Port 22 is used by SSH and SFTP.
Port 23 is used by Telnet.
Port 24 is not used by FTP.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 146

stem: Which of the following protocols uses a form of flow control called the sliding window technique?
explanation: The Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) uses a flow control technique in which the receiving system creates a window of a specific size and allows the transmitting system to send packets until that window is full. When the window is full, the sender stops transmitting. The receiver then sends back an acknowledgment packet that specifies the next packet it expects to receive from the sender. The User Datagram Protocol (UDP), Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP), and Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) do not use the sliding window technique or any other form of flow control.
whyWrong: UDP has no flow control.
HTTP is an Application layer protocol that relies on TCP for flow control.
SIP is a signaling protocol for VoIP calls and does not provide flow control.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 147

stem: Which of the following Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) control bits is set to 1 to initiate the termination of a session?
explanation: The termination phase of a TCP connection begins when either the client or the server sends a message containing the FIN control bit with a value of 1. The other control bits listed have nothing to do with the connection termination procedure, and there is no END bit.
whyWrong: The SYN bit starts a new connection rather than ending one.
The URG bit marks data as urgent.
There is no END control bit in the TCP header.
The PSH bit asks the receiver to pass data to the application at once.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 148

stem: A client on a TCP/IP network is attempting to establish a session with a server. Which of the following correctly lists the order of the TCP flags raised in the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) session establishment messages?
explanation: The TCP connection establishment exchange is a three-way handshake that uses TCP flags to specify the message type for each frame. The first frame contains a SYN flag from the client; the second frame contains the SYN and ACK flags from the server; and the last frame contains an ACK flag from the client.
whyWrong: The server combines its SYN and ACK in one message, so the setup has three messages, not four.
The handshake does not send two SYN messages followed by two ACK messages.
The handshake starts with a plain SYN from the client, not with a SYN/ACK.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 149

stem: Which of the following traffic types is used exclusively on IPv6 networks?
explanation: Anycast addresses are IPv6-only addresses designed to transmit to any one host in a multicast group. Unicast and multicast are traffic types used by both IPv4 and IPv6 networks, while broadcast is used only by IPv4.
whyWrong: Unicast traffic is used on both IPv4 and IPv6 networks.
Broadcast is an IPv4 traffic type, and IPv6 has no broadcast at all.
Multicast traffic is used on both IPv4 and IPv6 networks.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 150
note: The book explanation said IPv6 uses broadcast, which is wrong; that sentence was corrected. Anycast routing is also used with IPv4 in practice, but the book and the exam treat anycast addresses as an IPv6 feature.

stem: Which of the following BEST describes the function of the network medium?
options: The network medium provides the physical connection between networked computers.
The network medium provides the protocol used to transmit data between end systems.
The network medium passes data packets between two routers.
The network medium processes electrical or light signals and converts them to data.
explanation: The network medium provides the physical connection between networked computers. This connection can be made through a copper-based, fiber-optic, or wireless medium. The network medium is not a protocol, and it does not pass data packets; it only carries signals. The network medium does not process electrical or light pulses and convert them to data; it carries only the signals generated by transceivers.
whyWrong: Protocols are software rules at higher layers, not the network medium.
Routers pass packets, while the medium only carries signals.
Transceivers convert signals to data, while the medium only carries the signals.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 151

stem: Which of the following signal types is carried by copper cable?
explanation: Copper cables use electrical signals to transmit data. Fiber-optic is a cable type, not a signal type. Microwave signals cannot be transmitted over copper cable. Infrared signals are used only for wireless networks.
whyWrong: Fiber-optic is a cable type that carries light, not a signal type carried by copper.
Microwave signals travel through the air, not over copper cable.
Infrared signals are light used for some wireless links, not copper cable.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 152

stem: Identify the organizations that developed the general cable type standards for voice and data communications that are currently in use and identify their document names.
explanation: The three organizations that collectively developed the T568b document, which defines the standard for a structured cabling system for voice and data communications, are the American National Standards Institute (ANSI), the Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA), and the Electronic Industries Association (EIA). None of the other options are standards organizations or cabling standards.
whyWrong: TVA is not a cabling standards body, and C568 is not a cabling standard.
TWA is not a cabling standards body, and T530-A is not the general cabling standard.
TWA is not a standards body, and the document named is an IEEE LLC standard rather than a cabling standard.
TDA is not a standards body, and the document named is the IEEE wireless LAN standard.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 153
note: The general cabling standard is ANSI/TIA/EIA-568 (now TIA-568); T568B is one of its two wiring pinouts, so the book answer names the pinout rather than the standard.

stem: Which of the following cable types and connectors are used to attach a television set to a cable television (CATV) network?
options: A multimode fiber-optic cable and a Straight Tip (ST) connector
A coaxial cable and a Bayonet-Neill-Concelman (BNC) connector
A twisted-pair cable and an RJ-45 connector
A coaxial cable and an F-type connector
An AUI cable and a vampire tap connector
A twinaxial cable and a Bayonet-Neill-Concelman (BNC) connector
explanation: The cable type and connector used to attach a television set to a CATV network is a coaxial cable with a screw-on F-type connector. Although CATV networks typically use fiber-optic cables and ST connectors for outdoor connections, they do not use fiber for internal connections to television sets. Coaxial cables with BNC connectors are most commonly used for Thin Ethernet LANs, not CATV network connections. Twisted-pair cables and RJ-45 connectors are used for Ethernet LANs and telephone networks, but not CATV networks. AUI cables and vampire tap connectors are used for Thick Ethernet networks. Twinaxial cables are used for SATA 3.0 devices and 100 Gbit Ethernet connections, but not for CATV connections.
whyWrong: Fiber with ST connectors is used for some outdoor CATV links, not to connect the television set.
Coax with BNC connectors was used for Thin Ethernet, not CATV connections to a television.
Twisted pair with RJ-45 connectors is used for Ethernet LANs, not CATV.
AUI cables with vampire taps were used for Thick Ethernet.
Twinaxial cable is used for short high-speed data links such as DAC cables, not CATV.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 154

stem: Which of the following cable types is used for Thick Ethernet network segments?
explanation: The cable type used for Thick Ethernet segments is a coaxial cable called RG-8. RG-58 is used exclusively on Thin Ethernet segments. RJ-45 is a connector type used in twisted-pair cabling for data networks. RJ-11 is a connector type used in twisted-pair cabling for telecommunications networks.
whyWrong: RG-58 was used for Thin Ethernet segments.
RJ-45 is a twisted-pair connector, not a cable type.
RJ-11 is a telephone twisted-pair connector, not a cable type.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 155

stem: Which of the following cable types is used for Thin Ethernet network segments?
explanation: RG-58 coaxial cable is used exclusively for Thin Ethernet segments. RG-8 cable is used for Thick Ethernet segments. RJ-45 is a connector type used in twisted-pair cabling for data networks. RJ-11 is a connector type used in twisted-pair cabling for telecommunications networks.
whyWrong: RG-8 was used for Thick Ethernet segments.
RJ-45 is a twisted-pair connector, not a cable type.
RJ-11 is a telephone twisted-pair connector, not a cable type.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 156

stem: Which of the following coaxial cable types are still in general use? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: RG-6 and RG-59 are 75-ohm cables that are still used for cable television and similar connections. RG-8 and RG-58 are 50-ohm cables that were formerly used for Thick Ethernet and Thin Ethernet, respectively, but are no longer in general use.
whyWrong: RG-8 is a 50-ohm cable that was used for Thick Ethernet and is no longer in general use.
RG-58 is a 50-ohm cable that was used for Thin Ethernet and is no longer in general use.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 157

stem: Which of the following statements about the differences between fiber-optic Angled Physical Contact (APC) and Ultra Physical Contact (UPC) connectors are true? (Choose all that apply.)
options: APCs should only be joined to other APCs.
APCs generate more insertion loss than UPCs.
UPCs generate more return loss than APCs.
UPCs use a green connector boot or body.
explanation: Joining an APC to a UPC creates a mismatched connection that generates an extremely high rate of insertion loss (attenuation). APCs do generate more insertion loss than UPCs and less return loss (reflection). It is APCs, not UPCs, that use green boots or bodies on the connectors.
whyWrong: APC connectors, not UPC connectors, use a green boot or body.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 158

stem: Which of the following is not a type of fiber-optic connector?
explanation: Bayonet-Neill-Concelman (BNC) is a type of connector used with coaxial cable. Subscriber Connector (SC), Mechanical Transfer-Registered Jack (MT-RJ), Local Connector (LC), and Straight Tip (ST) are all types of fiber-optic connectors.
whyWrong: SC is a square push-pull fiber-optic connector.
MT-RJ is a small fiber-optic connector that holds two fibers.
ST is a round bayonet-style fiber-optic connector.
LC is a small fiber-optic connector with a latch.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 159

stem: Which of the following Physical layer transceiver module standards is the oldest and therefore the most obsolete?
explanation: The Gigabit Interface Converter (GBIC) transceiver standard was first published in 1995 and defines a maximum data transfer rate of 1.25 Gbps. It was rendered all but obsolete by the Small Form-factor Pluggable (SFP) standard, introduced in 2001, which ran at the same maximum speed but was smaller in size. Subsequent variations on the standard, such as SFP+, Quad Small Form-factor Pluggable (QSFP), and QSFP+, defined devices with faster transfer rates.
whyWrong: SFP replaced GBIC in 2001 with a smaller module at the same speed.
SFP+ is a later, faster version of SFP.
QSFP is a later four-channel module for higher speeds.
QSFP+ is a later, faster version of QSFP.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 160

stem: Which of the following cable types is typically configured in a star/hub and spoke topology, uses eight copper conductors arranged in four pairs, and uses RJ-45 connectors?
explanation: There are two main types of twisted-pair wiring used for data communications: unshielded twisted-pair (UTP) and shielded twisted-pair (STP). Both types can be used in a star/hub and spoke topology. UTP and STP cables contain eight copper conductors twisted in four pairs. UTP and STP cables use RJ-45 connectors to connect end systems to switches, patch panels, and wall plates. RG-8 and RG-58 coaxial cable can only be used in a bus topology. Fiber-optic cable can be used in a star/hub and spoke topology, but it uses either glass or plastic conductors and does not use RJ-45 connectors.
whyWrong: RG-8 is thick coaxial cable used in a bus topology.
RG-58 is thin coaxial cable used in a bus topology.
Fiber-optic cable uses glass or plastic fibers and does not use RJ-45 connectors.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 161

stem: Which of the following statements explains the purpose of the twists in twisted-pair cabling?
options: The twists completely eliminate crosstalk and electromagnetic interference (EMI) in adjacent wire pairs.
The twists prevent crosstalk in adjacent wire pairs and limit the effects of EMI on the signals carried over the cable.
The twists extend the bend radius allowance of the cable.
explanation: The twists in a twisted-pair cable prevent the signals on the different wires from interfering with each other (which is called crosstalk) and also provide resistance to outside electromagnetic interference. The twists have no effect on collisions. The twists cannot completely eliminate the effects of EMI. Twists have nothing to do with the bend radius allowance for the cable.
whyWrong: The twists have no effect on collisions.
The twists reduce crosstalk and EMI but cannot fully remove them.
The twists have nothing to do with the cable's bend radius.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 162

stem: Which of the following combinations of attributes describes the cable used for a Thin Ethernet network?
options: RJ-45, 50-ohm, 0.270-inch, coaxial cable with BNC connectors
RG-59, 75-ohm, 0.242-inch, coaxial cable with F connectors
RG-58, 50-ohm, 0.195-inch, coaxial cable with BNC connectors
RG-8, 50-ohm, 0.405-inch, coaxial cable with N connectors
RJ-6, 75-ohm, 0.242-inch, coaxial cable with BNC connectors
explanation: Thin Ethernet networks use a type of 50-ohm coaxial cable called RG-58, which is 0.195 inches in diameter and uses BNC connectors. A 75-ohm coaxial cable with F-type connectors is used for cable television networks, and RG-8 coaxial is the cable that Thick Ethernet networks use.
whyWrong: RJ-45 is a twisted-pair connector, not a coaxial cable grade.
RG-59 with F connectors is 75-ohm cable used for cable television.
RG-8 with N connectors is the thick coaxial cable used for Thick Ethernet.
RJ-6 is not a coaxial cable grade, and 75-ohm cable is used for television rather than Thin Ethernet.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 163

stem: Which of the following connector types are typically associated with Ethernet networks? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Thin Ethernet networks use coaxial cables with Bayonet Neill–Concelman (BNC) connectors. All unshielded twisted-pair (UTP) Ethernet networks use RJ-45 connectors. F-type connectors are used with coaxial cable, typically for cable television installations, but not for Ethernet. DB-9 connectors are commonly used for serial communications ports.
whyWrong: F-type connectors are used on coaxial cable for cable television, not Ethernet.
DB-9 connectors are used for serial ports.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 164

stem: Which of the following connector types was typically associated with a T-connector attached to the computer?
explanation: Thin Ethernet networks use a type of coaxial cable that runs from each computer to the next one, forming a bus topology. To connect the cable to the network computers, each network interface adapter has a T-connector attached to it, with two additional male Bayonet Neill–Concelman (BNC) connectors, to which you connect two lengths of network cabling.
whyWrong: RJ-45 connectors are used on twisted-pair cable and plug straight into the network adapter.
MT-RJ is a fiber-optic connector.
8P8C is the formal name of the RJ-45 style twisted-pair connector.
F connectors are used for cable television coax and screw directly onto the device.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 165

stem: Which of the following connector types are associated with fiber-optic cables? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Fiber-optic cable connectors all function on the same basic principles, but there are a variety of form factors from which to choose, including Straight Tip (ST), Local Connector (LC), and Mechanical Transfer–Registered Jack (MT-RJ). Multi-fiber Push On (MPO) is a fiber array connector that gathers multiple optical fibers into a single connection. RJ-11 is a twisted-pair cable connector, and F connectors are for coaxial cable.
whyWrong: RJ-11 is a twisted-pair connector used for telephone lines.
F connectors are used on coaxial cable.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 166

stem: Which of the following types of cable, when installed, sometimes employed a device called a vampire tap?
explanation: Thick Ethernet installations used a type of coaxial cable called RG-8. To connect a node to the network, installers ran a separate cable called an Attachment Unit Interface (AUI) cable from the computer to the RG-8 and connected it using a device called a vampire tap that pierced the sheathing to make contact with the conductors within. All of the other cable types listed use different types of connectors.
whyWrong: Unshielded twisted pair uses RJ-45 connectors, not vampire taps.
Shielded twisted pair uses RJ-45 or similar connectors, not vampire taps.
Multimode fiber uses fiber connectors such as SC, ST, and LC.
Single-mode fiber uses fiber connectors such as SC, ST, and LC.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 167

stem: Which of the following statements about single-mode and multimode fiber-optic cables are true? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Single-mode cables can span longer distances than multimode cables.
Single-mode cables are more resistant to electromagnetic interference than multimode cables.
Single-mode cables are more difficult to install than multimode cables.
Single-mode cables have a much larger core diameter than multimode cables.
explanation: Single-mode cables are capable of spanning longer distances than multimode because they have a narrower core diameter, reducing signal dispersion rates. Because the core consists of fewer (typically one or two) strands, single-mode cables are less flexible than multimode and cannot bend around corners as easily, making them more difficult to install. Because they use light impulses rather than electricity, all fiber-optic cables are completely immune to electromagnetic interference.
whyWrong: All fiber-optic cable is immune to EMI because it carries light, so single-mode has no advantage here.
Single-mode fiber has a much smaller core diameter than multimode fiber.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 168

stem: Which of the following statements about single-mode fiber-optic cable are true? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Single-mode cables use an LED light source, whereas multimode cables use a laser.
Single-mode cables can span longer distances than multimode cables.
Single-mode cables have a smaller core filament than multimode cables.
Single-mode cables have a smaller bend radius than multimode cables, making them easier to install.
Single-mode fiber-optic cables require a ground, whereas multimode cables do not.
explanation: Single-mode cables have a smaller core filament and can span longer distances than multimode cables. Single-mode cables also use a laser light source, have a larger bend radius, and do not require a ground.
whyWrong: Single-mode fiber uses a laser light source, while multimode fiber typically uses an LED.
Single-mode fiber has a larger bend radius than multimode, which makes it harder to install.
Fiber-optic cable carries light rather than electricity, so neither type needs a ground.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 170

stem: Ralph has been hired by a client to install cabling to connect two existing networks. The two networks are in different buildings approximately 1,000 feet apart. The cable type must support Gigabit Ethernet data rates of 1,000 megabits per second (Mbps) and provide a high level of resistance to electromagnetic interference (EMI). Your client wants the most economical cabling solution that meets their needs. Which of the following cable types BEST meets the needs of this client?
explanation: Multimode fiber-optic cable best meets the client's needs. Fiber-optic cable supports the required 1,000 Mbps data rate and can connect networks that are more than 1,000 feet apart. Fiber-optic cable is immune to EMI. Although both multimode and single-mode fiber would meet the corporation's general needs, multimode is best in this scenario because it is less expensive than single-mode fiber. Twisted-pair wiring (STP or UTP) meets the data rate and cost requirements but does not support connections longer than 100 meters. Thin coaxial cable does not support the data rate or distances longer than 185 meters.
whyWrong: STP cable is limited to 100-meter segments and does not fully resist EMI.
UTP cable is limited to 100-meter segments and is susceptible to EMI.
