Thin coaxial cable does not support Gigabit speeds and is limited to 185-meter segments.
Single-mode fiber would work but costs more than multimode fiber for this distance.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 172

stem: Which of the following are connector types used with coaxial cables? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Bayonet Neill–Concelman (BNC) connectors are used for coaxial Thin Ethernet networks, and N-type connectors with Thick Ethernet. F-type connectors are used for coaxial cable television installations. Straight Tip (ST) connectors are used with fiber-optic cable, and RJ-11 connectors are used for telephone installations.
whyWrong: ST connectors are used with fiber-optic cable.
RJ-11 connectors are used with telephone twisted-pair cable.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 173

stem: Which of the following cable connector types is not used with fiber-optic cable?
explanation: ST, SC, fiber LC, and MT-RJ are all connectors used with fiber-optic cables. F-type connectors are used with coaxial cables.
whyWrong: ST is a bayonet-style connector used with fiber-optic cable.
SC is a push-pull connector used with fiber-optic cable.
MT-RJ is a duplex connector used with fiber-optic cable.
LC is a small form factor connector used with fiber-optic cable.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 175

stem: Which of the following cable connector types have been rendered nearly obsolete by Universal Serial Bus (USB) connections? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: The DB-9 and DB-25 connectors were at one time ubiquitous on personal computers, providing peripheral connections to modems, printers, and other devices. They have since been largely eliminated in favor of USB. Bayonet Neill–Concelman (BNC) connectors were used for Thin Ethernet networking, but they have been replaced by unshielded twisted-pair (UTP) cable with RJ-45 connectors. RJ-11 connectors are used for telephone connections.
whyWrong: BNC connectors were replaced on LANs by twisted-pair cable with RJ-45 connectors, not by USB.
RJ-11 connectors are still used for telephone connections.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 176
note: DB-9 and DB-25 are not in the N10-009 connector list; matched to 1.5 connector types because the options are connectors.

stem: Which of the following cable types are typically used in newly constructed local area network (LAN) installations? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: The main cable types used in LANs today are multimode fiber-optic and unshielded twisted-pair. Single-mode fiber-optic is used primarily for long-distance wide area network (WAN) connections, and coaxial cable is no longer used for LANs.
whyWrong: Single-mode fiber is used mainly for long-distance WAN links rather than LAN installations.
Coaxial cable is no longer used for new LAN installations.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 177

stem: Which of the following statements are true about coaxial cable? (Choose all that apply.)
options: Coaxial cable has three conductors within the same sheath.
Coaxial cable has two conductors within the same sheath.
Coaxial cable has a copper core that carries light pulse signals.
Coaxial cable has a copper core that carries electrical signals.
Coaxial cable has an insulating outer sheath made of braided strands.
Coaxial cable has an insulating sheath made of either PVC or Teflon.
explanation: Coaxial cable has two conductors within the same sheath that share a common axis. These conductors are surrounded by an outer insulating sheath of either PVC or Teflon. Copper cables carry electrical signals. Only fiber-optic cables carry light pulse signals.
whyWrong: Coaxial cable has two conductors, a center core and a shield, not three.
Only fiber-optic cable carries light pulses; the copper core of coaxial cable carries electrical signals.
The braided strands form the second conductor (shield), and the outer insulating sheath is PVC or Teflon.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 178

stem: Which of the following statements about fiber-optic cabling are true? (Choose all that apply.)
options: There are two main fiber-optic cable types: single-mode and multimode.
Fiber-optic cable is typically used to span long distances.
Fiber-optic cables use IBM Data Connector (IDC) connectors.
Fiber-optic cables often use Straight Tip (ST) and Subscriber Connector (SC) connectors.
Single-mode fiber-optic cable uses a laser light source and a glass core.
Multimode fiber-optic cable uses a light-emitting diode (LED) light source.
explanation: Fiber-optic cable comes in two types: multimode and single-mode. Fiber-optic cables vary in light source (LED or laser), cable grade (glass or plastic), and size of the core conductor. Single-mode uses a higher-grade glass conductor with a laser light source. Multimode fiber uses an LED light source. Both types can use either ST or SC connectors to physically connect end devices to a fiber-optic network. Fiber-optic cable is used to extend networks over long distances. Fiber-optic cables do not use IDC connectors, which are intended for use with shielded twisted-pair (STP) cable.
whyWrong: IDC connectors are used with shielded twisted-pair cable, not fiber-optic cable.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 179

stem: Which of the following IEEE 802.3 specifications calls for CAT8 UTP cable exclusively?
explanation: 40GBase-T is a 40-gigabits-per-second (Gbps) Ethernet specification that calls for 4-pair CAT8 twisted-pair cabling for lengths up to 30 meters. 10GBase-T and 100Base-TX do not require CAT8 cable, and 1000Base-SX is a fiber-optic standard.
whyWrong: 10GBase-T runs on CAT6 or CAT6a cable and does not require CAT8.
100Base-TX runs on CAT5 or better cable and does not require CAT8.
1000Base-SX is a fiber-optic standard that uses multimode fiber.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 181

stem: Ralph has been hired to connect three local area networks (LANs) together with redundant paths that form a fault-tolerant backbone. The LANs reside on different floors in the same building and are approximately 600 meters apart. Each LAN is currently configured in a star/hub and spoke topology using twisted-pair cabling. Each LAN includes wall plates and rack-mounted patch panels and switches. Building and fire codes allow cables to run through existing risers, ceilings, and walls, but a 50,000-watt radio station occupies one of the floors between the LANs. Which topology, cable type, and installation method are BEST suited for this network?
options: Star/hub and spoke topology, fiber-optic cabling, and internal installation
Star/hub and spoke topology, coaxial cabling, and external installation
Mesh topology, fiber-optic cabling, and external installation
Bus topology, twisted-pair cabling, and internal installation
Mesh topology, fiber-optic cabling, and internal installation
Star/hub and spoke topology, twisted-pair cabling, and external installation
explanation: Ralph should use a mesh topology with redundant fiber-optic cable runs and an internal installation method. This will meet the requirements for connecting the LANs and providing redundancy and fault tolerance. Fiber-optic cable is immune to electromagnetic interference (EMI) and can span long distances. The internal installation method is most often used in larger networks, where end systems are geographically distant. The star/hub and spoke topology will not fulfill the requirements since it provides no redundancy. Twisted-pair cable cannot span distances more than 100 meters, and it is susceptible to EMI. Coaxial cable cannot span distances more than 500 meters, and it is also susceptible to EMI. The bus topology cannot use twisted-pair cabling and does not support cable runs longer than 500 meters.
whyWrong: A star topology connects each LAN to one center and does not give the redundant paths the backbone needs.
Coaxial cable is susceptible to EMI, and an external installation is not needed inside one building.
Mesh and fiber fit the need, but the cables can run through the building's risers, so an external installation is not needed.
A bus topology gives no redundancy, and twisted-pair cable cannot span 600 meters or resist the radio station's EMI.
Twisted-pair cable cannot span 600 meters and is susceptible to EMI from the radio station.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 182

stem: Alice is a network consultant who has been contracted to evaluate a network design created many years ago, to determine if the design is still viable. The network will support 20 workstations, scattered throughout the building, to run an inventory database application. The two most distant computers are 150 meters apart. The primary goal for the network design is to connect all 20 workstations to a single LAN running at 1 gigabit per second (Gbps). The two secondary goals are to provide sufficient fault tolerance for a single cable break to occur without affecting the entire network and to provide resistance to the electromagnetic interference (EMI) generated by machinery in the building. The earlier design calls for a CAT 6 UTP Ethernet LAN in a star/hub and spoke topology with all of the computers connected to a single switch. Which of the following statements about the old proposal is true?
options: The solution achieves neither the primary goal nor either of the secondary goals.
The solution achieves the primary goal but neither of the secondary goals.
The solution achieves the primary goal and one of the secondary goals.
The solution achieves the primary goal and both of the secondary goals.
explanation: The CAT 6 UTP network described in the old proposal is sufficient to connect the 20 workstations to a single LAN running at 1 Gbps, thus achieving the primary goal. The star/hub and spoke topology can tolerate a single cable break without affecting the entire network, but the UTP cable is susceptible to EMI, so one secondary goal could not be achieved.
whyWrong: The CAT6 UTP star network does meet the primary goal of a 1 Gbps LAN.
The star topology does meet the fault-tolerance goal because one cable break affects only one computer.
UTP cable is susceptible to EMI, so the EMI resistance goal is not met.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 183

stem: Ed is a network consultant who has been contracted to design the network for a new manufacturing plant. The plant consists of two buildings 150 meters apart: an office with 20 computers and a manufacturing facility that has 30 computers. The two most distant computers at the site are 225 meters apart. Ed's design calls for a Gigabit Ethernet network using fiber-optic cable. On receiving the proposal, the client asks Ed to justify the additional labor and expense of installing fiber-optic cable instead of unshielded twisted-pair (UTP). Which of the following is not a valid reason for choosing fiber-optic over UTP for this project?
options: The 225-meter distance between the two most distant computers exceeds Ethernet's maximum cable segment length for UTP.
Only fiber-optic cable can keep the two buildings electrically isolated.
Fiber-optic cable is completely resistant to any electromagnetic interference generated by the equipment in the manufacturing plant.
Fiber-optic cable provides a greater degree of tolerance to cable breaks than UTP.
explanation: Fiber-optic cable is not more tolerant of cable breaks than UTP. Some fiber-optic networks are fault tolerant, but the Ethernet fiber-optic specifications are not. UTP cables connecting a computer to a switch can be no longer than 100 meters, making 200 meters the maximum distance between two computers. Connecting two buildings with a copper-based cable creates an electrical connection between them, which can be hazardous. Fiber-optic cable does not create an electrical connection. Fiber-optic cable is also unaffected by the EMI generated by manufacturing equipment.
whyWrong: This is a valid reason because UTP links are limited to 100 meters per segment.
This is a valid reason because fiber does not create an electrical connection between the buildings.
This is a valid reason because fiber carries light and is immune to EMI.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 184

stem: Which of the following 802.3 10 Gigabit Ethernet specifications calls for the use of copper cable?
explanation: The 10GBase-CX4 specification calls for the use of a twinaxial copper cable with segments no longer than 15 meters. The 10GBase-LR, 10GBase-ER, 10GBase-LX4, and 10GBase-SR specifications all call for fiber-optic cable.
whyWrong: 10GBase-LR uses single-mode fiber-optic cable.
10GBase-ER uses single-mode fiber-optic cable.
10GBase-LX4 uses fiber-optic cable.
10GBase-SR uses multimode fiber-optic cable.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 185

stem: Alice is a network consultant who has been contracted to upgrade an existing Ethernet network to Gigabit Ethernet. The network consists of 20 workstations with integrated 100Base-TX/1000Base-T network interface adapters. The network cabling is Category 6 (CAT6) unshielded twisted-pair (UTP), installed when the building was constructed. All of the workstations are connected to a single 100Base-TX switch. Which of the following options would Alice find to be a valid upgrade path to Gigabit Ethernet?
options: Replace the CAT6 cable with at least Category 6a (CAT6a) and leave the existing network interface adapters and switch in place.
Install a 1000Base-T network interface card in each computer and leave the existing cables and switch in place.
Replace the CAT6 cable with at least CAT6a and replace the 100Base-T switch with a 1000Base-T switch.
Replace the 100Base-TX switch with a 1000Base-T switch and leave the existing cables and network interface adapters in place.
explanation: The multispeed network interface adapters in the computers can run at 1 Gbps speed using the existing CAT6 cable, but the 100Base-T switch must be replaced with a 1000Base-T switch. While the network might run better with a cable upgrade, it is not immediately necessary. Replacing the network interface adapters is not necessary because the existing multispeed adapters can run at 1 Gbps if they are connected to a 1000Base-T switch.
whyWrong: New cable alone does not help, because the 100Base-TX switch still limits the network to 100 Mbps.
The existing adapters already support 1000Base-T, and the 100Base-TX switch would still limit the speed.
The existing CAT6 cable already supports 1000Base-T, so replacing it is not needed.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 186

stem: Ralph is a network consultant with a client who wants him to design the local area network (LAN) for his company's new branch office. The site consists of a building with unshielded twisted-pair (UTP) cable already installed, which the client considered a major selling point when selecting the property. He wants Ralph to install the fastest possible LAN using the existing cable. After examining the site, Ralph notes that the cable is Category 6 (CAT6), installed using a star/hub and spoke topology, and that the individual cable runs are all 90 to 100 meters long. Which of the following Ethernet Physical layer specifications can Ralph use for the new network to provide the fastest transmission speeds without replacing the cable?
explanation: 1000Base-T is the fastest 802.3 Ethernet specification that can run on 100-meter CAT6 UTP cables. 10GBase-T requires at least Category 6a (CAT6a) UTP cable for a 100-meter segment. 100Base-TX can use CAT6 cable, but it runs at one-tenth the speed of 1000Base-T. 1000Base-LX and 1000Base-SX are fiber-optic specifications that cannot run on CAT6 UTP or any copper cable.
whyWrong: 10GBase-T needs CAT6a or better cable for 100-meter segments.
100Base-TX runs on CAT6 but at only one-tenth the speed of 1000Base-T.
1000Base-LX is a fiber-optic standard and cannot run on UTP cable.
1000Base-SX is a fiber-optic standard and cannot run on UTP cable.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 187

stem: Which Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) 802.3 standards for Ethernet support 10-megabit-per-second (Mbps) communications, and what are the correct segment limitations for each standard? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: The three IEEE 10 Mbps standards for Ethernet are 10Base2, 10Base5, and 10Base-T. 10Base2 is limited to 185-meter segments; 10Base5 is limited to 500-meter segments; and 10Base-T is limited to 100-meter segments. The other options are not valid.
whyWrong: 10Base2 segments can be up to 185 meters, not 100 meters.
There is no 100Base5 standard; the 500-meter thick coaxial standard is 10Base5.
10Base-T segments are limited to 100 meters, which is about 328 feet, not 328 meters.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 188

stem: Which of the following are Ethernet cable types that must be configured in a bus topology? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: The first version of DIX Ethernet (Version 1) supported RG-8 thick coaxial cable in a bus topology. Version 2 added support for thin coaxial cable (RG-58) but was still limited to a bus topology. RG-10 and RG-14 are not Ethernet cable types.
whyWrong: RG-10 is not an Ethernet cable type.
RG-14 is not an Ethernet cable type.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 189

stem: Wavelength-division multiplexing is a fiber-optic technique for carrying multiple signals on a single network medium. There are several types of this technique, including coarse wavelength-division multiplexing (CWDM), dense wavelength-division multiplexing (DWDM), and bidirectional wavelength-division multiplexing (BWDM, or just WDM). Which of the following is not one of the ways in which these types of multiplexing differ?
options: They carry different numbers of channels on a single medium.
They provide different amounts of signal amplification.
explanation: The types of wavelength division multiplexing use different spacing of the wavelengths they carry, which enables them to fit different numbers of channels on a single medium. WDM (or BWDM) carries two wavelengths for bidirectional communication. CWDM can carry up to 16 channels, and DWDM 40 or 80 (depending on the spacing used). Various amplification technologies (including EFDA and Raman) can expand the amount of usable wavelength in each type.
whyWrong: Different wavelength spacing is one of the ways the WDM types differ.
Carrying different numbers of channels is one of the ways the WDM types differ.
Different amounts of signal amplification is listed by the book as one of the ways the WDM types differ.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 190
note: WDM is not named in N10-009; matched to 1.5 transceivers (wavelengths). The book's answer treats signal amplification as a difference between the WDM types, which is arguable.

stem: Ralph is installing an Ethernet local area network (LAN) for a small business with two offices on opposite sides of a courtyard. Ralph plans to run a multimode fiber-optic cable across the courtyard, but the budget is limited, and he cannot use fiber for the whole network. Therefore, he installs unshielded twisted-pair (UTP) cable in the two offices, which have 10 and 12 workstations, respectively. Which of the following devices should Ralph use to join the two UTP installations together into one LAN using the fiber-optic run across the courtyard, while keeping the cost to a minimum?
explanation: Media converters will enable Ralph to join the multimode fiber-optic run to the UTP at both sides of the courtyard while maintaining a single network at minimum cost. Inexpensive small-business hubs and switches cannot join different media together. Routers can join different media, but they are more expensive, and they would separate the installation into three separate networks.
whyWrong: Inexpensive hubs cannot join fiber-optic and UTP media together.
Inexpensive small-business switches cannot join fiber-optic and UTP media together.
Routers can join different media but cost more and would split the installation into separate networks.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 191

stem: Under which of the following conditions is a cable installer required to use plenum cable?
options: When cables run close to sources of electromagnetic interference (EMI)
When cables are running through building air flow spaces
When data and voice traffic will be running over the same cable
When cables are running through areas of low temperature
explanation: Plenum cable is a type of cable intended for use within building air spaces (called plenums) that has an outer sheath that is more resistant to high temperatures and does not produce toxic fumes when it burns. The use of plenum cable has no effect on EMI or the type of traffic on the cable, nor is it required for low temperature areas.
whyWrong: Plenum cable is about fire safety and has no effect on EMI.
Plenum cable has no effect on the type of traffic the cable carries.
Plenum cable is not required for low-temperature areas.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 192

stem: Which of the following wireless networking standards is capable of supporting speeds over 72 Mbps and is also backward compatible with IEEE 802.11b and 802.11g?
explanation: IEEE 802.11n and 802.11ax support transmission speeds over 72 Mbps, and they both run on the 2.4 GHz band, so they are backward compatible with 802.11b and 802.11g equipment. IEEE 802.11 and 802.11a cannot run at 72 Mbps, and 802.11a is not compatible with 802.11b and 802.11g because it only runs on the 5 GHz band. IEEE 802.11ac can run at speeds over 72 Mbps, but it only runs on the 5 GHz band, so it is not compatible with 802.11b and 802.11g.
whyWrong: The original IEEE 802.11 standard runs at only 1 or 2 Mbps.
IEEE 802.11a runs at no more than 54 Mbps and uses only the 5 GHz band.
IEEE 802.11ac uses only the 5 GHz band, so it is not compatible with 802.11b and 802.11g.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 193

stem: Which of the following is a cellular communication technology that is virtually obsolete in the United States?
explanation: Time-division multiple access (TDMA) is a communication technique that splits a frequency into multiple time slots, enabling it to carry multiple data streams. Commonly used in 2G cellular systems, TDMA is no longer used by the major US carriers in their 3G systems. Code-division multiple access (CDMA), Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM), and Long-Term Evolution (LTE) are alternative communications techniques that are currently used by the major US cellular carriers.
whyWrong: GSM is still used by major US cellular carriers.
CDMA is still used by major US cellular carriers.
LTE is the current 4G technology used by major US cellular carriers.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 194

stem: Ralph is planning a wireless LAN installation for a warehouse with two offices, one at either end of the building, approximately 300 feet apart. If he installs a single access point (AP) in the center of the warehouse, equidistant from the two offices, which of the following standards should he look for when purchasing hardware so that workstations in both offices will be able to connect to the network at the best possible speed?
explanation: Wireless networks using equipment based on the IEEE 802.11ax standard can span indoor distances of up to 820 feet at speeds up to 9.6 Gbps. An 802.11n network can span distances of up to 175 feet, which meets the requirement, but at much slower speeds of only 600 Mbps. An 802.11ac network can run at faster speeds—up to 1.3 Gbps—but it is limited to approximately 115-foot distances. Networks using 802.11g equipment can span 150 feet, but they run at a maximum of 54 Mbps. An 802.11a network cannot span more than 75 feet, and it runs at no more than 54 Mbps.
whyWrong: IEEE 802.11a reaches only about 75 feet indoors at no more than 54 Mbps.
IEEE 802.11g reaches about 150 feet but runs at no more than 54 Mbps.
IEEE 802.11n reaches the offices but runs at only up to 600 Mbps.
IEEE 802.11ac runs faster than 802.11n but does not reach as far or as fast as 802.11ax.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 195

stem: Which of the following broadband WAN services provides equal amounts of upstream and downstream bandwidth?
explanation: The word symmetric in symmetric digital subscriber line (SDSL) means that the service provides equal amounts of bandwidth in both directions. The asymmetric in asymmetric digital subscriber line (ADSL) means that the service provides more downstream bandwidth than upstream. Cable and satellite services are also asymmetric, providing more bandwidth downstream than upstream.
whyWrong: ADSL is asymmetric and gives more downstream than upstream bandwidth.
Satellite service is asymmetric and gives more downstream than upstream bandwidth.
Cable broadband service is asymmetric and gives more downstream than upstream bandwidth.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 196
note: DSL is not in N10-009; matched to 1.5 wired media because the question compares broadband media and cable speeds.

stem: Ralph's company has expanded to include an additional building on the far end of the corporate campus, approximately 4 kilometers away from the building housing the datacenter. A single-mode fiber-optic cable connection has been installed between the new building and the datacenter for a 1000Base-BX10 connection, but the cable is not yet connected to a transceiver at the datacenter end. Noticing that there is a 1000Base-SX Ethernet transceiver module in the datacenter storeroom, Ralph is wondering if he could use this on the new cable run. Which of the following are reasons why this might not work? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: The 1000Base-SX standard calls for multimode cable with a maximum length of approximately 500 meters, whereas the new cable run is 4,000 meters and uses single-mode cable. The 1000Base-SX transceiver will also be incompatible with the 1000Base-BX10 transceiver at the other end. 1000Base-BX10 uses wavelengths from 1,300 to 1,600 nanometers (nm), whereas 1000Base-SX uses wavelengths of 770 to 860 nm.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 197

stem: A Small Form-factor Pluggable (SFP) Ethernet implementation uses direct-attach copper (DAC) connections for short distance runs within the datacenter. Which of the following cable types do the DAC connections use?
explanation: Direct-attach copper (DAC) connections use twinaxial cable, which has two conductors instead of the one used in coaxial cables. DAC connections also do not use twisted-pair cables, either shielded or unshielded, or fiber-optic cables.
whyWrong: DAC connections do not use unshielded twisted-pair cable.
DAC connections do not use shielded twisted-pair cable.
DAC connections are copper, so they do not use fiber-optic cable.
Coaxial cable has one center conductor, while DAC cable is twinaxial with two.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 198

stem: An electrician installing a new light fixture accidentally severs one of the LAN cables running through the dropped ceiling space. With which topology would the severed cable cause the greatest amount of disturbance to the network?
explanation: A cable break in a bus topology would split the network into two halves, preventing the nodes on one side of the break from communicating with those on the other. In addition, both halves of the network would be left with one unterminated end, which would prevent the computers on each side of the break from communicating effectively. A cable break in a star/hub and spoke or logical ring topology would only interrupt the connection of a single computer to the network. The mesh topology is not often used for LANs, but redundant network connections are a characteristic of mesh networks, which means that a single cable break would have no effect on the network.
whyWrong: In a star topology, a cable break disconnects only the one computer on that cable.
In a logical ring, a cable break interrupts only the connection of one computer.
A mesh topology has redundant paths, so a single cable break has no effect.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 199
note: The bus topology is not in N10-009; matched to 1.6 star/hub and spoke, the topology the question compares it with.

stem: Which of the following statements about a wired local area network (LAN) is true?
options: Wired LANs support only the star/hub and spoke topology.
Wired LANs support only the star/hub and spoke and bus topologies.
Wired LANs support only the star/hub and spoke and ring topologies.
Wired LANs can support ring, bus, or star/hub and spoke topologies.
explanation: A wired LAN is a group of computers within a small area, connected by a common network medium. A wired LAN can be configured using a ring, bus, or star/hub and spoke topology.
whyWrong: Wired LANs can also use bus and ring topologies.
Wired LANs can also use a ring topology.
Wired LANs can also use a bus topology.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 200
note: Bus and ring topologies are not in N10-009; matched to 1.6 star/hub and spoke.

stem: Which of the following is an example of a hybrid LAN topology?
options: A workstation with two network interface cards, one of which is connected to a star/hub and spoke network and one to a bus network
Four Ethernet switches connected using a bus topology
Four workstations, each with a separate network connection to each of the other three
Four Ethernet switches, each with a separate network connection to each of the other three
explanation: A hybrid LAN topology is a network that uses two or more of the basic topologies, connected together so that each workstation can communicate with all of the other workstations. Connecting four switches to a bus topology combines four star/hub and spoke networks in such a way that the workstations are all interconnected. Connecting a single workstation to a star/hub and spoke and a bus network enables that workstation to access both networks, but it does not enable other workstations to access both topologies. Four workstations, each with a separate connection to the other three, is a mesh network topology, not a hybrid. Four connected switches expands the star/hub and spoke topology, but it does not create a hybrid topology.
whyWrong: One workstation with two network cards does not join the two networks into one hybrid topology.
Workstations each connected to every other workstation form a mesh topology.
Switches each connected to every other switch form a mesh topology, not a hybrid.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 201

stem: Which type of network connects local area networks (LANs) in distant locations?
explanation: WANs (wide area networks) connect LANs that are geographically distant. A LAN (local area network), as the name implies, is a group of computers, not other LANs, and it is contained within a small area. MANs (metropolitan area networks) connect LANs in a single metropolitan area; they are not confined to a small area. A MAN is typically larger than a LAN but smaller than a WAN. A campus area network (CAN) typically includes a group of adjacent buildings, such as those of a corporation or university.
whyWrong: A LAN is a group of computers in a small area and does not connect distant LANs.
A MAN connects LANs within one metropolitan area, not distant locations.
A CAN connects networks in a group of adjacent buildings, such as a campus.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 202
note: LAN/MAN/WAN/CAN network types are not listed in N10-009; matched to 1.6 point to point (links between distant LANs).

stem: Which of the following topologies is used by the majority of new Ethernet networks installed today?
explanation: Virtually all of the new Ethernet networks installed today use the star/hub and spoke topology, with one or more switches functioning as a cabling nexus. Ethernet no longer uses the bus topology, and it does not support point-to-point or mesh topologies.
whyWrong: Ethernet no longer uses the bus topology.
Point to point is not the topology used to connect the devices of a new Ethernet LAN.
Ethernet LANs do not use a mesh topology to connect their devices.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 203

stem: Alice has constructed a five-node failover cluster in which all five servers are connected to a hard disk array using a dedicated Fibre Channel network. Which of the following terms describes this network arrangement?
explanation: A storage area network (SAN) is a network that is dedicated to carrying traffic between servers and storage devices. A personal area network (PAN) provides communication among devices associated with a single person, such as smartphones. A wide area network (WAN) is a network that connects devices or networks at different geographic locations. A metropolitan area network (MAN) is a type of WAN that connects devices within a limited geographic area.
whyWrong: A PAN connects the devices of one person, such as a smartphone and headset.
A WAN connects networks at different geographic locations.
A MAN connects networks within one metropolitan area.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 204

stem: On an Ethernet network using the star/hub and spoke topology, which of the following devices can function as the cabling nexus that forms the figurative center of the star?
explanation: A switch can function as the cabling nexus at the center of an Ethernet star/hub and spoke topology. Each of the devices on the network is connected by a cable to the switch. Routers are used to connect networks to each other; they cannot function as the center of a star/hub and spoke topology. Firewalls are not cabling devices, and access points are used on wireless networks.
whyWrong: A firewall filters traffic and is not a cabling device.
A router connects networks to each other and is not the center of a star.
An access point connects wireless devices and is not the cabling center of a wired star.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 206

stem: Which of the following cabling topologies provides the greatest number of redundant paths through the network?
explanation: A mesh topology is one in which every node is directly connected to every other node, thus providing complete redundancy through the network. In a star/hub and spoke topology, each node is connected to a central nexus, providing each with a single path to the rest of the network. In a ring topology, each node is connected to two other nodes, providing two possible paths through the network. In a bus topology, nodes are chained together in a line, providing no redundancy.
whyWrong: A star topology gives each node a single path through the central device.
A ring topology gives each node only two possible paths.
A bus topology chains nodes in a line and gives no redundancy.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 207

stem: Which of the following Ethernet Physical layer options does not use the star/hub and spoke topology?
explanation: 10Base2 is the Physical layer specification for Thin Ethernet, which uses coaxial cable in a bus topology. 10Base-T, 100Base-TX, and 1000Base-T all use twisted-pair cable in a star/hub and spoke topology.
whyWrong: 10Base-T uses twisted-pair cable in a star/hub and spoke topology.
100Base-TX uses twisted-pair cable in a star/hub and spoke topology.
1000Base-T uses twisted-pair cable in a star/hub and spoke topology.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 208
note: Matched to 1.6 star/hub and spoke; 10Base2 bus is a legacy topology not in N10-009.

stem: Which of the following statements is true about the differences between a peer-to-peer network and a client-server network?
options: Peer-to-peer networks are inherently less secure than client-server networks.
Peer-to-peer networks are illegal, while client-server networks are legal.
On peer-to-peer networks, every workstation is capable of authenticating users.
On a peer-to-peer network, all workstations must share their resources.
explanation: A peer-to-peer network calls for each workstation to maintain accounts for authenticating users that access their shared resources. On a client-server network, authentication is centralized. Peer-to-peer networks can be more difficult to administer than client-server networks, but they are not inherently less secure. Peer networks sharing copyrighted content on the Internet are illegal, but it is not illegal to share private resources on a peer-to-peer network. Workstations on a peer-to-peer network are not required to share their resources, but they are capable of it.
whyWrong: Peer-to-peer networks can be harder to manage, but they are not inherently less secure.
Peer-to-peer networks are legal; only sharing copyrighted content is illegal.
Workstations on a peer-to-peer network can share resources but are not required to.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 209
note: Peer-to-peer and client-server networks are not in N10-009; matched to the closest 1.6 architecture topic.

stem: Ed has been hired by a private company to connect two remote sites with a wide area network (WAN). Each of these sites has more than 200 users, and they all need to constantly transfer files across the WAN. One of the sites has a customer database that is accessed by both sites at all hours of the day. Access to the database and other information is time sensitive and constant. The company estimates that their aggregate bandwidth needs to be approximately 40 Mbps. Management says that they need to guarantee access to this information and that money is not a factor in the WAN implementation. Which WAN technology should Ed recommend for this scenario?
options: An ADSL (asymmetrical digital subscriber line) connection
explanation: For this scenario, the best of the options given is a dedicated leased line connection. This is because the bandwidth requirements are constant and the data transfer rates are high. To support the 40 Mbps data rate, Ed should recommend a T-3 dedicated leased line, running at 44.735 Mbps. Standard modem connections, CATV, and ADSL connections are all too slow.
whyWrong: A modem-to-modem connection is far too slow for a constant 40 Mbps need.
A CATV connection is too slow and does not guarantee the bandwidth the company needs.
An ADSL connection is too slow, and its upstream bandwidth is lower than its downstream bandwidth.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 210
note: Leased lines (T-3) are not in N10-009; matched to 1.6 point to point.

stem: Ralph is an employee of a company that offers the option to telecommute from home. As a telecommuting employee, he needs to connect to the company network to access client information, transfer files, and send email through a virtual private network (VPN) connection. Ralph is investigating the different wide area network (WAN) services available for the remote connection before he implements one. His home is over 30 years old; the existing telephone wiring was not run through conduit, and the wiring seems to be deteriorating. Ralph has cable television (CATV) service, and his home is also approximately 20,000 feet from the nearest telephone central office. He wants to implement the fastest remote connection service possible, but cost is a factor in the decision. Which WAN technology should Ralph implement?
explanation: In this scenario, the best solution is for Ralph to use his existing CATV service for the remote connection. CATV offers faster data rates than standard modem-to-modem service and supports VPN connections. A dedicated fractional T-1 line is expensive and is not typically used for remote user connections. Since Ralph's telephone lines are not run through conduit and the distance to the central office is more than 18,000 feet, he probably cannot use DSL technology, because it requires good-quality lines and close proximity to a central office.
whyWrong: A fractional T-1 leased line is expensive and is not typically used for remote user connections.
A modem-to-modem connection is much slower than broadband service.
DSL needs good telephone wiring and a location within about 18,000 feet of the central office.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 211
note: WAN services (CATV, DSL, T-1) are not in N10-009; matched to 1.5 wired media (coaxial cable).

stem: Which two of the following constructs provide roughly the same function? (Choose two that apply.)
explanation: A Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) trunk provides a connection between the private and public domains of a unified communications network. A Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) gateway provides a connection between an IP network and the public switched telephone network (PSTN). Both of these provide a conduit between a subscriber's private network and the network furnished by a service provider. A channel service unit/data service unit (CSU/DSU) is a device that provides a router on a private network with access to a leased line. A smartjack provides signal conversion, diagnostic testing, and other capabilities to leased line subscribers. A virtual private network (VPN) concentrator is a type of router that enables multiple client systems to access a network from remote locations.
whyWrong: A CSU/DSU gives a router on a private network access to a leased line.
A smartjack provides signal conversion and diagnostic testing for leased line subscribers.
A VPN concentrator lets many remote clients connect securely to a network.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 212
note: SIP trunks and VoIP gateways are not named in N10-009; matched to the 1.4 ports and protocols table (SIP).

stem: Which of the following wide area network (WAN) services typically uses a switched fabric that was called a cloud long before the term came into general use?
explanation: Frame Relay is a packet switching service that uses a single leased line to replace multiple leased lines by multiplexing traffic through a cloud. Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) uses a switched fabric, but it is not referred to as a cloud. A fractional T-1 is part of a leased line that connects two points, so there is no switching involved and no cloud. SONET is a Physical layer standard that defines fiber-optic connections; it does not call for switching or use the term cloud .
whyWrong: ATM uses a switched fabric, but that fabric is not called a cloud.
A fractional T-1 is part of a leased line between two points, with no switching and no cloud.
SONET is a Physical layer standard for fiber-optic connections that does not use switching or a cloud.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 213
note: Frame Relay, ATM, and SONET are not in N10-009; matched to 1.6 point to point (WAN links).

stem: Ralph has been contracted to consult for a company that wants to update its legacy Ethernet network to Gigabit Ethernet. When examining the site, he discovers that the network is still using coaxial-based Thin Ethernet. What change in network topology must occur to upgrade the existing network to Gigabit Ethernet using unshielded twisted-pair (UTP) cable?
explanation: All coaxial-based Ethernet networks, including Thin Ethernet, use a bus topology. All UTP-based Gigabit Ethernet networks use a star/hub and spoke topology. Therefore, an upgrade from coaxial to UTP cable must include a change in topology from bus to star/hub and spoke. Ethernet networks never use a mesh topology.
whyWrong: Ethernet networks do not use a mesh topology, and UTP Gigabit Ethernet uses a star.
The existing Thin Ethernet network uses a bus, not a mesh.
The existing network is a bus, and UTP Gigabit Ethernet does not use a bus.
The existing network is a bus, and Ethernet networks do not use a mesh topology.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 214

stem: Which of the following BEST describes the function of a vSwitch (or virtual switch)?
options: A vSwitch is a software product that enables a computer with multiple network adapters to function as a switch.
A vSwitch is a feature in layer 3 switches that enables VLANs on the same switch to communicate with each other.
A vSwitch is a feature in layer 3 switches that enables VLANs on different switches to communicate with each other.
A vSwitch enables virtual machines (VMs) running on the same hypervisor to communicate with each other internally.
explanation: In most virtualization products, when you create multiple virtual machines on one host computer, they can communicate with each other internally using a built-in virtual switching capability. A computer with multiple network adapters can function as a router, but not as a switch. Layer 3 switches can provide virtual routers that connect VLANs together, but not virtual switches. The function that enables VLANs on different switches to communicate is called trunking, not virtual switching.
whyWrong: A computer with multiple network adapters can function as a router, but not as a switch.
Communication between VLANs on one switch is routing in a layer 3 switch, not a vSwitch.
Communication between VLANs on different switches uses trunking, not a vSwitch.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 215

stem: On which of the following virtual networking components can you create VLANs?
explanation: You can create virtual local area networks (VLANs) on a virtual switch, just as you can create them on many physical switches. In most cases, virtual components function just like their physical counterparts. Virtual NICs are components of virtual machines and therefore do not provide functions spanning entire networks. Virtual routers function at the Network layer and virtual firewalls at the Application layer, so neither of these can host VLANs, which operate at the Data link layer.
whyWrong: A virtual NIC is part of one virtual machine and cannot host VLANs.
A virtual router works at the Network layer and cannot host VLANs, which work at the Data link layer.
A virtual firewall filters traffic and cannot host VLANs, which work at the Data link layer.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 216

stem: Which of the following components is responsible for providing a virtualized hardware environment and running virtual machines?
explanation: The hypervisor is the hardware or software component responsible for managing virtual machines and providing the virtualized hardware environment on which they run. Virtual servers and virtual switches are components that are part of the virtual network infrastructure enabled by the hypervisor. A virtual private network (VPN) concentrator is a type of router that enables multiple remote clients to connect to a network; it has nothing to do with virtual networking.
whyWrong: A virtual server is a virtual machine that runs on the hypervisor.
A vSwitch connects virtual machines and is part of the infrastructure that the hypervisor provides.
A VPN concentrator lets many remote clients connect to a network and has nothing to do with virtualization.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 217

stem: Which of the following is the proper term for a computer with a hypervisor on which you can create virtual machines and other virtual components?
explanation: A computer with a hypervisor, on which you can create virtual machines, is referred to as a host. The virtual machines themselves are called guests. Network-attached storage (NAS) refers to a device containing shared drives that is connected to a network. A storage area network (SAN) is a separate network dedicated to shared storage devices.
whyWrong: A guest is a virtual machine that runs on the host.
NAS is a device with shared drives that is connected to a network.
A SAN is a separate network dedicated to shared storage devices.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 218

stem: In which of the following components can a virtual firewall be implemented?
explanation: A virtual firewall is a service or appliance that performs the same functions as a physical network firewall: packet filtering and monitoring. In a virtual environment, firewalls can take the form of software components installed on a guest virtual machine or a hypervisor host system. A firewall can also be incorporated into a virtual switch.
whyWrong: A host operating system is a valid place, but so are all the other options.
A guest operating system is a valid place, but so are all the other options.
A dedicated virtual machine is a valid place, but so are all the other options.
A virtual switch is a valid place, but so are all the other options.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 219

stem: Which of the following is not a protocol that uses tunneling to establish secured links between TCP/IP systems?
explanation: Network address translation (NAT) enables workstations on private networks to access the Internet by substituting a public IP address in packets generated with private addresses. Layer 2 Tunneling Protocol (L2TP), IPsec, and Multipoint Generic Routing Encapsulation (MGRE) are all protocols that encapsulate packets in an encrypted form within another protocol to secure the contents.
whyWrong: L2TP is a tunneling protocol that encapsulates packets inside another protocol.
IPsec can create secure tunnels between TCP/IP systems.
MGRE is a tunneling protocol that encapsulates packets inside another protocol.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 220

stem: Which of the following is not the name of one of the layers in the three-tier datacenter architecture?
explanation: The three-tier hierarchical architecture for datacenters consists of core, distribution, and access layers. The access layer in a datacenter contains servers; the distribution layer contains redundant switch connections; and the core layer provides high-speed transport between the switches. There is no intermediate layer in the architecture.
whyWrong: The core layer provides high-speed transport between switches in the three-tier model.
The distribution layer contains the redundant switch connections in the three-tier model.
The access layer contains the servers and end devices in the three-tier model.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 221

stem: Which of the following is not a reason why the spine and leaf datacenter topology is superior to the standard three-tier topology?
options: The spine and leaf arrangement uses a full mesh switching topology.
In a spine and leaf topology, all data flows require the same number of hops.
The spine and leaf topology is less expensive to implement than the three-tier topology.
The spine and leaf topology uses software-defined networking to direct traffic, rather than blocking ports using the spanning tree protocol.
explanation: The spine and leaf topology uses a full mesh topology in its two layers of switches. This is more expensive than the three-tier topology, but it reduces latency by requiring the same number of hops in the path between any two routers. The use of software-defined networking provides adaptive path determination without the use of the Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) for layer 2 port blocking.
whyWrong: The full mesh between spine and leaf switches is one of its advantages.
Equal hop counts between any two devices are one of its advantages because they reduce latency.
Using SDN instead of spanning tree port blocking is one of its advantages.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 222

stem: Which of the following BEST describes the difference between east-west and north-south traffic in a datacenter?
options: East-west describes traffic between devices at the same layer of the OSI model, while north-south describes traffic between OSI model layers.
East-west is switch-to-switch traffic, while north-south is switch-to-router traffic.
East-west traffic stays within the datacenter, while north-south traffic does not.
East-west is backbone traffic among switches and routers, while north-south is traffic to end systems, such as servers.
explanation: East-west traffic describes traffic flow within the datacenter, while north-south is traffic between devices inside the datacenter and outside devices. The terms east-west and north-south do not pertain to the OSI model layers or to specific devices used.
whyWrong: East-west and north-south do not describe OSI model layers.
East-west and north-south do not describe the types of devices that exchange the traffic.
North-south traffic goes in and out of the datacenter, not just to end systems such as servers.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 223

stem: Top-of-rack switches most commonly form which layer of the datacenter topology?
explanation: In a typical datacenter topology, racks contain servers that implement applications. A leaf switch at the top of the rack connects the servers in the rack together and also connects to a spine switch that links to the rest of the datacenter. The top-of-rack switches are not classified as backbone, spine, or core devices.
whyWrong: Backbone is not the name of a layer in the spine and leaf topology.
Spine switches connect the leaf switches together and are not at the top of each rack.
The core is a layer of the three-tier model, not the switch at the top of a rack.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 224

stem: Which of the following statements about switches is not true?
options: Switches are Data link layer devices that connect network devices in a star/hub and spoke topology.
Switches amplify and repeat signals received through one port out all other ports regardless of the destination.
Switches use MAC addresses to identify the devices connected to specific ports.
Switches provide internal crossover circuits and use uplink ports to form a hierarchical star/hub and spoke topology.
explanation: Switches are Data link layer devices that amplify and repeat incoming signals only through the port for which the data is destined, not through all ports. Switches are used to physically connect end systems to a star/hub and spoke topology. Switches typically provide an internal crossover circuit connection. Uplink ports are sometimes used to extend the distance of a star/hub and spoke network, forming a hierarchical star.
whyWrong: This is true because switches are Data link layer devices at the center of a star.
This is true because switches learn MAC addresses to forward frames to the right port.
This is true because switches have internal crossover circuits and uplink ports.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 225

stem: A collapsed core network is one in which the standard three-tier hierarchical model is compressed into two tiers. Which of the following two tiers are combined to form this architectural model?
explanation: In a collapsed core network, the core and distribution layers are combined, creating a simpler design that is less expensive to implement. A collapsed core network does not combine the distribution and access tiers or the core and access tiers. There is no intermediate tier in the three-tier hierarchical model.
whyWrong: A collapsed core does not combine the distribution and access tiers.
A collapsed core does not combine the core and access tiers.
There is no intermediate tier in the three-tier hierarchical model.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 226

stem: Which of the following is the most accurate description of the subnetting process on an IPv4 network?
options: You extend the IP address by adding bits for a subnet identifier.
You borrow bits from the network identifier to create a subnet identifier.
You borrow bits from the host identifier to create a subnet identifier.
You create a subnet identifier by borrowing half of the bits from the network identifier and half from the host identifier.
explanation: You cannot extend the IPv4 address beyond its 32-bit size, and you cannot remove bits from the network identifier, or the packets will not be routed properly. You must therefore create a subnet by borrowing bits from the host identifier.
whyWrong: An IPv4 address cannot be extended beyond its 32 bits.
Removing bits from the network identifier would break the routing of packets.
Subnet bits come only from the host identifier, not half from each identifier.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 228

stem: Which of the following IPv4 addresses are you unable to assign to a network host? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: IPv4 addresses with first byte values from 224 to 239 are Class D addresses, which are reserved for use as multicast addresses. Therefore, you cannot assign 229.6.87.3 to a host. 103.256.77.4 is an invalid address because the value 256 cannot be represented by an 8-bit binary value. The other options, 1.1.1.1 and 9.34.0.1, are both valid IPv4 addresses.
whyWrong: 1.1.1.1 is a valid Class A address that can be assigned to a host.
9.34.0.1 is a valid Class A address that can be assigned to a host.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 229

stem: How many bits are allocated to the host identifier in an IPv4 address on the 10.72.0.0/17 network?
explanation: The value after the slash in a Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) address specifies the number of bits in the network identifier. An IPv4 address has 32 bits, so if 17 bits are allocated to the network identifier, 15 bits are left for the host identifier.
whyWrong: 8 host bits would be a /24 network, not /17.
16 host bits would be a /16 network, not /17.
17 is the number of network bits, not host bits.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 230

stem: Which of the following are not valid IPv4 addresses in the private address space defined by RFC 1918? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: RFC 1918 defines the private address space as the following ranges: 10.0.0.0–10.255.255.255, 172.16.0.0–172.31.255.255, and 192.168.0.0–192.168.255.255. 172:33:19:7 and 172.15.2.9 both fall outside the specified private Class B range, and therefore are not valid private addresses.
whyWrong: 10.255.255.255 is within the private range 10.0.0.0 to 10.255.255.255.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 231

stem: Alice has been instructed to create an IPv4 network with 8 subnets and 30 hosts per subnet. She has been assigned a Class C network address. Which of the following subnet masks will she have to use?
explanation: To create a network with 8 subnets and 30 hosts per subnet, Alice would have to allocate 3 of the 8 bits in the last octet for subnet identifiers. This would result in a binary value of 11100000 for the last octet in the subnet mask, which converts to a decimal value of 224.
whyWrong: A /25 mask gives only 2 subnets from a Class C network.
A /26 mask gives only 4 subnets from a Class C network.
A /28 mask gives 16 subnets but only 14 hosts per subnet.
A /29 mask gives only 6 hosts per subnet.
A /30 mask gives only 2 hosts per subnet.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 232

stem: Which of the following is the default subnet mask for an IPv4 Class A network?
explanation: A Class A address uses only the first octet as the network identifier, which yields a binary subnet mask of 11111111 00000000 00000000 00000000. In decimal form, the subnet mask is 255.0.0.0. The 255.255.0.0 mask is for Class B addresses, and 255.255.255.0 is for Class C addresses. 255.255.255.255 is the broadcast address for the current network.
whyWrong: 255.255.0.0 is the default mask for a Class B network.
255.255.255.0 is the default mask for a Class C network.
255.255.255.255 is the broadcast address for the current network, not a default mask.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 233

stem: Which of the following is the range of IPv4 addresses that Automatic Private IP Addressing (APIPA) assigns to DHCP clients that cannot access a DHCP server?
explanation: According to RFC 3927, when a DHCP client cannot access a DHCP server, APIPA assigns it an address on the 169.254/16 network, the range of addresses for which is 169.254.0.0 to 169.254.255.255. An address in this range lets the client talk only to other hosts on the same local link, so it usually means the DHCP server could not be reached.
whyWrong: The 10.0.0.0 range is RFC 1918 private address space, not APIPA.
The 192.168.0.0 range is RFC 1918 private address space, not APIPA.
The 224.0.0.0 range is Class D multicast address space.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 234

stem: In which IPv4 class is the address 127.0.0.1 found?
explanation: Address 127.0.0.1 is the designated IPv4 local loopback address, and as such, it is reserved. It falls between Class A, which has first octet values from 1 to 126, and Class B, which has first octet values of 128 to 191.
whyWrong: The book treats the 127 range as reserved for loopback and outside the Class A range of 1 to 126.
Class B addresses have first octet values from 128 to 191.
Class C addresses have first octet values from 192 to 223.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 235
note: Many references place 127.0.0.0/8 inside the Class A range (0–127) and reserve it for loopback; the book's answer, None of the above, treats it as outside every class.

stem: To which class does the following IPv4 address belong: 190.126.14.251?
explanation: All Class B addresses have first octet values between 128 and 191. The first octet range of a Class A address is 1 to 126, and the Class C first octet range is 192 to 223. Class D addresses have a first octet range of 224 to 239. Class E addresses have a first octet range of 240 to 255.
whyWrong: Class A addresses have first octet values from 1 to 126.
Class C addresses have first octet values from 192 to 223.
Class D addresses have first octet values from 224 to 239.
Class E addresses have first octet values from 240 to 255.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 236

stem: Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) is a standard for IPv4 addressing that includes the capability to create subnets using any number of IP address bits, rather than using 8-bit blocks. Which of the following terms describes this ability?
explanation: Variable-length subnet masking (VLSM) describes the process of subnetting an IPv4 network address by assigning an arbitrary number of host bits as subnet bits, providing administrators with great flexibility over the number of subnets created and the number of hosts in each subnet. Automatic Private IP Addressing (APIPA) is the process by which a DHCP client assigns itself an IP address when no DHCP servers are accessible. Virtual local area networks (VLANs) are logical structures used to create separate broadcast domains on a large, switched network. Extended Unique Identifier-64 (EUI-64) is an addressing method used to create IPv6 link local addresses out of media access control (MAC) addresses.
whyWrong: APIPA assigns 169.254.x.x addresses when a DHCP server cannot be reached.
A VLAN is a logical layer 2 network on a switch, not a subnetting method.
EUI-64 creates an IPv6 interface identifier from a MAC address.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 237

stem: Ralph has been instructed to use the network address 10.12.0.0/14 for the new network he is installing. What subnet mask value should he use when configuring his computers?
explanation: The 14-bit prefix indicated in the network address will result in a mask with 14 ones followed by 18 zeroes. Broken into 8-bit blocks, the binary mask value is as follows: 11111111 11111100 00000000 00000000. Converted into decimal values, this results in a subnet mask value of 255.252.0.0.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 238

stem: Ed has been hired to design a company's network. The company has an assigned Class C network address of 192.168.30.0. Ed's client wants the network to be configured with 10 subnets, each with 14 hosts. Is this configuration possible with the given address, and if so, how many subnets and hosts can Ed create on the network?
options: Yes, this will work. By using 4 subnet bits, it is possible for Ed to create up to 16 subnets. He can then use the remaining 4 host bits to create 14 hosts on each subnet.
No, this will not work. A Class C address cannot be subnetted to create 8 subnets.
No, this will not work. Although there are sufficient bits available to create 10 subnets, there are not enough bits left over for Ed to create 14 hosts per subnet.
Yes, this will work. Ed can create 10 subnets with 14 hosts per subnet. By using 3 subnet bits, he can create 10 subnets, which leaves 5 bits to create up to 30 hosts per subnet.
explanation: In this scenario, the company has a Class C Internet Protocol (IPv4) address, which consists of 24 network bits and 8 host bits. The company wants 10 subnets and 14 hosts per subnet, so Ed must subdivide the 8 host bits into subnet and host bits. He can allocate 4 of the 8 host bits for subnets, enabling him to create up to 16 subnets. This leaves 4 bits for host addresses, enabling Ed to create 14 hosts per subnet.
whyWrong: A Class C address can be subnetted into 8 or more subnets by borrowing 3 or more host bits.
Borrowing 4 subnet bits still leaves 4 host bits, which gives exactly 14 hosts per subnet.
3 subnet bits give only 8 subnets, which is fewer than the 10 needed.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 239

stem: What is the greatest number of subnets you can create with a Class A IPv4 address if you use a 14-bit subnet identifier?
explanation: The formula for calculating the number of subnets you can create using a subnet identifier of a given length is 2^x, where x is the number of bits in the subnet identifier. Therefore, with a 14-bit subnet, you can conceivably create 2^14, or 16,384, subnets.
whyWrong: 256 subnets need only 8 subnet bits.
1,022 is 2 to the 10th power minus 2, which does not match a 14-bit subnet identifier.
1,024 subnets come from a 10-bit subnet identifier.
16,382 subtracts 2, which is not needed when counting subnets with this formula.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 240

stem: Alice has been asked to design her company's Internet Protocol (IPv4) addressing scheme. The company has been assigned a Class C network address of 192.168.30.0. Alice's director wants 4 subnets with 28 hosts per subnet. How many bits are required for subnets? How many bits are required for hosts? What will the new subnet mask be for this network?
options: 3 subnet bits, 5 host bits, and subnet mask 255.255.255.240
4 subnet bits, 3 host bits, and subnet mask 255.255.255.248
3 subnet bits, 5 host bits, and subnet mask 255.255.255.224
5 subnet bits, 3 host bits, and subnet mask 255.255.255.192
explanation: In this scenario, the last byte of the IP address assigned to the company must be subdivided into 3 subnet bits and 5 host bits. The 3 subnet bits will give Alice up to 8 subnets, with 5 host bits for up to 30 hosts per subnet. The new subnet mask is 255.255.255.224. The 224 is the decimal equivalent of the binary value 11100000, which represents the 3 subnet bits and the 5 host bits.
whyWrong: 255.255.255.240 has 4 subnet bits, not 3.
4 subnet bits and 3 host bits add up to only 7 bits, and 3 host bits allow only 6 hosts.
5 subnet bits leave only 3 host bits, and 255.255.255.192 has only 2 subnet bits.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 241

stem: The default mask for an IPv4 Class B network is 255.255.0.0. How many subnet bits do you need to create 600 subnets with 55 hosts per subnet, and what is the new subnet mask for the network?
options: 10 subnet bits with a subnet mask of 255.255.255.192
9 subnet bits with a subnet mask of 255.255.255.128
10 subnet bits with a subnet mask of 255.255.224.0
11 subnet bits with a subnet mask of 255.255.255.192
explanation: A standard Class B address with a mask of 255.255.0.0 has 16 bits that can be used for subnets and hosts. To get 600 subnets, you must use 10 of the available bits, which gives you up to 1024 subnets. This leaves 6 host bits, which gives you up to 62 hosts per subnet, which exceeds the requirement of 55 requested by the client. Using 9 bits would give you only 510 subnets, while 11 bits would give you 2046 subnets but leave you only 5 bits for a maximum of 30 hosts, which is not enough.
whyWrong: 9 subnet bits give only 512 subnets, which is fewer than the 600 needed.
255.255.224.0 has only 3 subnet bits, not 10.
11 subnet bits leave only 5 host bits for 30 hosts, which is fewer than the 55 needed.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 242

stem: What is the greatest number of host addresses you can create on a single subnet of a network with the following address: 172.16.0.0/20?
explanation: The formula for calculating the number of hosts you can create using a host identifier of a given length is 2^x – 2, where x is the number of bits in the host identifier. You cannot create a host with an address of all zeroes or all ones, which is why you subtract 2. On a network that uses 20 bits for network identification, 12 bits are left for the host identifier. Using those 12 bits, you can create 2^12 – 2 or 4,094 host addresses.
whyWrong: 142 is not a result of the 2 to the x minus 2 formula for 12 host bits.
144 is not a result of the 2 to the x minus 2 formula for 12 host bits.
4,096 includes the network and broadcast addresses, which cannot be assigned to hosts.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 243

stem: Ralph has an IPv4 Class B network with a subnet mask of 255.255.248.0. How many subnets can he create, and how many hosts can he create per subnet?
explanation: With a Class B subnet mask of 255.255.248.0, the binary form of the third and fourth bytes is 11111000 00000000. There are 5 subnet bits, providing up to 32 subnets and 11 host bits, providing up to 2,046 hosts.
whyWrong: 255.255.248.0 on a Class B network gives 5 subnet bits for 32 subnets, not 64.
30 subnets and 1,022 hosts match 5 subnet bits with only 10 host bits, which is not this mask.
62 subnets and 1,022 hosts match a 255.255.252.0 mask.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 244

stem: Convert the binary mask 11111111.11111111.11100000.00000000 into its equivalent decimal value. What is the decimal representation of this mask?
explanation: The decimal value for 11111111 is 255, the value for 11100000 is 224, and the value for 00000000 is 0, so the mask is 255.255.224.0. Each octet is converted on its own by adding the place values (128, 64, 32, and so on) of the bits that are set to 1.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 245

stem: If you have an IPv4 network address of 192.168.1.32/27, what is the valid range of host addresses you can use for your workstations?
explanation: With a network address of 192.168.1.32 and 27 mask bits, the subnet mask value is 11111111.11111111.11111111.11100000 in binary form, or 255.255.255.224 in decimal form. This leaves 5 bits for the host identifier. The valid range of host bits is therefore 00001 (1) through 11110 (30). This gives you a range of 192.168.1.32 + 1 (33) through 192.168.1.32 + 30 (62).
whyWrong: 192.168.1.63 is the broadcast address of this subnet and cannot be assigned to a host.
192.168.1.33 is the first valid host address, so the range does not start at .34.
The range starts at 192.168.1.33, and 192.168.1.63 is the broadcast address.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 246

stem: Alice has been assigned the IPv4 network address 172.21.0.0/22 for the creation of a new department network in her company. How many host addresses does she have available to her?
explanation: To calculate the number of host addresses available, Alice must determine the number of host bits in the address, which is 10, raise 2 to that power, and subtract 2 for the network and broadcast addresses, which are unusable for hosts. The formula is therefore 2^x – 2. 2^10 – 2 = 1,022.
whyWrong: 510 is the host count for a /23 network with 9 host bits.
512 is 2 to the 9th power and also does not subtract the network and broadcast addresses.
1,024 does not subtract the network and broadcast addresses.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 247

stem: Automatic Private IP Addressing (APIPA) assigns IPv4 addresses from which of the following classes to Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) clients that cannot contact a DHCP server?
explanation: When a DHCP client cannot access a DHCP server, APIPA assigns it a Class B address using the network address 169.254/16, which yields the address range 169.254.0.0 to 169.254.255.255. The first octet, 169, falls in the Class B range of 128 to 191.
whyWrong: APIPA addresses begin with 169, which is not in the Class A range of 1 to 126.
APIPA addresses begin with 169, which is not in the Class C range of 192 to 223.
Class D addresses, 224 to 239, are reserved for multicast and are never assigned by APIPA.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 248

stem: Which of the following Internet Protocol (IPv4) address classes identifies multicast addresses?
explanation: Class D addresses are used for multicast transmissions. Class A, Class B, and Class C addresses are used for unicast transmissions. Class E is for experimental use only.
whyWrong: Class A addresses are used for unicast transmissions.
Class B addresses are used for unicast transmissions.
Class C addresses are used for unicast transmissions.
Class E addresses are reserved for experimental use.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 1: Networking Concepts, Review Questions question 249

stem: Which of the following is an address that you can assign to a host on a private IPv4 network?
explanation: The address 10.1.0.253 is a proper address in the private address range 10.0.0.0 to 10.255.255.255. The address 192.167.9.46 falls outside the designated private IP address range, which is 192.168.0.0 to 192.168.255.255, and is therefore not a viable address on a private network. 172.16.255.255 is a broadcast address, which you cannot assign to a host. 225.87.34.1 falls in the Class D multicast address range and cannot be assigned to a single host.
whyWrong: 192.167.9.46 is outside the private range 192.168.0.0 to 192.168.255.255.
172.16.255.255 is a broadcast address with the default Class B mask and cannot be assigned to a host.
