In NAT mode, the VM gets its address from the host, which translates its traffic onto the physical network.
Isolation mode is not a standard VM networking mode that takes addresses from the physical network.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 7: Network Architecture, Review Questions question 2
note: Hypervisor networking modes are not a named N10-009 topic; tagged with 1.2 physical and virtual appliances (the virtual switch).

stem: Which type of switch connects all devices in one rack to the rest of the network?
explanation: A ToR (top of rack) switch connects all the other devices in its rack to the rest of the network. In a spine-and-leaf design, the ToR switches are the leaf switches, and each one connects to every spine switch. It is often mounted at the top of the rack for easy access and cable management.
whyWrong: A spine switch connects to the leaf switches of many racks, not to the devices in one rack.
An EoR (end of row) switch serves all the racks in a row, not just one rack.
A core switch carries backbone traffic for the whole network, not the devices of one rack.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 7: Network Architecture, Review Questions question 3

stem: Which cloud management technique executes a series of tasks in a workflow?
explanation: Orchestration is the automation of many tasks so that they run together in a complex, lengthy workflow. The tasks and their order are defined in a template, also called a playbook. A well-orchestrated cloud deployment needs little hands-on time and reduces human error.
whyWrong: Automation runs individual tasks without human input, while orchestration joins those tasks into a workflow.
YAML is a data format often used to write templates, not a management technique.
An SLA is a contract that sets the service levels a provider must meet.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 7: Network Architecture, Review Questions question 5

stem: What are two advantages to using virtualization on a network? (Choose two.)
explanation: Virtualization lets one powerful host run many VMs, so hardware that would sit mostly idle is used efficiently. Each VM is also separated from the others, so a fault or a security threat in one VM is isolated from the rest. Increased complexity and a single point of failure are disadvantages of virtualization, not advantages.
whyWrong: Increased complexity is a disadvantage of virtualization.
Running many VMs on one host creates a single point of failure, which is a disadvantage.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 7: Network Architecture, Review Questions question 6
note: Virtualization benefits are not a named N10-009 topic; tagged with 1.2 physical and virtual appliances. Added (Choose two.) to the stem to match the two answers the stem asks for.

stem: Which resource can ensure repeatability of tasks?
explanation: A playbook, or template, defines a set of reusable tasks in code. Rerunning the same playbook configures resources exactly the same way each time, which gives repeatability. Doing the same work by hand in a GUI rarely gives identical results.
whyWrong: A code branch is a copy of the code for development and testing, not a definition of repeatable tasks.
A repository stores versions of code but does not run tasks.
A pipeline moves code through build, test, and deploy stages, but the playbook defines the repeatable tasks.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 7: Network Architecture, Review Questions question 7

stem: What kind of hypervisor is installed directly on top of the server’s firmware?
explanation: A type 1 hypervisor installs on a computer before any OS and runs directly on top of the server's firmware. It is itself a minimal operating system that partitions the hardware among VMs. The book notes that calling it a bare-metal hypervisor is not accurate, because it still relies on firmware to talk to the hardware.
whyWrong: The book calls the bare-metal name inaccurate, because a type 1 hypervisor runs on firmware rather than on bare hardware.
A type 2 hypervisor installs as an application inside a host OS.
A hosted hypervisor is another name for a type 2 hypervisor, which runs inside a host OS.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 7: Network Architecture, Review Questions question 8
note: Answer written from the chapter, which calls bare metal an erroneous name for a type 1 hypervisor; many other sources treat the two as the same, so options 1 and 2 overlap. Hypervisors are not a named N10-009 topic; tagged with 1.2 virtual appliances.

stem: You’ve been tasked with providing infrastructure to a team of app developers who are working on a new system for HR to track overtime and comp days. The app will be accessed by employees on their mobile phones, tablets, and laptops. The developer team needs to test the app in several OS environments, and they want to run the code directly in the cloud without managing servers. Which type of cloud service will meet all these requirements?
explanation: PaaS gives developers ready platforms, including the OS and runtime, on which to build and test applications in several environments. Serverless compute, a PaaS service, lets them run code directly in the cloud without managing a server. The app is then reachable from phones, tablets, and laptops over the Internet.
whyWrong: IaaS would make the team build and manage the virtual servers themselves.
Storage is a cloud resource type, not a service model that lets developers run and test code.
Compute is a cloud resource type, and on its own it still means managing servers.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 7: Network Architecture, Scenario-Based Questions question 3

stem: You work as a website developer on a team designing some improvements to your company’s internal website. As you finish your to-do list for the morning, which consists of several minor changes to a portion of the website’s search engine code, a coworker asks if you’d like to join a small group for lunch. What should you do FIRST before you leave?
explanation: A commit uploads your changes to the branch you are working on. Developers should commit small changes often so they are saved and joined into the shared code before conflicts with other people's work build up. Merging into production comes later, after others test and approve the changes.
whyWrong: Merging puts the changes into the production code, which should happen only after testing and approval.
A branch is a copy of the code you work in, and your changes are already in one.
Reversing your changes would throw away the morning's work.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 7: Network Architecture, Scenario-Based Questions question 4
note: Changed the stem from 'What should you do before you leave?' to add FIRST, to make the qualifier explicit.

stem: Which of the following techniques expands a broadcast domain?
options: Adding more routers to a network
Adding more layer 2 switches to a network
Adding more VLANs to a network
Adding a SAN to a network
explanation: Adding more layer 2 switches to a network expands the broadcast domain because the switches transmit broadcast messages to all their ports. You can use physical devices like routers to create separate LANs and, therefore, separate broadcast domains. At layer 2, you can create virtual LANs to break up the broadcast domain. A SAN will not transmit broadcast messages from a LAN.
whyWrong: Routers do not forward broadcasts, so each router interface creates a separate broadcast domain.
Each VLAN is its own broadcast domain, so adding VLANs breaks the broadcast domain into smaller ones.
A SAN does not carry broadcast messages from the LAN.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation, Self-Check question 1

stem: Which SAN connection technology can run over ordinary Ethernet NICs without any special equipment needed?
explanation: iSCSI (Internet SCSI) can work on a twisted-pair Ethernet network with ordinary Ethernet NICs. FC (Fibre Channel) requires special hardware: specialized FC switches connect servers with each other and with the outside network. Instead of NICs, FC devices communicate through HBAs (host bus adapters). SATA (Serial Advanced Technology Attachment) cables connect a computer’s hard drive to its motherboard. IB (InfiniBand), like FC, requires specialized network hardware.
whyWrong: Fibre Channel needs special hardware such as FC switches and host bus adapters.
SATA is a cable interface that connects a drive to a motherboard, not a SAN network technology.
InfiniBand, like Fibre Channel, needs specialized network hardware.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation, Self-Check question 3

stem: What is the binary number 1111 1111 in decimal?
explanation: An 8-bit binary number of all 1s is equal to 255 in decimal. Each bit adds its place value: 128 + 64 + 32 + 16 + 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 255. This is a good conversion to memorize, because 255 appears in every octet of a subnet mask that is all network bits.
whyWrong: Decimal 100 is 0110 0100 in binary.
Decimal 8 is 0000 1000 in binary.
Decimal 192 is 1100 0000 in binary.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation, Self-Check question 4

stem: Which of the following statements is false?
options: Subnetting makes problems easier to locate and resolve.
Routing is more efficient when IP address spaces are mathematically related.
Network documentation is easier to manage when segments are properly subnetted.
Routers more easily manage IP address spaces that overlap.
explanation: It’s not true that routers more easily manage IP address spaces that overlap —if IP address ranges connected to a router’s own interfaces overlap, the router will not be able to route messages accurately between the LANs. Benefits of subnetting include easier management of network documentation and easier location and resolution of network problems. Routing is more efficient on larger networks when IP address spaces are mathematically related at a binary level.
whyWrong: This statement is true, because subnetting keeps a problem inside one smaller segment.
This statement is true, because related address spaces let routers summarize routes.
This statement is true, because well-planned subnets make the network easier to document.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation, Self-Check question 5

stem: What is the network ID of the IP address 192.168.72.149/16?
explanation: The CIDR notation of /16 indicates the first 16 bits, or two octets, of the IP address identify the network ID: 192.168. By convention, 0s can be used to complete the four octets when referring to the network ID: 192.168.0.0. The host ID is 0.0.72.149. For 192.168.72.0 to be the network ID and 0.0.0.149 to be the host ID, the CIDR notation would have had to be /24.
whyWrong: 0.0.0.149 would be the host ID only with a /24 prefix.
0.0.72.149 is the host ID, not the network ID.
192.168.72.0 would be the network ID only with a /24 prefix.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation, Self-Check question 6

stem: Which network space in AWS prevents Internet access for its hosts?
explanation: A private subnet hosts resources, such as EC2 instances or database instances, that should not be accessible from the Internet. A VPC (virtual private cloud) is a customer-managed, software-defined portion of a larger, cloud-based network that can contain subnets and many other kinds of network resources. A public subnet hosts resources that should be accessible directly from the Internet. An IG (Internet Gateway) is a gateway device that allows traffic to exit AWS’s own infrastructure.
whyWrong: A VPC is the whole customer network space, which can hold both public and private subnets.
A public subnet hosts resources that must be reachable directly from the Internet.
An Internet gateway gives a VPC access to the Internet rather than preventing it.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation, Self-Check question 9

stem: Which resource performs computing at the user’s location?
explanation: An edge device is an endpoint device that can perform limited computations at or near the user’s location. A jump box is an EC2 instance in a public subnet used to gain privileged access to a resource hosted in a private subnet. A NAT gateway is a logical appliance that performs NAT functions, providing filtered, protected access from resources in the private subnet to services on the Internet. A CDN (content delivery network) takes advantage of globally distributed infrastructure and smaller data centers or partner network resources to deliver data closer to users before entering the public Internet infrastructure—it does not, however, perform compute services at those locations.
whyWrong: A jump box is an instance in a public subnet used to reach resources in a private subnet.
A NAT gateway gives resources in a private subnet filtered access to the Internet.
A CDN caches and delivers data closer to users but does not perform compute at their location.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation, Self-Check question 10
note: Edge computing is not a named N10-009 topic; tagged with 1.2 applications (CDN), which the chapter discusses with it.

stem: How many bits of a class A IP address are used for host information?
explanation: A class A address uses its first octet (8 bits) for the network ID, which gives the default mask 255.0.0.0. The other three octets, 24 bits, hold host information. This is why a class A network can have so many hosts.
whyWrong: 8 bits is the network portion of a class A address, not the host portion.
16 bits is the host portion of a class B address.
32 bits is the whole IPv4 address, which includes the network portion.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation, Review Questions question 1

stem: If a server has a subnet mask of 255.255.255.224, how many bits in its IP address identify the host?
explanation: The mask 255.255.255.224 is /27, because 224 is 1110 0000 in binary and adds 3 network bits to the first 24. That leaves 32 − 27 = 5 bits to identify the host. Five host bits give 2^5 − 2 = 30 usable hosts per subnet.
whyWrong: 27 bits is the network portion of this mask, not the host portion.
8 bits would be the host portion of a /24 mask such as 255.255.255.0.
30 is the number of usable hosts per subnet, not the number of host bits.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation, Review Questions question 2

stem: What is the greatest number of bits you could borrow from the host portion of a class B subnet mask and still have at least 130 hosts per subnet?
explanation: A class B address has 16 host bits. Borrowing 8 bits leaves 8 host bits, which gives 2^8 − 2 = 254 usable hosts per subnet. Borrowing 9 bits would leave 7 host bits and only 126 hosts, which is fewer than 130.
whyWrong: Borrowing 0 bits works but makes no subnets, and more bits can be borrowed while keeping 130 hosts.
Borrowing 9 bits leaves 7 host bits, which gives only 126 usable hosts.
Borrowing 10 bits leaves 6 host bits, which gives only 62 usable hosts.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation, Review Questions question 3
note: Removed the stem's reference to Table 8-4; the question can be worked out without it.

stem: What do well-chosen subnets accomplish? (Choose two.)
options: IP address spaces overlap for easier management.
Network documentation is easier to manage.
Routing efficiency is increased by ensuring IP address spaces are not mathematically related.
Problems only affect one subnet at a time, making them easier to pin down.
explanation: Well-chosen subnets make network documentation easier to manage, because each segment has a clear, planned address range. They also limit a problem to one subnet at a time, so it is easier to locate and resolve. Address spaces should not overlap, and routing is more efficient when address spaces are mathematically related.
whyWrong: Overlapping address spaces stop a router from routing correctly between the LANs.
Routing is more efficient when address spaces are mathematically related, not when they are unrelated.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation, Review Questions question 4
note: The chapter lists both option 1 and option 3 as benefits of subnetting, so the question was made a Choose two question.

stem: Which hexadecimal block in an IPv6 address is used for the Subnet ID?
explanation: In a typical IPv6 global address, the first three blocks (48 bits) are the site prefix assigned to the organization. The fourth block, 16 bits, is the subnet ID, which can create up to 65,536 subnets. The last four blocks are the interface ID.
whyWrong: The first block is part of the site prefix, which identifies the organization's global routing prefix.
The third block is the last part of the 48-bit site prefix.
The eighth block is part of the 64-bit interface ID that identifies the host.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation, Review Questions question 5

stem: Subnetting operates at the __________ layer while VLANs function at the __________ layer.
explanation: Subnetting divides IP address space, so it works at the network layer (layer 3). VLANs group switch ports and tag frames, so they work at the data link layer (layer 2). Both split a network into smaller broadcast domains, at different layers.
whyWrong: Subnetting uses IP addresses, which belong to the network layer, not the physical layer.
VLANs work with frames at the data link layer, not with signals at the physical layer.
VLANs work at the data link layer, not the application layer.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation, Review Questions question 8

stem: A VPC is most similar in concept to a(n) __________.
explanation: A VPC is a network space in the cloud where the customer defines IP addressing, subnets, routing, and firewall-type protections. This makes it similar in concept to an on-premises LAN. Like a LAN, a VPC can be divided into several subnets.
whyWrong: A VLAN is one logical segment of a switched network, while a VPC is a whole network that can hold many subnets.
A router is one device that joins networks, not a whole network space.
A switch is one device that connects hosts, not a whole network space.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation, Review Questions question 10

stem: You are designing a cloud infrastructure to host a web server and a database instance. The web server will need to be accessible for all your clients, who live in three different countries. You and your business partner are the only ones who should have access to the database instance. What appliance should only the web server have a route to find?
explanation: An Internet gateway lets traffic pass between a VPC and the Internet. Only the web server's subnet, the public subnet, should have a route to the Internet gateway so clients can reach it. The database stays in a private subnet with no route to the Internet gateway, and admins reach it through a jump box.
whyWrong: A private subnet is a network space for resources like the database, not an appliance to route to.
A public subnet is the network space that holds the web server, not an appliance.
A jump box is used by admins to reach the private database, not by clients to reach the web server.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 8: Network Segmentation, Scenario-Based Questions question 4

stem: You just moved into a rural office space that has telephone service but no cable. Which WAN service could you use without needing to install new wiring to your location?
explanation: DSL (digital subscriber line) operates over the PSTN (public switched telephone network), which is a network of lines and carrier equipment that provide landline telephone service to homes and businesses. Cable broadband uses the coaxial cable wiring used for TV signals. Fiber broadband and leased fiber both require fiber cables, although it’s possible there could be a fiber broadband service that reaches a nearby node, which then runs over the phone lines for the final stretch to the office’s location.
whyWrong: Fiber broadband needs fiber cable to be run to the office.
Leased fiber needs a fiber line to be installed to the office.
Cable broadband needs the coaxial TV cabling that the office does not have.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 9: Wide Area Networking, Self-Check question 1
note: WAN services such as DSL are not a named N10-009 topic; tagged with 1.5 wired media (DSL runs over telephone wiring with RJ11 connectors).

stem: Which WAN service offers active-active load balancing?
explanation: An SD-WAN (software-defined wide area network) managed network offers active-active load balancing where it can choose the best physical WAN connection for different types of traffic according to traffic prioritization and current network conditions. DSL, cable, and fiber broadband all offer “best-effort” service over a single connection to the ISP.
whyWrong: Cable broadband is a best-effort service over a single connection to the ISP.
DSL is a best-effort service over a single connection to the ISP.
Fiber broadband is a best-effort service over a single connection to the ISP.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 9: Wide Area Networking, Self-Check question 3

stem: Which device can be used to increase network performance by caching websites?
explanation: A proxy server can improve performance for users accessing resources external to their network by caching files. A firewall is a specialized device or software that selectively filters or blocks traffic between networks. An IDS (intrusion detection system) monitors network traffic, generating alerts about suspicious activity. An AWS security group filters traffic into and out of a single EC2 instance.
whyWrong: A firewall filters or blocks traffic between networks but does not cache websites.
An IDS monitors traffic and raises alerts but does not cache websites.
A security group filters traffic to a cloud instance but does not cache websites.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 9: Wide Area Networking, Self-Check question 7

stem: Which firewall type can protect a home network from adult content not suitable for the family’s children?
explanation: Application layer firewalls can block designated types of traffic based on application data contained within packets. The simplest form of a firewall is a packet-filtering firewall, which is a network device or application that only examines each message’s header. Host-based firewall software only protects the computer on which it’s installed. A stateless firewall manages each incoming packet as a stand-alone entity without regard to currently active connections.
whyWrong: A packet-filtering firewall examines only packet headers, so it cannot see the content.
A host-based firewall protects only the computer it runs on, not the whole home network.
A stateless firewall treats each packet alone and does not inspect application content.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 9: Wide Area Networking, Self-Check question 8

stem: Which OSI layer is responsible for directing data from one LAN to another?
explanation: The network layer (layer 3) uses logical addresses such as IP addresses to route data from one LAN to another. Routers work at this layer. The data link layer only moves frames between nodes on the same LAN.
whyWrong: The transport layer manages end-to-end delivery between applications, not routing between LANs.
The data link layer moves frames within one LAN using MAC addresses.
The physical layer sends bits as signals over the medium.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 9: Wide Area Networking, Review Questions question 1

stem: What virtual resource is used to protect network interfaces in the cloud?
explanation: A security group, such as an AWS security group or an Azure NSG, filters traffic into and out of an individual instance's network interface. It works much like a host-based firewall. Tools such as NACLs and network security lists filter traffic for a whole subnet instead.
whyWrong: A NACL filters traffic for a whole subnet, not for individual network interfaces.
A network security list filters traffic for a subnet or other virtual network space.
A virtual firewall is a general term for a firewall appliance running as a VM, not the cloud resource that protects each interface.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 9: Wide Area Networking, Review Questions question 3

stem: Who is responsible for the security of hardware on which a public cloud runs?
options: Both the cloud customer and the cloud provider
explanation: In a public cloud, the provider owns and runs the physical data centers, servers, storage, and network hardware. Under the shared responsibility model, the provider always secures this physical layer, whatever the service model. The customer shares responsibility only for the layers it controls, such as its data, accounts, and (in IaaS) the guest OS and applications.
whyWrong: The customer never has physical access to the public cloud hardware, so it cannot secure it.
The responsibility for hardware does not change with the service model; it always stays with the provider.
Responsibility is shared only for the higher layers such as data, identities, and applications, not the hardware.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 9: Wide Area Networking, Review Questions question 6
note: The shared responsibility model is not named in the N10-009 objectives; tagged with 1.3 deployment models (public cloud) as the closest topic.

stem: You’re setting up a cloud deployment to run a business-critical database, along with backups and read-only copies distributed across multiple geographical regions to increase redundancy and decrease latency. Employees at your location must be able to access the data safely. Which cloud connectivity option will create a connection from your office network that is always available with industry-standard encryption for sensitive data in transit?
explanation: A site-to-site VPN to the cloud provider builds an encrypted tunnel between the office network and the cloud network that stays up all the time. Its IPsec encryption protects sensitive data in transit, even when the tunnel runs over the Internet. A direct connection gives low latency and predictable performance, but it usually does not encrypt traffic by itself.
whyWrong: A direct connection is a dedicated leased line that often has no encryption of its own and relies on isolation or an added security layer.
A plain Internet connection does not encrypt the traffic between the office and the cloud.
A client VPN protects only one device at a time and is not an always-on link for the whole office network.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 9: Wide Area Networking, Scenario-Based Questions question 1

stem: You’re securing a network expansion for a high school, and school officials are concerned about the kinds of Internet access students might have on the network. Primarily, they want to ensure they can block traffic that contains problematic website content or gaming communications. What kind of firewall will give you the greatest ability to filter for this type of traffic?
explanation: An application layer firewall examines the payload of each message, not only its header, so it can block designated types of traffic by their application data. That lets it block responses from websites with questionable content and identify gaming communications. Stateless and stateful firewalls filter mainly on header and connection information at the network and transport layers.
whyWrong: A stateless firewall checks each packet's header on its own and cannot look at website content or application data.
A stateful firewall tracks connection state but does not inspect the application payload for content.
A host-based firewall protects only the computer it is installed on, not the whole school network.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 9: Wide Area Networking, Scenario-Based Questions question 3

stem: Which security device relies on a TAP or port mirroring?
explanation: An NIDS (network-based intrusion detection system) sits off to the side of network traffic and is sent duplicates of packets traversing the network from a switch configured with port mirroring or from a TAP device. An HIDS (host-based intrusion detection system) runs on a single computer to detect attacks to that one host. An HIDS solution might also include FIM (file integrity monitoring), which alerts the system of any changes made to files that shouldn’t change, such as operating system files. Like HIDS, an HIPS (host-based intrusion prevention system) protects a specific host and doesn’t need access to all network traffic.
whyWrong: An HIPS protects a single host and does not need copies of all network traffic.
A threat assessment is a review process that identifies threats, not a device that receives mirrored traffic.
A posture assessment examines the network for ways it might be compromised and is not a device fed by a TAP.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management, Self-Check question 6

stem: What information in a transmitted message might an IDS use to identify network threats?
explanation: Signature-based detection in an IDS looks for identifiable patterns, or signatures, in transmitted messages that are known to indicate exploits or other unwanted traffic. These signatures must be updated regularly through signature management so the IDS can recognize new threats. Anomaly-based detection is the other common method, and it compares traffic with a baseline instead.
whyWrong: FIM checks files on a host for unexpected changes and does not inspect transmitted messages.
Port mirroring is a switch feature that copies traffic to a monitoring device; it is not information in a message.
An ACL is a list of rules on a router or firewall that permits or denies traffic, not a pattern inside a message.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 10: Risk Management, Review Questions question 2

stem: Which of the following statements is false?
options: Zero trust reduces possible lateral movement of an attack.
Zero trust reduces implicit trust granted after authentication.
explanation: When applying a zero trust security model, the size of attack surfaces is reduced because resources are individually protected rather than defining a larger network space with protected resources contained inside it. Zero trust increases observability because every request is logged, and all traffic is inspected. Zero trust reduces possible lateral movement of an attack because resources are isolated from other resources by requiring authenticated communication between them. Zero trust reduces implicit trust granted after authentication because it takes a default deny posture toward every entity and every request.
whyWrong: This statement is true, because zero trust logs every request and inspects all traffic.
This statement is true, because isolated resources must authenticate to each other, which limits lateral movement.
This statement is true, because zero trust takes a default deny posture toward every entity and request.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 11: Access Control, Self-Check question 8

stem: What is the security side of the SASE framework?
explanation: The security side of the SASE framework—collectively referred to as SSE (security service edge) —incorporates many security services that, together, can protect distributed resources. On the networking side, SASE relies on SDN (software-defined networking) and SD-WAN (software-defined wide area networking) technologies to connect resources located in widespread locations. SaaS (Software as a Service) applications often run on independent platforms in the cloud and can be better secured by the implementation of a SASE framework.
whyWrong: SDN is part of the networking side of SASE, not its security side.
SaaS is a cloud service model whose applications SASE can help protect.
SD-WAN is part of the networking side of SASE, not its security side.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 11: Access Control, Self-Check question 9

stem: Which SASE security component most often includes DLP monitoring?
explanation: A CASB (cloud access security broker) solution enforces access control and DLP (data loss prevention) policies on cloud-hosted resources, especially data. FWaaS (Firewall as a Service) is a cloud-hosted firewall that provides scalable NGFW (next generation firewall) services for cloud-based network spaces. Similar to a firewall, an SWG (secure web gateway) sits between users and the Internet to filter incoming traffic and block risky or unauthorized outgoing traffic, such as communication with sites known to contain malicious content. ZTNA (zero trust network access) refers to controlling remote access not to networks but to applications, data, and services independently of the type of network connection used.
whyWrong: FWaaS is a cloud-hosted firewall that filters traffic and is not the component known for DLP policies.
An SWG filters web traffic between users and the Internet but is not the component most associated with DLP.
ZTNA controls remote access to applications and data, not DLP monitoring of cloud data.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 11: Access Control, Self-Check question 10

stem: Which of the following technologies is part of the networking portion of SASE?
explanation: SASE combines a networking side and a security side. The networking side relies on SDN and SD-WAN to connect resources in widely spread locations. The security side, called SSE, includes services such as CASB, SWG, FWaaS, and ZTNA.
whyWrong: CASB is a security service in the SSE side of SASE.
An SWG is a security service in the SSE side of SASE.
FWaaS is a security service in the SSE side of SASE.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 11: Access Control, Review Questions question 10

stem: As you’re building a new smartphone app for employees at your company, you need to decide what security tool will let you require that the user’s phone be updated to a specific OS version in order to use the app. This requirement should be implemented and checked every time the user signs into the app. Which solution is the BEST fit to enforce this requirement?
explanation: ZTNA controls access to applications, data, and services instead of to whole networks, whatever connection the user has. It checks the identity and the device posture, such as the OS version, each time the user requests access to the app. This makes it the best fit for a requirement that is checked at every sign-in.
whyWrong: FWaaS is a cloud-hosted firewall that filters traffic and does not check a phone's OS version at app sign-in.
An SWG filters web traffic to and from the Internet and does not enforce device requirements for an app.
A CASB enforces access and DLP policies on cloud-hosted resources rather than checking device posture at each app sign-in.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 11: Access Control, Scenario-Based Questions question 4

stem: Which bandwidth management technique limits traffic specifically between a single sender and a single receiver?
explanation: Flow control addresses the number of frames that can be handled from end to end between a single sender and a single receiver. Congestion control addresses traffic throughout the network. QoS (quality of service) techniques allow for more nuanced control of what happens to the traffic once it’s on the network. Traffic shaping is a QoS technique.
whyWrong: Congestion control manages traffic throughout the network, not only between one sender and one receiver.
Traffic shaping is a QoS technique that manages the type and amount of traffic across a network or interface.
QoS controls how different kinds of traffic are treated across the network, not end to end between two hosts.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery, Self-Check question 5
note: Data link layer flow control is not a named sub-bullet in N10-009; tagged with 1.1 Layer 2 as the closest topic.

stem: Which flow control method resends a lost frame along with all frames sent with it?
explanation: With the Go-Back-N sliding window flow control method, the sender retransmits all frames in the window, even if only one frame was lost. With the Stop-and-Wait method, only one frame is sent at a time. With the Selective Repeat sliding window method, only the lost frame is resent while successive frames continue to be sent. Backpressure is a congestion control technique.
whyWrong: Selective Repeat resends only the lost frame while new frames continue to be sent.
Stop-and-Wait sends only one frame at a time, so there are no other frames to resend with it.
Backpressure is a congestion control technique, not a flow control method that resends frames.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery, Self-Check question 6
note: Data link layer flow control is not a named sub-bullet in N10-009; tagged with 1.1 Layer 2 as the closest topic.

stem: Which of the following statements is true?
options: When streaming a movie, the transmission is sensitive to loss and tolerant of delays.
When sending an email, the transmission is sensitive to delays and tolerant of loss.
When streaming a movie, the transmission is sensitive to delays and tolerant of loss.
When sending an email, the transmission is sensitive to loss and sensitive to delays.
explanation: Delayed traffic for a streaming movie results in reduced quality, while an occasional skipped video frame will likely not be noticeable. This means that, when streaming a movie, the transmission is sensitive to delays and tolerant of loss. An email, however, can tolerate a brief delay, but lost data can result in a corrupted message. Therefore, when sending an email, the transmission is sensitive to loss and tolerant of delays.
whyWrong: A streaming movie tolerates an occasional lost frame but suffers from delays.
Email tolerates a brief delay, but lost data can corrupt the message.
Email is sensitive to loss but tolerant of a brief delay.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery, Self-Check question 7

stem: What port do SNMP agents listen on?
explanation: SNMP agents on managed devices listen for requests from the NMS on UDP port 161. The NMS listens on UDP port 162 for trap messages that agents send when an event occurs. Ports 20 and 21 belong to FTP.
whyWrong: Port 21 is the FTP control port.
Port 162 is where the NMS receives SNMP traps, not where agents listen.
Port 20 is the FTP data port.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery, Review Questions question 2

stem: What field in an IPv4 packet is altered to prioritize video streaming traffic over web surfing traffic?
explanation: DiffServ is a QoS technique that prioritizes traffic at layer 3 by marking the DiffServ field of an IPv4 packet. The first 6 bits of this 8-bit field are the DSCP value, which tells routers how to forward the stream. A video stream can get a high priority while web surfing gets a low priority.
whyWrong: The Traffic Class field is the similar QoS field in IPv6 packets, not IPv4 packets.
The Priority Code Point is a QoS field in the VLAN tag of an Ethernet frame, not in an IPv4 packet.
The Time to Live field limits how many hops a packet can travel and does not set priority.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery, Review Questions question 3

stem: Which data link layer flow control method offers the most efficient frame transmission when sending large volumes of data?
explanation: With the Selective Repeat sliding window method, the receiver acknowledges received frames with selective acknowledgments, and only the unacknowledged frame is resent. The sender keeps sending new frames while space is available in the window. This is more efficient for large volumes of data, although it is more complex because the receiver must reorder frames.
whyWrong: Go-Back-N resends every frame in the window when one frame is lost, which wastes bandwidth.
A choke packet is a congestion control signal, not a flow control method for sending frames.
Stop-and-Wait sends only one frame at a time and waits for each acknowledgment, which is the least efficient method.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery, Review Questions question 7
note: Data link layer flow control is not a named sub-bullet in N10-009; tagged with 1.1 Layer 2 as the closest topic.

stem: Your roommate has been hogging the bandwidth on your router lately. What feature should you configure on the router to limit the amount of bandwidth their computer can utilize at any one time?
explanation: Traffic shaping is a QoS technique that manages the type and amount of traffic that crosses a network or interface at any moment. On a router it can limit, or police, the bandwidth that one computer can use at a time. This keeps one heavy user from slowing down everyone else on the connection.
whyWrong: Power management saves energy on devices and does not limit bandwidth.
Congestion control manages traffic levels across the network but does not cap one computer's bandwidth.
Flow control manages how many frames a single receiver can accept, not how much bandwidth a user gets.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Chapter 12: Performance and Recovery, Scenario-Based Questions question 3

stem: While troubleshooting a workstation connectivity problem, you enter the following command: ping 127.0.0.1. The response indicates the test failed. What can you determine about that workstation?
options: Its network cable is faulty or not connected to the wall jack.
Its TCP/IP stack is not installed properly.
It has been prevented from transmitting data past the default gateway.
Its DNS name server specification is incorrect.
explanation: The address 127.0.0.1 is the IPv4 loopback address, so a ping to it never leaves the workstation. It tests only whether the computer's own TCP/IP stack is installed and working. A failed loopback ping means the TCP/IP stack has a problem, while cabling, gateway, DHCP, and DNS issues would not affect this test.
whyWrong: A loopback ping does not leave the computer, so a faulty or disconnected cable does not cause it to fail.
Traffic to the loopback address never reaches the default gateway, so gateway problems do not affect it.
A loopback ping does not depend on the address that DHCP assigns.
A ping to a numeric address needs no name resolution, so DNS settings do not affect it.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 7

stem: Which of the following ports would be used during a domain name lookup?
explanation: DNS uses port 53 for name lookups. Clients send most queries over UDP port 53, and DNS uses TCP port 53 for large responses and zone transfers. The other ports belong to remote access, email, and secure web protocols.
whyWrong: Port 22 is SSH (and SFTP).
Port 23 is Telnet.
Port 110 is POP3.
Port 443 is HTTPS.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 10

stem: You have installed and configured two virtual web servers and a virtual mail server on a physical server. What networking mode will you assign to each server’s vNIC to ensure that the virtual machines’ clients on the Internet can access the virtual machines?
explanation: In bridged mode, a vNIC reaches the physical network through the host's NIC and gets its own IP address on the LAN, so other nodes can reach the VM directly. VMs that must be available at a fixed address, such as web servers and mail servers, should use bridged mode. The hypervisor's virtual switch that makes this connection is a virtual network appliance.
whyWrong: NAT mode hides the VMs behind the host's address, so outside clients cannot reach them directly.
Host-only mode lets VMs talk only with the host and each other, not with the physical network.
Internal mode keeps traffic among VMs on the host and gives no path to outside clients.
Grouped is not a vNIC networking mode.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 13
note: Virtualization networking modes are not named in N10-009; tagged to 1.2 physical and virtual appliances (the virtual switch).

stem: The software on a firewall you recently installed on your network examines each incoming packet. It blocks or allows traffic based on a set of criteria—including source IP address, destination ports, and TCP flags—and it does not evaluate traffic in relation to other traffic. What type of system is this? Choose TWO.
explanation: A firewall that checks each packet on its own against rules such as source IP address, destination port, and TCP flags is a packet-filtering firewall. Because it does not track connections or relate one packet to others, it is also a stateless firewall. Stateful firewalls, by contrast, keep track of sessions.
whyWrong: A host-based firewall runs on one computer, and the scenario describes the filtering method, not where it runs.
A stateful firewall tracks connections and judges packets in relation to earlier traffic.
An application layer firewall inspects the content of traffic for specific applications, not just header fields.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 17

stem: From your laptop, you need to remote into a switch to make some configuration changes. Which transport layer protocol and TCP/IP port should you open in Windows Firewall to make this work using Telnet?
explanation: Telnet uses TCP port 23. To reach the switch with Telnet, the firewall must allow TCP traffic on port 23. Telnet sends data in plain text, so SSH on TCP port 22 is the secure choice when the device supports it.
whyWrong: Telnet runs over TCP, not UDP.
Port 22 is SSH, and SSH runs over TCP, not UDP.
TCP port 22 is SSH, not Telnet.
Port 21 is the FTP control port, and FTP runs over TCP.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 20

stem: Recently, your company’s WAN experienced a disabling DDoS attack. Which of the following devices could detect such an attack and prevent it from affecting your network in the future?
explanation: A NIPS (network-based intrusion prevention system) watches traffic for a whole network and can act to block an attack it detects. It can stop DDoS traffic before it affects hosts. Host-based systems protect only one host, and detection-only systems do not block traffic.
whyWrong: A honeypot is a decoy that attracts attackers and does not protect the network from a DDoS attack.
A SIEM collects and correlates logs and alerts but does not block traffic itself.
An HIPS protects only the single host it runs on.
An HIDS only detects and logs attacks on one host and does not block them.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 21

stem: In a spine-and-leaf architecture, what type of switch is typically connected to a spine layer switch?
explanation: In a spine-and-leaf architecture, every leaf switch connects to every spine switch. Servers and other devices connect to the leaf switches, and the spine switches form the backbone. Spine switches do not connect to each other.
whyWrong: A core switch belongs to the three-tier hierarchical model, not the spine-and-leaf design.
A distribution switch is a layer of the three-tier model, which spine and leaf replaces.
An access switch is part of the three-tier model; in spine and leaf the leaf switches play that role.
Spine switches connect only to leaf switches, not to other spine switches.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 25

stem: What is the default subnet mask for the IP address 154.13.44.87?
explanation: The first octet of 154.13.44.87 is 154, which falls in the class B range of 128 through 191. The default subnet mask for a class B address is 255.255.0.0, so the first two octets identify the network. Class A uses 255.0.0.0 and class C uses 255.255.255.0.
whyWrong: 255.255.255.255 is the limited broadcast address, not a default subnet mask.
255.255.255.0 is the default mask for class C addresses, which start at 192.
255.0.0.0 is the default mask for class A addresses, which start at 1 through 126.
0.0.0.0 is not a usable subnet mask for a host address.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 26

stem: Your CFO has approved installing new backbone cabling on your school’s campus. One of the buildings is particularly far away from the others—nearly a kilometer. Which Ethernet standard will reach the distant building without the use of a repeater?
explanation: 1000BASE-LX uses long 1,300-nanometer wavelengths and supports segments of up to 5,000 meters on single-mode fiber. That makes it the standard for backbones between buildings that are about a kilometer apart. The other standards reach only a few hundred meters or less.
whyWrong: 10GBASE-T runs over twisted-pair copper with a maximum segment of 100 meters.
1000BASE-SX uses multimode fiber and reaches only about 550 meters.
10GBASE-SR uses multimode fiber and reaches only a few hundred meters.
1000BASE-T runs over twisted-pair copper with a maximum segment of 100 meters.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 27

stem: Which of the following is often used to secure data traveling over VPNs that use L2TP?
explanation: L2TP encapsulates data for a VPN but does not encrypt it. It is usually paired with IPsec, which provides the encryption and authentication for the tunnel. This combination is often written as L2TP/IPsec.
whyWrong: OpenVPN is a separate VPN solution that uses TLS, not a security layer for L2TP.
GRE is a tunneling protocol that encapsulates traffic but does not encrypt it.
Kerberos is an authentication protocol for network sign-in, not VPN data encryption.
SSH secures remote command-line sessions and is not used to secure L2TP tunnels.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 28

stem: You have purchased an outdoor access point capable of exchanging data via the 802.11n or 802.11ac wireless standard. According to these standards, what is the maximum distance, in meters, from the access point that wireless clients can travel and still reliably exchange data with the access point if there are no obstacles between them?
explanation: 802.11n and 802.11ac both list a maximum range of about 70 meters indoors and about 250 meters outdoors with no obstacles. Walls, furniture, and interference reduce the real range. An outdoor access point with clear line of sight can therefore reach clients up to about 250 meters away.
whyWrong: 20 meters is far less than the range of 802.11n or 802.11ac.
70 meters is the typical indoor range, not the outdoor range.
100 meters is the maximum segment length for twisted-pair Ethernet, not the 802.11 outdoor range.
450 meters is beyond the outdoor range listed for 802.11n and 802.11ac.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 30

stem: What is the network ID for a class C network that contains the group of IP addresses from 194.73.44.10 through 194.73.44.254?
explanation: A class C network uses the default mask 255.255.255.0, so the first three octets (194.73.44) identify the network. The network ID has all host bits set to 0, which gives 194.73.44.0. The address with all host bits set to 1, 194.73.44.255, is the broadcast address.
whyWrong: 194.73.44.1 is the first usable host address, not the network ID.
194.73.0.0 would be the network ID only with a class B mask of 255.255.0.0.
194.73.44.255 is the broadcast address of this class C network.
194.1.1.1 is a host address in a different network.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 33

stem: You are rearranging nodes on your Gigabit Ethernet network. Due to a necessarily hasty expansion, you have decided to supply power to a wireless router in a makeshift data room using PoE. Which of the following is likely the cheapest cabling you could use to connect this wireless router to the network’s backbone?
explanation: Cat 5e twisted-pair cable supports Gigabit Ethernet and PoE up to 100 meters. It is the least expensive cable on the list that meets both needs. Cat 6 also works but costs more, and coax and fiber cannot carry PoE to the router.
whyWrong: RG-6 coaxial cable is used for cable broadband and TV, not Gigabit Ethernet with PoE.
RG-59 coaxial cable is used for short video runs, not Gigabit Ethernet with PoE.
Single-mode fiber cannot carry PoE and costs more than copper.
Cat 6 supports Gigabit Ethernet and PoE but costs more than Cat 5e.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 37

stem: Which of the following is a valid MAC address?
explanation: A MAC address is a 48-bit physical address written as six pairs of hexadecimal digits, such as C3:00:50:00:FF:FF. It is used at the data link layer (layer 2) to deliver frames on the local network. IP addresses, by contrast, are logical addresses used at layer 3.
whyWrong: 153.101.24.3 is an IPv4 address, not a MAC address.
::9F53 is a shortened IPv6 address, not a MAC address.
FE80::32:1CA3:B0E2 is an IPv6 link local address, not a MAC address.
D0:00:00:00 has only four octets, but a MAC address has six.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 40

stem: On an IPv6 network, which of the following is a host computer’s loopback address?
explanation: The IPv6 loopback address is ::1, written with its prefix as ::1/128. It is the IPv6 equivalent of the IPv4 loopback address 127.0.0.1. A host uses it to test its own TCP/IP stack.
whyWrong: 1.0.0.1 is a public IPv4 address, not a loopback address.
FE80::1 is a link local IPv6 address, not the loopback address.
127::1 mixes IPv4 and IPv6 notation and is not a valid loopback address.
127.0.0.1 is the IPv4 loopback address, not the IPv6 one.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 49

stem: Which of the following devices can be used to separate broadcast domains? Choose TWO.
explanation: A broadcast domain is all the nodes a broadcast message reaches, and routers do not forward broadcasts, so each router interface marks the edge of one. A managed switch can also separate broadcast domains by placing ports in different VLANs. Hubs, repeaters, and access points pass broadcasts on and only extend a broadcast domain.
whyWrong: An access point bridges wireless clients onto the same LAN, so it extends the broadcast domain.
A repeater only regenerates the signal at layer 1 and passes broadcasts on.
A hub repeats every frame out of every port, so all its nodes share one broadcast domain.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 56
note: The book gives no answer key; switch is counted as correct because managed switches separate broadcast domains with VLANs.

stem: A Windows workstation is configured to use DHCP, but it cannot find a DHCP server. You run ipconfig in PowerShell. Which of the following IP addresses is MOST LIKELY reported by Windows?
explanation: When a Windows client set for DHCP cannot reach a DHCP server, it assigns itself an APIPA address in the range 169.254.0.1 through 169.254.255.254. An address such as 169.254.1.120 therefore shows that DHCP failed. APIPA addresses let the host talk only with other hosts on the same local segment.
whyWrong: 129.0.0.1 is a public IPv4 address that Windows does not assign itself.
255.255.255.0 is a subnet mask, not an IP address.
192.168.0.1 is a private address that a DHCP server or administrator assigns, not Windows on its own.
172.16.2.18 is a private RFC 1918 address that comes from a DHCP server or manual setup.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 68

stem: Which of the following transmission media is most resistant to interference?
explanation: Fiber-optic cable carries data as pulses of light, not electrical signals. It is therefore immune to EMI and RFI and does not suffer crosstalk. Copper cables and wireless transmissions are all affected by interference to some degree.
whyWrong: Twinaxial cable is shielded copper but is still subject to some electrical interference.
STP cable reduces interference with shielding but still carries electrical signals.
802.11ac radio signals are easily affected by interference from other devices and obstacles.
Coaxial cable resists interference with its shielding but is still copper that carries electrical signals.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 76

stem: What is the function of protocols and services at the network layer of the OSI model?
options: To manage the flow of communications in both directions during a session
To add segmentation and assembly information
To add logical addresses and properly route data
To apply electrical pulses to the wire
explanation: The network layer (layer 3) adds logical addresses, such as IP addresses, to packets. It also decides the path that data takes between networks, which is routing. Routers work at this layer.
whyWrong: Managing the dialog between two nodes during a session is the session layer (layer 5).
Segmentation and reassembly information is added by the transport layer (layer 4).
Encoding and encryption of data happen at the presentation layer (layer 6).
Placing electrical pulses on the wire is the job of the physical layer (layer 1).
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 80

stem: Suppose your Windows laptop’s wireless network adapter is configured to use the 802.11n wireless networking standard. Also, suppose a café you visit has a popular model of an 802.11ac access point. Assuming you have the correct SSID and logon credentials, what will MOST LIKELY happen when you attempt to associate with the café’s wireless network?
options: Your wireless networking client will be able to see the access point but will be unable to associate with it.
Your wireless networking client will not be able to see the access point.
Your wireless networking client will be able to see the access point and attempt to associate with it, but the incompatible frequencies will prevent successful association.
Your wireless networking client will be able to see the access point and attempt to associate with it, but the incompatible security techniques will prevent successful association.
Your wireless networking client will be able to see the access point and successfully associate with it.
explanation: 802.11ac access points are backward compatible with 802.11n clients, because both standards can use the 5 GHz band. The 802.11n laptop can see the access point and associate with it, though at 802.11n speeds. With the correct SSID and credentials, the connection succeeds.
whyWrong: Backward compatibility means an 802.11n client can associate with an 802.11ac access point, not just see it.
An 802.11n client can detect the 802.11ac access point because both use the 5 GHz band.
802.11n and 802.11ac share the 5 GHz band, so the frequencies are compatible.
Both standards support the same security methods, such as WPA2, so security is not a barrier.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 83

stem: Which protocol supports recovery of a router config file?
explanation: TFTP (Trivial File Transfer Protocol) uses UDP port 69 to copy files without authentication. Network devices commonly use it to back up and restore configuration files and firmware images. A router can load a saved config file from a TFTP server to recover its settings.
whyWrong: A UPS is an uninterruptible power supply, not a protocol.
SSH provides secure remote command-line access, not a file transfer for config recovery in this case.
SNMP monitors and manages devices but is not used to copy config files back to a router.
An OID is an identifier for a managed object in an SNMP MIB, not a protocol.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 86

stem: A virtual switch includes several virtual ports, each of which can be considered a _________________.
explanation: A virtual switch is a logical device that a hypervisor creates to pass frames between VMs and the physical network at the data link layer. Each of its virtual ports connects one vNIC and forwards frames like a bridge port. Hypervisors call this connection a bridge or a switch.
whyWrong: A router works at layer 3 between networks, while a virtual switch port forwards frames at layer 2.
A gateway connects different networks, not a single vNIC to a virtual switch.
A hub repeats every signal out of all ports at layer 1 and does not forward by MAC address.
A repeater only regenerates signals at layer 1 and has no ports for separate nodes.
source: CompTIA Network+ Guide to Networks (West), Cengage – Appendix C: Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 90

stem: A company expects its online store to need twice as many web servers each year as its customer base grows. Which cloud characteristic BEST describes the ability to add compute, storage, and network resources to meet this growing workload?
explanation: Scalability is the cloud's capacity to handle a growing workload by adding resources such as compute, storage, or networking. It lets the IT department expand its cloud-hosted VM environment with little effort as demand rises.
whyWrong: Multitenancy is one provider serving many customers on shared infrastructure.
A security list is a set of traffic rules attached to a cloud subnet.
A cloud gateway links the internal network to the cloud; it does not add capacity.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 7: Cloud Computing Concepts and Options

stem: Which statement describes the difference between scalability and elasticity in cloud computing?
options: Scalability is the capacity to grow to meet a larger workload; elasticity is adjusting resources up and down automatically as demand changes.
Scalability is sharing hardware among many customers; elasticity is isolating each customer in its own network.
Scalability applies only to private clouds; elasticity applies only to public clouds.
Scalability removes resources when demand falls; elasticity can only add resources.
explanation: Scalability is the cloud's capacity to handle increasing workloads by adding compute, storage, or networking resources. Elasticity is the dynamic, often automatic, adjustment of resources to match demand as it rises and falls. A cloud must be elastic to scale quickly, so the two work together.
whyWrong: Sharing hardware among customers is multitenancy, and isolating a customer's network is a VPC.
Both characteristics apply to public, private, and hybrid clouds.
Elasticity adds and removes resources, and scalability is about growth, so the roles are reversed.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 7: Cloud Computing Concepts and Options

stem: What does a network security group (NSG) do in a cloud environment?
options: It acts as a virtual firewall that allows or denies traffic to and from virtual machines, interfaces, and subnets.
It links the company's on-premises network to the cloud provider over a private circuit.
It runs routers and switches as software instead of dedicated hardware.
It gives each tenant a logically isolated network inside the public cloud.
explanation: A network security group is a virtual firewall in the cloud. Its rules allow or deny traffic to and from resources such as virtual machines, network interfaces, and subnets, and the rules can be updated as the environment changes.
whyWrong: A private circuit to the cloud is a cloud connectivity option such as Direct Connect.
Running network devices as software is network functions virtualization (NFV).
An isolated network inside a public cloud is a virtual private cloud (VPC).
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 7: Cloud Computing Concepts and Options

stem: An administrator creates a network security list in a cloud tenancy. Which entity is the list typically associated with, so that its rules apply to the virtual NICs inside it?
explanation: A network security list is a set of security rules that govern traffic for cloud resources. It is associated with an entity, typically a subnet, and every virtual NIC in that subnet is subject to the lists attached to the subnet. Security lists came before network security groups and work in a similar way.
whyWrong: Security lists filter network traffic, not the actions of a user account.
A DNS zone holds name records and has no traffic rules.
A storage bucket holds objects; security lists apply to network interfaces in a subnet.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 7: Cloud Computing Concepts and Options

stem: A company's network has each floor wired as a star around a switch, and the floor switches are joined to each other with redundant links in a partial mesh. Which term BEST describes this topology?
explanation: A hybrid topology combines two or more physical topologies, here star on each floor and mesh between the floor switches. Many large networks are hybrids because each part of the network uses the layout that suits it best.
whyWrong: Point to point is a single direct link between two devices.
Spine and leaf is a data center design in which every leaf switch connects to every spine switch.
Collapsed core merges the core and distribution layers of the three-tier model.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 2: Network Topologies, Architectures, and Types

stem: Which of the following wireless protocols can operate at 2.4 GHz? (Choose four.)
explanation: Wireless standards specify an RF range on which communications are sent. The 802.11b and 802.11g standards use the 2.4 GHz range. 802.11a and 802.11ac use the 5 GHz range. 802.11n can operate at 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz. 802.11ax operates in both the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz ranges.
whyWrong: 802.11a operates only in the 5 GHz band.
802.11ac operates only in the 5 GHz band.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: You are installing a wireless network solution that uses a feature known as MU-MIMO. Which wireless networking standards are you possibly using? (Choose two.)
explanation: MU-MIMO is used by the 802.11ac and 802.11ax standards and makes multiuser MIMO possible (increasing the range and speed of wireless networking). MIMO, itself, enables the transmission of multiple data streams traveling on different antennas in the same channel at the same time.
whyWrong: 802.11a predates MIMO and uses a single data stream.
802.11b predates MIMO and uses a single data stream.
802.11n introduced single-user MIMO but does not support MU-MIMO.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 6: Wireless Solutions, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: You have been given a physical wiring schematic that shows a section of horizontal cable running through the ceiling space and over fluorescent lights. Given this information, what cable recommendation might you make, if any?
options: Nonplenum cable should be used between the IDF and MDF.
The horizontal cable run should use plenum cable.
The patch cable connecting the printer should be shorter.
Leave the network cabling as is.
explanation: In this scenario, a section of horizontal cable runs through the ceiling and over fluorescent lights. This cable run might be a problem because such devices can cause electromagnetic interference (EMI). Alternatively, plenum cable is used in this scenario. Shielded twisted-pair (STP) may have worked as well.
whyWrong: Nonplenum cable is not the fix for a horizontal run through the ceiling space.
A shorter printer patch cable does not address the cable run over the fluorescent lights.
The run over the fluorescent lights is a possible problem, so leaving the cabling as is ignores it.
source: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Cram (Dulaney) – Chapter 8: Network Operations, Cram Quiz 2 question 1
note: The wiring schematic was lost in extraction; the stem now states the detail the book's explanation uses. The book pairs plenum cable with an EMI problem: plenum rating is about fire safety in air-handling spaces, while STP (which the book also mentions) is what resists EMI.

stem: Which of the following are techniques used in traffic shaping to prevent networks from being overwhelmed by data transmissions? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: Bandwidth throttling is a traffic shaping technique that prevents specified data streams from transmitting too many packets. Rate limiting is a traffic shaping technique that controls the transmission rate of sending systems. A broadcast storm is a type of network switching loop. NAT is a method by which private networks can share registered IP addresses. Neither of these last two is a traffic shaping technique.
whyWrong: A broadcast storm is the result of a switching loop, not a traffic shaping technique.
NAT lets private networks share registered IP addresses and is not a traffic shaping technique.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 5

stem: Which of the following terms refers to methods by which network traffic is prioritized to prevent applications from suffering faults due to network congestion?
explanation: Quality of service (QoS ) is a general term that refers to various mechanisms for prioritizing network traffic so that applications or data streams requiring a certain level of performance are not negatively affected by lower-priority transmissions. Port forwarding is a routing method that redirects traffic intended for one IP address and port number to another. Dynamic routing is a method by which routing tables are automatically updated with new information as the routing fabric of an internetwork changes. Virtual local area networks (VLANs) are a means for partitioning a broadcast domain into discrete units that are functionally equivalent to physical LANs.
whyWrong: Port forwarding redirects traffic for one IP address and port to another.
Dynamic routing updates routing tables automatically as the network changes.
VLANs divide a broadcast domain into separate logical LANs.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 6

stem: Which of the following mechanisms for prioritizing network traffic uses a 6-bit classification identifier in the Internet Protocol (IP) header?
explanation: Differentiated services (DiffServ) is a mechanism that provides quality of service (QoS) on a network by classifying traffic types using a 6-bit value in the Differentiated Services (DS) field of the IP header. Class of service (CoS) is a similar mechanism that operates at the Data link layer by adding a 3-bit Priority Code Point (PCP) value to the Ethernet frame. Traffic shaping is a means of prioritizing network traffic that typically works by delaying packets at the Application layer. Quality of service (QoS ) is an umbrella term that encompasses a variety of network traffic prioritization mechanisms. Administrative distance is a value that routers use to select the most efficient routing protocol.
whyWrong: CoS adds a 3-bit Priority Code Point value to the Ethernet frame at the Data link layer.
Traffic shaping prioritizes traffic by delaying packets and does not use the 6-bit IP header field.
QoS is the umbrella term for all traffic prioritization mechanisms.
Administrative distance is a value that routers use to choose between routing protocols.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 7

stem: Which of the following Network layer protocols include a Time to Live (TTL) field? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: The Internet Protocol (IP) in both of its versions (IPv4 and IPv6) includes a TTL field in its message header that limits the number of times a packet can be routed on a network. Each router processing the packet reduces the TTL value by one until it reaches zero, after which it is discarded. The Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) and the Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP) do not have a TTL field.
whyWrong: ICMP messages travel inside IP packets and have no TTL field of their own.
IGMP messages travel inside IP packets and have no TTL field of their own.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 22

stem: Which of the following is not a method of traffic shaping?
explanation: WAN optimization is not a form of traffic shaping, because it compresses data streams and transmits incremental file updates. Traffic shaping uses techniques like rate limiting, bandwidth throttling, and self-limiting to delay the transmission of specific types of data packets to optimize network performance.
whyWrong: Rate limiting is a traffic shaping technique that controls the sending rate.
Bandwidth throttling is a traffic shaping technique that limits specific data streams.
Self-limiting is a traffic shaping technique in which the sender limits its own rate.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 23

stem: Which of the following statements about proxy servers and NAT servers are true? (Choose all that apply.)
options: NAT servers and proxy servers can both provide Internet access to clients running any application.
NAT servers and proxy servers both use public IP addresses.
NAT servers and proxy servers both access Internet servers and relay the responses to network clients.
NAT servers and proxy servers both cache web data for later use.
explanation: To provide clients with Internet access, a NAT or proxy server must have direct access to the Internet, which requires using a registered, or public, IP address. Both NAT and proxy servers function as the middleman in transactions between the client computers on a private network and Internet servers. The NAT or proxy server transmits the client's service request to the Internet server as though it was its own and, after receiving the reply, relays the response back to the client. Because NAT servers function at the Network layer, clients can use any application to access the Internet through the server. Proxy servers, however, operate at the Application layer and can provide Internet access only to certain types of client applications. Proxy servers are capable of caching web data for later use, because they are Application layer devices that read the Application layer protocol data in the message packets they receive. NAT servers are Network layer processes that forward packets with no knowledge of the Application layer information in their contents.
whyWrong: Only NAT servers work with any application, because proxy servers support only certain applications.
Only proxy servers cache web data, because NAT servers do not read Application layer data.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 24

stem: Which two of the following functions is the multifunction device on a small office, home office (SOHO) network known as a broadband router LEAST likely to provide? (Choose two.)
explanation: Broadband routers generally do not function as proxy servers, which are Application layer devices used to regulate access to the Internet. They are also typically not virtual private network (VPN) headends, which enable multiple remote VPN clients to connect to the network. Many broadband routers are also WAPs, enabling users to construct a LAN without a complicated and expensive cable installation. Many broadband routers have switched ports for connections to wired devices, such as printers and computers. Most broadband routers use DHCP to assign IP addresses to devices on the private network.
whyWrong: Many broadband routers include a wireless access point.
Many broadband routers include switched ports for wired devices.
Most broadband routers act as a DHCP server for the private network.
source: CompTIA Network+ Practice Tests: Exam N10-009 (Zacker) – Chapter 2: Network Implementation, Review Questions question 25

stem: Small office, home office (SOHO) networks typically use a multifunction connectivity device that can perform all but which one of the following functions?
explanation: SOHO multifunction devices typically function as routers connecting the local network to an Internet service provider (ISP), switches providing wired connections to host devices, Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) servers assigning IP addresses, Domain Name System (DNS) servers resolving names into IP addresses, network address translation (NAT) routers providing hosts with private IP addresses access to the Internet, and APs providing wireless devices with access to the network. They do not function as hubs.
whyWrong: SOHO devices typically act as DHCP servers that assign IP addresses.
SOHO devices typically act as DNS servers or forwarders for the local network.
SOHO devices typically include switched ports for wired devices.
SOHO devices typically route between the local network and the ISP.
SOHO devices typically perform NAT so private hosts can reach the Internet.
